articleTitle: Development of Flexible Textile Patch Antenna Using Coating Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper explores the development of a flexible textile patch antenna, manufactured using a coating technique with the intended application for IEEE 802.11a wireless communications. The utilization of textile material offers adequate flexibility, enabling its usage as a body-worn antenna. The proposed patch antenna comprises three layers of cotton applied as a dielectric substrate. An inset-fed radiating patch is implemented using a coating technique, by brushing a square patch and feeding line pattern on the top side of upper layer cotton using conductive paint. To evaluate the flexibility of patch antenna, the characterization is performed under flat and bending conditions. The characterization results show that the proposed textile patch antenna works well at the frequency of 5.8 GHz in both conditions, demonstrating its flexibility without compromising its radiation characteristics. The measured bandwidths are 1.2 GHz and 3.8 GHz for flat and bending conditions, respectively, or the fractional bandwidths of 20.68% and 65.5%. In spite of these differences, the proposed textile patch antenna can produce adequate bandwidth response suitable for the desirable application.

articleTitle: ABS-based 3D Printed Bowtie Antenna Fed by Planar Marchand Balun for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: One of the manufacturing technologies which have been widely penetrating many fields is a 3D printing technique. With the growth of materials science, the technology has also been implemented to manufacturing radio frequency (RF) and wireless communication devices. This paper proposes design, realization, and characterization of a planar Marchand balun fed bowtie antenna manufactured by a 3D printing technology. An acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) material is used with the technology as a dielectric substrate, while a conductive coating paint is applied as conducting materials for antenna realization. The ABS-based dielectric substrate has the thickness of 0.8 mm with the relative permittivity of 2.6. The proposed bowtie antenna, fed by a planar Marchand balun, is designed to operates at the frequency of 2.4 GHz, which is globally available and unlicensed as a standard range for wireless communication. The characterization results demonstrate the effective functionality of proposed bowtie antenna at the frequency of 2.4 GHz with the impedance bandwidth of 800 MHz within the frequency of 2.03 GHz to 2.83 GHz. It can be inferred that the proposed bowtie antenna emerges as well-suited for diverse wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Non-Folded Capacitor-Based Flexible Phase-Difference Branch-Line Couplers for Butler Matrix Feeding Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper proposes a flexible phase difference (FPD) coupler without a folded line. The proposed FPD coupler is based on a branch-line structure with four capacitors mounted at each intersection point of the through and coupled arms. To demonstrate the effectiveness of coupler, a $2.4 \mathrm{G H z}$ 45° FPD coupler has been designed and measured. The measurement and simulation results agreed well. The bandwidth of $10-\mathrm{dB}$ reflection coefficient $\left(S_{11}\right)$ is $380 \mathrm{MHz}(15.83 \%$) from the frequency of 2.18 GHz to 2.56 GHz. The transmission coefficient $\left(S_{21}\right)$ is -3.48 dB on average with the imbalance of $\pm 0.42 \mathrm{~dB}$, while the phase difference is -44.84° on average with the imbalance of ±3.18°.

articleTitle: Non Invasive Glucose Detection Using Triple-Pole Triangular CSRR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, the authors propose a compact microwave sensor designed for monitoring the Blood Glucose Levels (BGL) of both hyperglycaemic (BGL 200 mg/dL) and hypoglycaemic (with BGL 50 mg/dL) patients. Our approach involves the development of a metamaterial microwave biosensor featuring a Triple Pole Triangular Complementary Split-ring Resonator (TP-TCSRR) operating across the blood glucose concentration range of 50-500 mg/dL. This unique structure is novel in this application. The theoretical analysis and numerical modelling of the TP-TCSRR sensor are conducted using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. When the sensor’s sensitivity is demonstrated through simulation in the range of 50-500 mg/dL, the results exhibited a distinct leftward frequency shift. To the best of our knowledge, distinct frequency shifts, particularly at lower glucose concentrations such as 50, 70, and 100, have not been reported till now. The sensor exhibited a maximum sensitivity up to 3.8 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> dB/(mg/dL) and 377 kHz/(mg/dL). Moreover, with the advantages such as affordability, compact size, operational versatility across various glucose concentrations, and enhanced sensitivity, particularly in low and high glucose concentrations (ranging from 50-100 mg/dL), this sensor concept a promising candidate for wearable non-invasive blood glucose monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Radar-based Investigation of Electromagnetic Waves Under Different Temperature and Humidity Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents investigations of the influence of temperature and humidity variations on electromagnetic signals within the frequency range of 68 GHz to 92 GHz. Assuming the environmental air acts as a frequency-dependent dielectric material, the propagation of electromagnetic waves depends on the thermal and molecular composition, and consequently, influences the measured phase. Two main scenarios are explored: varying temperature at constant relative humidity and varying relative humidity at constant temperature. Experimental data is collected using an W -band radar system within a controlled environment of a climate chamber. They validate theoretical models, providing insight about the relationship between temperature, humidity, and phase differentials. The conclusive measurements reveal that phase variations induced by fluctuations in air temperature and humidity are detectable.

articleTitle: ELF/VLF Micro-Array Transmitters with Fe-Co high-μ core for Space Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recent laboratory experiments [1–4] demonstrated that a small diameter, large aspect ratio multiloop solenoid antenna with a core of non-conducting high-μ material, could efficiently inject Whistler and EMIC waves in the ELF/VLF frequency range in space plasmas. The small radiation resistance due to the small diameter is compensated with the increase in the magnetic moment by the high-μ core. Initial experiments utilized high-μ ferrite core and are known as Ferrite Loop Antenna (FLA) elements. Subsequent experiments utilized commercial ferrofluids. In this case the high-μ core was due to an ensemble of 10-20 nm magnetite nanoparticles, dispersed in low-viscosity fluids known as Magnetic Nano-Transmitter (MNT) elements. The most important result of these experiments was that a phased two-element crossed dipole FLA or MNT array could generate high-amplitude Whistler and EMIC waves like the ones previously generated by Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF) antennas [5], but with radiation resistance more than 30dB larger. The observed waves had helical phase surfaces described by $\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\pm++\mathbf{k z}-\omega t)}$. The combination of a magnetic loop that propagates along $\mathbf{B}_{\mathbf{0}}$ while rotating about it, is known as helicon topology.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Feature Investigation of Scattering from Manmade Structures for Improving Change Detection of Flood-affected Urban Area
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Change detection using time-series polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) is an effective method for recognizing disaster-affected urban area [1]. However, the accuracy of the conventional method may not be enough if exterior of building is not damaged but road surrounding the building is covered by ruble and/or sediment of the flooded water after flood event, as in Figure 1 (a). For such case, primary scattering (double bounce scattering) from the building area is not changed but secondary/tertiary scattering (surface scattering/volume scattering) from other parts may be changed. It is not easy to detect the change of the secondary/tertiary scattering, since the power of such scattering is generally not large. So, we now take notice of the change detection concerning scattering with small power, in addition to primary scattering with large power.

articleTitle: 2-bit Reflective Electromagnetic Surface for X-band Beam Control Function
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a 2-bit reflective electromagnetic surface (RES) design for X-band beam control function based on tunable resonator approach. The beam control function is usually involved in X-band radio systems that require deflection of reflected waves in a certain direction. The proposed RES is configured by three layers with the dimensions of $\mathrm{1 6 0 ~ m m} \times \mathrm{8 0 ~ m m}$. The top layer is structured by $16 \times 16$ unit cells, which are a combination of 2 -bit or four state configurations of unit cell structure, namely state 00, state 01, state 10, and state 11. Basically, the unit cell structure in each state consists of four tunable open-ended resonators with varied length which can be connected or disconnected to produce the state configurations. The four state configurations produce four phase variations with the phase difference between states of 90°. This structure configuration is deployed on an FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate with the groundplane on the opposite side. Theoretically, the maximum reflected wave for the normal incident wave can be deflected by the proposed RES in the direction of approximately 21° from the normal reflection angle. This prediction is then confirmed through simulation and measurement. The proposed RES can be developed later by integrating PIN diodes to control the state of configuration, thereby improving its reconfigurability.

articleTitle: Method of Moments for the Two-Dimensional Analysis of Array-Fed Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a Method of Moment (MoM) formulation for the two-dimensional analysis of array-fed meta-surface (MTS) antennas. In the considered problem, the MTS is only modulated along one direction and translationally invariant along the other one. The MoM is first formulated for the case of a MTS of finite length fed with an array of active elements, with no particular constraint on the feed spacing, nor on the weight associated with each element. Then, the methodology is particularized to the case of a periodic MTS fed with an infinite array of active elements of same amplitude, with constant feed spacing and linear phase shift between elements. In both cases, the implementation is closely analysed and simulation results are shown to cross-validate both approaches. It can be concluded that the implemented methodologies can provide very fast and accurate results.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Polarization Performance for X-Band Metasurface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental investigation of polarization performance for metasurface absorber using horn antennas. The absorber which is designed to work at X -band frequency is configured by split ring resonator (SRR) with striplines. One of the horn antennas is connected to signal generator, while another one is to spectrum analyzer, whereby a device under test (DUT) is installed in front of both antennas. The absorber as a DUT has the dimensions of $278.4 \mathrm{~mm} \times 278.4$ mm, in which its polarization performance is characterized in three orientation angles, namely $0^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}$ and 90°. The angle of orientation is determined based on the alignments between the position of horn antennas which have linear polarization and the striplines of the absorber. The measurement results are analyzed using the ones taken by a copper conductor plat as comparison which has the same size and measurement distance. It shows that the orientation angle of ${ }^{0}$ between the antennas and the striplines has the maximum normalized absorption of -23.19 dB at the frequency of 8.88 GHz. The absorption decreases with the alteration of orientation angle to 45° and 90° for -18.07 dB and -12.15 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A breast microwave sensing system utilizing a fixed antenna array: system design and feasibility of material characterization using transmission measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A new system was built to serve as a tool in transitioning from a pre-clinical breast imaging rotating-radar bed system to a portable, low-cost medical device. This study presents the design of the new microwave sensing system and the feasibility of estimating an average relative permittivity using the transmission coefficient. The system was designed for multistatic operation in air, collecting S-parameter measurements using a 360° static array of 24 Vivaldi antennas. The system operates in the range of 700 MHz to 8 GHz. A two-antenna array setup was used to estimate the relative permittivity of wood by transmission coefficient measurements. The RMSE of the frequency-averaged relative permittivity was $0.1 \pm 0.2$ when using horn antennas, and $0.4 \pm 0.2$ when using Vivaldi antennas.

articleTitle: Lithography Process Verification on Porous PET Membranes for Cell Measurements Using THz-TDS Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Thin porous PET membranes are used for growing epithelial cells on top, employed within a cultivation environment for cells originating from the lung. Structuring those membranes with a resonator array by using a lithographic process enables a very sensitive electromagnetic measurement of changes within the epithelial cells, providing a biosensing platform for cell vitality measurements up to 3 THz. Due to the low thickness with $12 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and $23 \mu \mathrm{m}$ of the membranes and its microscopic pores, the process is prone to fabrication issues. In this work, the verification of this lithographic process is performed by a THz time-domain spectrometer with imaging capabilities. Additionally, the complex permittivity of the membrane material is characterized in the THz region.

articleTitle: Design of multifunctional metasurface based on Conformational Space Annealing (CSA) algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metasurfaces are two-dimensional structures featuring intricately arranged unit cells that manipulate the properties of electromagnetic waves or light, such as reflection, refraction, and transmission. These properties benefit applications like frequency filters, lenses, and beam steering, leading to extensive research in various fields.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic sources localization problem for indoor surveillance through opportunistic sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The future pervasive internet will be an extremely complex environment, where communication and sensing functions will be integrated exploiting a multitude of complementary enabling technologies operating for different purposes. These include target detection, classification, identification, false alarm mitigation, tracking, and precise localization. Unlike cameras, one notable advantage of these technologies is their effectiveness under varying lighting conditions and even in smoky environments, while maintaining privacy. Notably, current progress in electronics and digitalization allows for the creation of highly efficient sensors that are inexpensive, low-power and compact. A critical challenge lies in developing precise mathematical models to describe how electromagnetic waves propagate and scatter in complex environments and how sensors interact with each other as well as with their surroundings. These models lay the groundwork for advanced data processing methods that yield accurate and reliable results, reducing issues like missed detections, false alarms, noise and clutter/multipath effects. This is especially important in complex scenarios like indoor environments, where unconventional observation methods may be utilized.

articleTitle: BDS for Railway Train Localization Test and Evaluation Using 3D Environmental Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) has been applied in railway train control systems in several railway lines in China. The BDS has advantages as delivering the maneuver location without support from other train borne sensors, but the BDS performance can be degraded due to the environment blockage along the railway tracks. As to study the BDS performance during the journey of the train, a throughout procedure to test the BDS performance and comparing it with the reference system is necessary to test the signal propagation and reception. But the test procedure can be too costly in both time and equipment. So to study the performance in a more detailed way, we explore the BDS signal propagation in a simulated environment, identified the BDS signal as both Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) in the setup simulation environment in the lab using the 3D environmental information. The collected data from the train operation in the Sanjiadian railway station has been modelled into parametrical 3D environmental scenarios to create a “zero-on-site” testing environment for performance study. The test cases for train operation with BDS signal for train localization has been generated, the BDS performance has also been studied with several receivers to investigate the BDS performance in various signal reception degradation environments. The repeatability of the test procedure and accuracy are studied, and the optimization using the pre-information of LOS/NLOS are also applied both for parametric performance evaluation and also for performance optimizations.

articleTitle: Beyond the IC - Couplers, Channels and Components for High-Performance Polymer Microwave Fiber Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, Polymer Microwave Fiber (PMF) has attracted attention as a promising communication technology for short and medium distances, offering a wide and relatively flat bandwidth while exhibiting resilience to electromagnetic interference (EMI). These properties present an advantage over traditional wireline systems, while its potential for integration in commodity CMOS technology provides a cost benefit compared to optical communication [1].

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Koopman Autoencoders for Dimensionality Reduction and Forecasting of Nonlinear Kinetic Plasma-Wave Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Accurate simulations of nonlinear kinetic plasma-wave interactions are essential for the design and analysis of high-power microwave devices, fusion energy devices, terahertz and directed energy devices, as well as for studying a host of ionosphere and magnetosphere phenomena and their impact on space assets. However, large-scale kinetic plasma simulations that rely on popular electromagnetic particle-in-cell (EMPIC) algorithms face a significant computational burden due to the need to individually simulate thousands to millions of charged particles (ions, electrons). To address this, reduced order models such as proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) [1] and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) have proved especially useful [2].

articleTitle: Diffraction by Planar Junctions of Uniaxial Chiral Half-Planes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution assesses the plane wave diffraction caused by the edge discontinuity of a planar junction formed by two uniaxial chiral half-sheets. The incidence direction is supposed to be oblique with respect to the discontinuity. Each lossless half-sheet is anisotropic and characterized by permittivity, permeability and chirality parameters. This last parameter combines electric and magnetic fields to electric and magnetic flux densities in constitutive relations. Moreover, permittivity and permeability values along the optical axis, which is perpendicular to the sheet surfaces, are different from the values associated to the transverse axes.

articleTitle: Antenna gain pattern blindness due to mutual coupling in broadband arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The SKA-low observatory aims to use 512 stations of 256 antenna phased array to perform the next level of radio frequency astronomical observations. This most recent Aperture Array Verification System, AAVS3, operates a regular sunflower head ‘Vogel’ layout design [1]. Using method-of-moments simulations of these stations, including mutual coupling, we observe a blind spot at zenith of the embedded element pattern (EEP) at 125 MHz [2], corresponding to a drop in power of around 5 dB.

articleTitle: Free-standing compound anapoles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Transparency effects in photonics: cloaking, transformation optics, and anapole states have limitations following from Devaney-Wolf theorems. Accordingly, the weak and strong solutions obey the condition for the suppressed radiating harmonics in the far-field zone. In real systems, this condition is fulfilled only for certain harmonics that can be considered invisible. From the multipole decomposition approach, all transparency effects allow one to suppress certain main multipoles, while the higher-order non-resonant multipoles are always presented in the multipole spectra. Nevertheless, in this work, we propose free-standing compound anapole all-dielectric metasurface demonstrates the minimizing of radiating intensities of multipoles for a two centrosymmetric particle unit-cells. In accordance to multipole approach, the radiating multipoles of each particle compensate to each other in the compound system independent on angles and polarizations of the incident wave. We study proposed metamaterial theoretically and experimentaly in THz frequency range, as well as we study in microwave the scattering of electromagnetic wave by single compound structure. Therefore, we fabricate the sample by means of free-standing surface technique on the base of silicon wafer. These results have advanced applications in light-matter THz photonics.

articleTitle: Energetic Particle Dynamics and Magnetospheric Plasma Waves: Observations and Future Missions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Natural emissions in the form of plasma waves occur in the terrestrial magnetosphere and include both broad band emissions (e.g., plasmaspheric hiss) and discrete emissions (e.g., Electromagnetic Ion Cyclotron- EMICwaves, whistler mode chorus). These plasma waves not only energize but also precipitate charged particles present in the terrestrial radiation belts (for reviews see Kanekal and Miyoshi 2021; Millan and Thorne, 2007; Thorne 2010). It is well known that large solar wind structures such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions lead to enhanced wave activity and lead to enhanced relativistic electron populations as well as their precipitation into the atmosphere. Less known are the radiation belt electron interaction with mesoscale transient solar wind structures such as periodic density structures (PDS). Here we report upon a recent event study of relativistic electron response to PDS in the heart of the radiation belts. We provide an overview of energetic electron dynamics ranging from rapid energization resulting from interplanetary shocks (IP) to mesoscales PDSs. We show pitch angle distribution response of highly relativistic electrons to plasma waves as well as loss due to electron microburst precipitation. Electron precipitation is known to influnce atmospheric chemistry and therby global climate change. We also describe a mission concept to quanitfy systematically electron microburst loss into the atmosphere.

articleTitle: An Absorbable ECOG system Compatible to MRI.
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We introduce our innovative HF-2 technology that integrates intracranial recordings with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for preclinical research. This system enhances our capabilities to simultaneously record signals from electrocortical (ECoG) called Polymer Thick Film Organic Substrate (PTFOS) [1, 2] electrodes, alongside acquiring functional MRI (fMRI) data in animal subjects. Such concurrent ECoG and fMRI recordings offer an unmatched perspective on the comprehensive network activities across cortical areas in animal models, thereby deepening our understanding of neural organization. Simultaneous ECoG/depth/fMRI is particularly transformative, providing insights into functional connectivity and oscillatory properties at both high temporal and spatial resolutions [3]. This multimodal approach is crucial for advancing research in numerous areas of neuroscience and medicine, offering detailed insights into the brain’s functional architecture.

articleTitle: Frequency inversion method and device for malignant melanoma detection using RF/microwaves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The paper considers an inverse problem of reconstructing the spatially distributed complex dielectric permittivity function using backscattered data of the electric field in the frequency domain. We develop iterative algorithm for reconstruction of this function. Numerical example show the performance of the proposed algorithm in 2D. Additionally, we present at the first time the new prototype of device for the malignant melanoma detection which is modelled in HFSS/Ansys. Results of measurements of scattered parameters in HFSS/Ansys show significant phase distortion in the case when melanoma is present compared to the case when melanoma is absent.

articleTitle: Studying the Effects of Water Content in Breast Microwave Imaging with a Volunteer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Microwave Imaging (MWI) has been studied for early breast cancer detection in the last few decades. Volunteer and patient studies have recently been performed in academia and industrial environments [1]. Nevertheless, the axillary region, which may be affected by breast cancer, has not been assessed in such studies.

articleTitle: Method for Estimating Scatterer Information from the Response Waveform of a Backward Transient Scattered Field When a Line Source and an Observation Point are at Same Position
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is presented a method for estimating scatterer information from the response waveform of a backward transient field for E-polarization scattered by a two-dimensional (2-D) coated cylinder when an electric line source and an observation point are at the same position. The three types of scatterer information treated in this paper are the relative permittivity of a coating medium layer, its thickness, and the outer radius of a coated cylinder. Estimation formulas are derived using the time-domain Fourier transform method (TD-FTM) and the amplitude intensity ratios (AIRs) of adjacent backward transient scattered field components. The estimates are obtained by substituting the numerical data of the response waveform and the numerical parameters of a pulse source function into the estimation formulas and performing iterative calculations. The effectiveness of the estimation method is verified by comparing the estimates with the set values.

articleTitle: Resonance Scattering by Two Concentric Spherical Shells with Circular Apertures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rigorous solution of the plane wave diffraction problem for two open spherical concentric shells (see Fig.1) has been described in [1]. The problem has been solved by the Method of Analytical Regularization (MAR). Employment of the MAR led to the coupled infinite linear algebraic equations with matrix operators that are compact perturbations of the identity. This allowed us to construct a highly efficient (fast converging) numerical algorithm, using the truncation version of these equations, where the computational accuracy depends only on the truncation number N. The solution is uniformly valid for any desired aperture size described by the angular parameters $\theta_{b}=\pi-\theta_{0}$ and $\theta_{a}=\pi-\theta_{1}$.

articleTitle: Dielectric sensing of deeply subwavelength analytes using epsilon-near-zero waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The advent of metamaterials brought new wave-matter interaction paradigms to manipulate field and waves at will. Their applications are numerous: antennas, lenses, invisibility cloaking, computing, vortex beams and more. In turn, epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) metamaterials opened up new phenomena for light manipulation due to their exotic propagation constant, wavenumber and characteristic impedance. In 2008, it was demonstrated that a rectangular waveguide can emulate ENZ media by working near the cutoff frequency [1]. Moreover, the incredible field confinement inside the ENZ waveguide provided interesting features for sensing applications [2]. Our work further develops the idea of a dielectric body sensor based on a ENZ waveguide by considering an analyte partially filling the waveguide [3] and demonstrating empirically the setup [4].

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging of Partially Known Targets Through a Mild Data-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Microwave imaging is a powerful tool in many applications where non-destructive and non-invasive inspections are requiredsince the adopted frequency range allows the use of relatively cheap and safe apparatuses. However, the image reconstruction process, especially when a quantitative reconstruction of the dielectric properties of the target is required, involves the solution of an inverse problem, which is notably non-linear and ill-posed. In this framework, different techniques have been proposed in the last years, ranging from stochastic to deterministic solving schemes [1]. In several cases, the imaging problem is however related to the identification of defects and inclusions inside (partially) known host structures. In such conditions, the inclusion of some a-priori information into the inversion procedure may allow a significant enhancement in the retrieved solution.

articleTitle: Mm-wave wireless sensor networks with zero energy consumption through backscattering metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The future of 6 G communications emphasizes a deep understanding of human environments for improved quality of life and work efficiency. IoT sensors will play a crucial role, gathering extensive data about living environments for tasks like environmental monitoring and structural oversight [1]. The success of these systems hinges on cost-effectiveness, energy efficiency, and minimal maintenance requirements. Traditional IoT sensors, despite advancements, still face challenges such as power consumption and limited lifespans, particularly in indoor settings where energy harvesting is difficult. RFID sensors offer potential with their ability to transmit data without additional power, but their cost and reliability in harsh environments pose barriers to widespread adoption [2].

articleTitle: Interferometric Coherence of Bistatic Radar Observations and Spatial Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The coherence of Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) observations has many applications, including monitoring of surface topography changes, soil moisture, forest biomass and snow water equivalent. The InSAR phase measurement accuracy depends on the interferometric coherence of radar signals from two repeat passes. The interferometric coherence can be influenced by spatial resolution and geometry offset in observations in addition to temporal variabilities of land cover. The formulation of interferometric coherence for nominal backscattering geometry has been well established but has not yet been presented for bistatic forward radar scattering. In this article, we present the theoretical expression of interferometric coherence for bistatic geometry along the forward scattering direction. We model the natural variability by bivariate Gaussian distributions of the phase changes of repeat pass radar observations, which can be characterized by spatial correlation and standard deviations of terrain cover changes. We have completed a set of parametric analyses to assess the dependence on satellite baseline offset, spatial resolution, and cross-track distance. Specifically, we applied the theoretical expression to examine the impact of spatial variability of snow depths on the interferometric coherence for two SAR measurement geometries: monostatic backscattering SAR and bistatic forward looking Signals of Opportunity SAR and illustrated their differences.

articleTitle: High-Precision Calculation for the Cut-Off Wave Numbers for Waveguides of Arbitrary Cross Sections with Inner Conductors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A method for the accurate calculation of the cut-off wavenumbers of a waveguide with an arbitrary cross section and a number of inner conductors is demonstrated. A secure basis for formulating the spectral problem relies upon concepts of integral and infinite-matrix (summation) operator-valued functions depending nonlinearly on the frequency spectral parameter; whilst a variety of methods might be employed in determining the cut-off wavenumbers so specified, the Method of Analytical Regularization provides a route to the construction of an algorithm that is well-conditioned (and hence reliable). The algorithm is based on a mathematically rigorous solution of the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for the Helmholtz equation in the interior of the waveguide, excluding the regions occupied by the inner conductor boundaries; it results in a highly efficient method of calculating the cut-off wavenumbers and the corresponding non-trivial solutions representing the modal distribution. The ability to calculate the cut-off wavenumbers with any prescribed and proven accuracy provides a secure basis for treating the wavenumbers so found as “benchmark solutions”.

articleTitle: Time Domain Kirchhoff Integration in FDTD
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper reports on an efficient implementation of time domain Kirchhoff surface integration of vector fields for FDTD in rectangular coordinates, specifically using GPUs with the CUDA language. Applications include the connection of two or more FDTD space domains with arbitrary orientation and sampling. An example will be shown for a reflectarray [1] illuminated by an off axis eight-element patch antenna array.

articleTitle: DD-MLFMA-slotFFT Framework for the Electromagnetic Solution of Mounted Finite Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The interest in the electromagnetic behavior of periodic structures has significantly increased due to their crucial role in advancing cutting-edge applications in nanoscale and metasurface devices in scattering networks, plasmonic crystals, and nanophotonics. The rise of these technologies makes the improvement of the state-of-the-art methods in computational electromagnetics for the efficient solution of these kind of periodic structures even more crucial than ever. Traditional approaches predominantly centered on methods tailored for infinite periodic structures based on Floquet’s theorem and the Ewald transformation. However, although these methods have been demonstrated as powerful tools in the design process, they are not suitable for integration with other systems and sensors due to the limitation of infinite periodic structures or the accurate modeling of complex physical phenomena like edge effects and standing waves, vital phenomena for certain applications.

articleTitle: Design and Measurements of a Prototype Quadruple-Ridged Flared Horn for the ngVLA Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Next Generation Very Large Array (ngVLA), a project of the National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO), is a new radio astronomy interferometer consisting of approximately 244 shaped offset Gregorian dual reflector antennas each with an 18-meter aperture diameter and an additional 19 antennas in the core with 6-meter aperture diameter. The instrument will be built on the Plains of San Agustin in New Mexico, U.S.A. [1]. The details of the reflector antenna design are given in [2].

articleTitle: Plasma Wave Signatures Associated with Dusty Space Debris
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Space debris in Low Earth Orbit, roughly 200 km to 1000 km altitude, will continue to become an ever-increasing threat as more manmade objects inhabit space. Remediation techniques will rely on accurate detection using ground-based or space-based radio sounding and in situ measurements. Small objects of the order of cm are particularly difficult to detect but are still hazardous. Possibilities for detecting such small debris continue to be investigated and one possibility is the signature associated with a wide variety of plasma waves produced by the moving, supersonic, debris in the space plasma at this altitude. For example, past theoretical predictions include production of precursor ion acoustic solitons upstream from the debris and a typical wake field downstream. Magnetosonic waves in the magnetized LEO plasma produced by the debris have also been proposed. Some recent space-based measurements indicate electromagnetic Alfven waves and electrostatic lower hybrid waves may be observed in the vicinity of the debris. Another important phenomenon associated with the debris embedded in the LEO space plasma is charging due to fluxes of the charged particles onto the debris as well as photoemission in sunlight. It has been predicted that for debris larger than microns, there is no consequential impact on the actual orbit dynamics, however, there are possibilities for detection of the small, charged debris particles with various sensing techniques. The impact of the debris charging on the characteristics of the plasma waves must be considered. Fluctuations in the debris charge state could be important for the production and characterization of the waves produced by the debris. For example, in a dusty plasma of micron sized grains, it is known that fluctuations in the dust charge may excite or damp plasma waves. Also, as another example, plasma density and velocity inhomogeneities in the vicinity of the moving space debris have been proposed to produce plasma waves in the lower hybrid frequency band that have been observed by spacecraft. These inhomogeneities may be impacted by the debris charging as shown in the past in dust expansion across magnetized plasma. This work considers the impact of the debris charging on the production of plasma waves specifically in the lower hybrid frequency range. A hybrid Particle-In-Cell (PIC) and fluid plasma model is used to investigate production of lower hybrid waves due to motion of a debris cloud on the order of microns to centimeters through a magnetized plasma. The model uses the Orbit Limited Motion (OLM) model to describe time-varying charge on the debris cloud while the background fluid plasma density is self-consistently adjusted due to capture of plasma onto the debris cloud. The characterization of the plasma waves in the vicinity of the debris is considered for varying debris cloud and plasma parameters.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Broadband Cancellation of Scattering from Metasurfaces with OAM and Combined Phase Profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The mechanisms of wide-angle broadband phase scattering cancellation from Patcharatnam-Berry (PB) metasurfaces (MSs) with orbital angular momentum (OAM) and combined phase profiles are examined. MS modules (structural elements) consisting of 144 meta-particles in the form of rectangular patches with rectangular cutouts are designed. The scattering characteristics of MS modules of the same size, differing in different PB-phase profiles, are compared: a module with OAM generation, modules with two different parabolic profiles (concave and convex), and modules with a combination of an OAM profile and a parabolic profile. The simulation showed that all profiles provide 8–10 dB cancellation of backscattered co- and cross-fields in the 8.5–21 GHz band. Parabolic profiles produce vortex scattering with greater diffusion. Combining these profiles with the OAM profile demonstrates the greatest diffusion, with the generation of two coaxial central vortices with different opening angles and OAM modes. Wide-angle diffuse co-field cancellation is maintained over an ultra-wide frequency band.

articleTitle: Full-metal metasurface for surface wave tailoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a low-profile inductive surface using metallic mushroom structures at L-band frequencies. The goal is to achieve an efficient surface wave excitation from the metasurface when it is placed in the near environment of a radiating monopole antenna. Simulation results show that the proposed full-metal metasurface exhibits an increase of 9 dB in the vertical electrical field at its output end and above the ground. Thanks to the absence of lossy dielectric material, this study is a first step towards the implementation of easy-to-fabricate metasurfaces in High Frequency Surface Wave Radars (HFSWR).

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Internal Parameters of SiC MOSFET on EMI of Traction Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) is the third-generation power semiconductor, which is crucial to improve the efficiency of traction system. Its fast-switching speed and high voltage level make it an ideal power device. However, the high switching frequency of SiC MOSFET may lead to overvoltage and high frequency oscillation at the traction motor end, causing electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems. Current research often ignores the switching characteristics of SiC devices, and it is difficult to accurately evaluate the EMI interference level in the system. Therefore, in the traction system using SiC MOSFET, it is necessary to study the modeling of SiC MOSFET devices in depth to understand the influence of changes in parasitic parameters inside the device on the switching characteristics, and further analyze the electromagnetic interference problems that this change may cause to the system. By studying the influence of the internal parasitic parameters of SiC MOSFET devices on the switching characteristics in detail, the system design can be better optimized, the risk of electromagnetic interference can be reduced, and the stability and reliability of the system can be improved. This research will provide important guidance for the future application of SiC power devices in traction systems and promote the further improvement of system performance.

articleTitle: Study Regarding the Tunability of a Frequency Selective Surface Having Incorporated Active Devices and Control Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The demand for tunable devices in modern communication networks is rising. This article proposes a design for a tunable frequency selective surface which has two states (simulating ON and OFF states of PIN diodes). In order to bias the active parts, PIN diodes are employed as active devices for tuning and control networks incorporated in the structures. The suggested designs have been evaluated using electromagnetic simulation. Parametric studies are done to enhance the tunability of the proposed structures.

articleTitle: Multi-band Radio Astronomy Receivers: A Concept Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Concurrent multi-band observations are a cornerstone of future radio astronomy and very-long baseline interferometry (VLBI). While some telescopes can incorporate multiple independent receivers with a shared optical path (SOP) for concurrent observation, others require single feeds and separate RF front-ends to cover multiple bands. We examine the state-of-the-art in feeds, couplers, isolators, low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) and downconverters, to determine the relative value of wideband RF front-ends vs. receivers with multiple, discrete operating bands. It is found that the implementation of wideband feeds and isolators do not offer significant drawbacks to their multi-band equivalents, but that concurrent multi-band LNAs and noise couplers may offer some advantages over wideband LNAs. While broadband mixers are readily available, different downconversion and intermediate frequency (IF) processing approaches are highlighted, which may be customized to the specific bands of interest.

articleTitle: Evaluation of equivalent sheet impedance from isofrequency curves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metasurfaces are structures made of one or several layers of subwavelength metallic patches printed on a grounded dielectric substrate. To ease the design and modeling of metasurfaces, the array of patches is genearlly homogenized under the local periodicity assumption and described using an equivalent sheet impedance or isofrequency curve. Recently, a fast fullwave method based on the Method of Moments (MoM) has been proposed to rapidly and accurately compute the isofrequency curves of metasurface-like periodic array of patches. In this work, we extract an equivalent sheet impedance from the isofrequency curve of a given array of patches by imposing the transverse resonance condition. If the metasurface involves several metallizations, the equivalent surface impedances of each sheet is computed independently and the different sheets are combined afterward. The proposed method is validated through numerical examples. Interestingly, the equivalent sheet impedance extracted from the isofrequency curve of the fundamental TM mode can also accurately reproduce the isofrequency curve of the fundamental TE mode.

articleTitle: A frequency tunable rectangular patch antenna based on anisotropic artificial material at C-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper describes a novel frequency tunable rectangular patch antenna based on a technique involving an anisotropic artificial dielectric layer. This technique enables the synthesis of effective permittivity in relation to the geometry dimensions of the antenna (1). The dimensions of this patch antenna have been done considering the traditional guideline that states the length must be have half effective wavelength and the width according to the impedance of the antenna (2).

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission Using an Intelligent Metamaterial Array Non-Homogeneous
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The objective of this work is to propose a simple system of wireless power transmission, that uses a metamaterial matrix capable of directing the flow lines, by manipulating the magnetic permeability of the unit cells the matrix, to specific region of interest and allow the efficiency of the system to be maintained uniformly over four possible placements of the transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) coils. Another differential of this system refers to the location of the positioning of the metamaterial matrix, which is located in the vicinity of the transmitter unit, rather than at the central distance of “Tx” and “Rx observed” in most studies, thus allowing the magnetic field to be guided intelligently from the start of the transmission stage.

articleTitle: PTFE-Ni Metamaterial Absorber for Optical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Research about electromagnetic absorbers has accelerated, spurred by the potential applications of metamaterials within the optical region of the frequency spectrum. Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), with its low refractive index, and resistance to oxidation, stands out among most absorption media. Its advantages include oxidation resistance, prolonged device lifespan, stability in the long term, and effectiveness within the visible electromagnetic spectrum [1]. Recent studies explore the use of PTFE in constructing metamaterial absorbers (MAs) via 3D printing technology. This approach capitalizes on 3D printing’s evolution and versatility, enabling the production of MAs with enhanced flexibility, speed of production, and cost-effectiveness [2].

articleTitle: Calculation of EMP Conducted Environment Based on Hierarchical Uncertainty Quantification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Early-time high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP), as a typical kind of electromagnetic pulse (EMP), will generate high voltages and large currents on transmission lines and cause serious effects to the terminal equipment. The conducted environment represented by the statistical results of induced currents or voltages is widely used to describe the consequence of the radiated environment.

articleTitle: On the Feasibility of a Generic Phased Array Feed for the European VLBI Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The feasibility of using a generic Phased Array Feed (PAF) for the radio telescopes within the European VLBI Network (EVN) is explored. Taking into consideration the variations in size ($\mathrm{1 4} \mathrm{~ m}-100 \mathrm{~m}$) and primary focal distance to diameter ratios $f / D(0.3-0.5)$ of the EVN reflectors, the achievable aperture efficiency of a generic array feed is investigated. For the scan range of $0^{\circ}-5^{\circ}$, a parametric study based on encircled power is performed to find the optimum location, shape and size of the array. It is concluded that for a generic PAF design, the smallest $f / D$ ratio decides the required array size for a certain aperture efficiency and scan angle. A spherical array with specific radius of curvature and displacement from the focus is found to achieve $80 \%$ aperture efficiency with smaller size, both in terms of radius projected onto the focal plane and surface area, than a planar array placed in the focal plane.

articleTitle: Circuit modeling of Metasurfaces with Printed Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metasurfaces are the 2D version of metamaterials technology and are designed as planar periodic structures with unit cell size of less than $0.1 \lambda$. The metamaterials can be characterized by the homogenization method as surfaces with effective tensor electric ($3 \times 3$ matrix) and magnetic ($3 \times 3$ matrix) susceptibilities. In case of metasurfaces with printed elements and arbitrary geometry (our case study) the metasurface can be represented by a tensor shunt admittance ($2 \times 2$ matrix) at the interface between two transmission lines representing the two media on the two sides of the metasurface. The tensor shunt admittance can be extracted based on the boundary conditions at the location of the metasurface elements. As such the tensor shunt admittance depends on the metasurface geometry and the media on the two sides of the metasurface. In the literature, we can find two fundamental methods to extract the tensor shunt admittance. In the first method, the extraction is based on the analysis of the unit cell scattering parameters, while in the second method the extraction is based on the analysis of the sampled near field on top of the unit cell metasurface element. The scattering parameters analysis is performed for the dominant Floquet mode in the metasurface unit cell using two orthogonal polarization measurements or simulations. The circuit modeling holds for a relatively narrow incident angular sector around the normal to the metasurface plane. For larger incident angles on the metasurface the shunt admittance model fails due to diffraction and spatial dispersion effects from the metasurface elements. To improve the model performance beyond 50° incident angle there are two options. The $1^{\text {st }}$ option is to recalibrate the model based on measurements or simulations taken at 50° and compute a new tensor shunt admittance based on the data measured at 50°. The $2^{\text {nd }}$ option is to modify the model of the shunt admittance and a more complex circuit modeling is required to represent the metasurface positioned at the interface between two different media. The circuit modeling of the metasurface accelerates the design cycle of a multilayer metasurface structure like radomes and flat lenses instead of the analysis based on a volumetric problem with an effective refractive index.

articleTitle: Biomedical Imaging and Impressioning using Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The advent of X-Ray Computerized Tomography using Radon transforms for imaging of human bodies in the 1970s gave rise to a strong interest in imaging using microwaves. The primary thrust behind such interest lied in the non-harmful effects of low-power microwaves in comparison to potentially ionizing X-rays. The field of imaging using microwaves has traditionally evolved based on inverse scattering theories that were steeped in integral equations’ formulations of the electromagnetic radiation or acoustic problems. Inverse scattering problems were fundamentally based on reconstructing the dielectric permittivity or magnetic permittivity profile of a specific medium or object. In biomedical imaging, however, reconstructing the precise concise profile of the object (such as the human body), is not of importance but rather generating an image or an impression that indicates the presence of an anomaly such as a fracture in a bone, a blood clot, or a tumorous growth within the body. In these modalities, the primary goal is to create a contrast between the constituents of the human body. Therefore, mathematically complex ill-posed inverse scattering methods may not be most suitable or even practical for imaging or impressioning human bodies.

articleTitle: Toward Vector Generalized Source Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The two-dimensional (2-D) transverse electric (TE) case is used for the development and demonstration of a vector generalized source integral equation (GSIE) formulation for the surface scattering problem, suitable for essentially-convex scatterers. The formulation uses magnetic current wires as sources for auxiliary dyadic components to the free-space Green’s function of point filamentary sources. The auxiliary component is designed to cancel the magnetic field tangential to a (perfect magnetic conductor) convex surface, acting as a shield. The resulting modified Green’s function exhibits a deeps shadow behind the shield, reduces the effective dimensionality of the interactions between large subdomains of the scatterer, and enhances the rank-deficiency of associated moment matrix blocks. The formulation complements the previously presented transverse magnetic (TM) effectively scalar 2-D formulations. As such, its derivation is a stepping stone toward that of three-dimensional GSIEs and vector auxiliary sources.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Shadowing and Range Effects caused by the Scattering of Wind-Turbines in some distance to Radar Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Wind-Turbines WTs are located single or dislocated within wind-farms WF often close to radar systems, such as Air-Traffic-Control-Radar ATC or Air Defense Radar ADR or Meteo-Radar MR. A distinct effect of the WT is the shadowing and the potential associated range reduction by the scattering of the WT in the back of the WT.

articleTitle: Field Averaging Techniques in Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work we present two field averaging techniques for structured electromagnetic materials. One is concerned with 3D-periodic composite media, while the other one is concerned with 2D-periodic planar structures. In the first case, the field averaging is prescribed by the integral form of Maxwell’s equations and is carried out along the paths laying at the boundaries of the unit cell. In the second case, the integration regions are prescribed by the Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions. Both techniques are useful in homogenization of structured materials such as metamaterials and metasurfaces, for the extraction of their effective material parameters and surface susceptibilities, respectively.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Array-based Belts for Respiratory Activity Monitoring: Respiratory Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This study focuses on the application of Fiber Bragg Grating Arrays (FBGA) for monitoring respiratory activity. Respiratory belts were placed on the chest, and upper and lower abdomen, and data was acquired in standing, sitting, and supine position for varied breathing patterns i.e. Normal, Accelerated, and Apnea. In the study, wavelets were utilized as compared to conventional filter-based techniques and Daubechies has been observed to be more reliable as a minimal amount of RMSE and PRD were reported. Coherence index values above threshold values ($\gt 0.5$) were reported majorly for all postures indicating the similarity of frequency components contained within array data. Limitations of conventional techniques for monitoring respiratory activity and variations observed in breathing patterns are also discussed in the conducted study.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Scattering Estimation of Urban Buildings by Using PolSAR data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radar polarimetry is a powerful tool to discriminate scattering phenomena of the targets. This technique has been applied to earth observation by satellite-bome synthetic aperture radar (SAR), called Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR). Polarimetry can be used to observe land cover classification based on differences in polarimetric scattering nature of targets on the earth surface. In addition, changes in the surface conditions can be detected in time-series dataset. This is expected to be a disaster monitoring technique.

articleTitle: Polarization Inversion in P. T. D - Symmetric Single Layered Polarizers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Definitions of incident and reflected modes in the $\mathcal{P} \cdot \mathcal{T} \cdot \mathcal{D}$ formulation result in co-polarized non-reflection for 45° and 135° polarizations with respect to the mirror plane. For other incident polarizations, the non-reflection angle is rotated and reflections are inverted. A number of applications is envisioned, including a reflective polarizer described below.

articleTitle: A Reconstruction Method for the Surface Potential of the High Voltage Charged Body Based on Quasi-Static Electric Field Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, the large-scale AC and DC extra-high voltage transmission projects have been put into practical operation. Moreover, along with the breakthroughs and innovations in communication and artificial intelligence technologies, power systems are being promoted in the more innovative and intelligent development direction, which puts forward higher requirements for the monitoring and evaluation of the important status of various types of key high-voltage power equipment in the power systems.

articleTitle: Plasma signatures of small orbital debris in LEO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Since the beginning of the space age, the number of orbital debris has skyrocketed to levels which seriously threaten the current and future use of space. It is estimated that -36,500 objects greater than 10 cm and orders of magnitude more smaller objects are currently in orbit, created predominantly by collisional events. The smaller objects, with characteristic size less than ~1 cm, are extremely hard to detect and cannot be tracked with existing technology but, with typical velocities of ~10 km/s, can create significant damage upon impact. Furthermore, with the ongoing commercialization of space and constellations of thousands of satellites envisioned in the near future, the orbital debris problem is expected to become much worse and methods for detection, tracking, characterization and possibly removal are much needed.

articleTitle: Self-consistent wakefield and space-charge simulations for electron injectors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In electron accelerators, the dynamics of the particle beam is affected by internal space-charge forces as well as by wakefields. The latter represent electromagnetic fields scattered by the walls of the surrounding accelerator cavities. In a typical beam dynamics simulation, particle trajectories are tracked assuming free-space propagation, whereas the wakefield contribution is either neglected or is considered separately in a post-processing step. We propose a self-consistent simulation model which allows to quantify the coupled effect of space-charge fields and the beam-cavity interaction induced by electromagnetic wakefields. The model is applied in beam dynamics simulations for the electron injector of the SwissFEL, for which a clear impact of wakefields on the beam properties is demonstrated.

articleTitle: TE-waves in waveguide structures filled with graded dielectric media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Graded dielectric media composites, with negative-index materials (NIM), are of interest for various applications such as microwave graded-index (GRIN) lenses [1, 2], wideband THz filtering [3], and enhanced energy harvesting [4]. Graded dielectric media with regular positive-index materials are also of importance in e.g. the field of biosensing. One example is mimicking of dielectric phantoms for the characterization of biological tissue’s properties and response to electromagnetic radiation [5, 6].

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of cactus pear and Dactylopius opuntiae measurement for electromagnetic applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Understanding the complex permittivity of agricultural pests and their host plants is crucial for developing innovative pest control strategies. This study investigates the dielectric properties of the cactus pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) and its pest, Dactylopius opuntiae, using a coaxial probe method across frequencies from 0.5 to 20 GHz. Our research aims to assess dielectric heating’s viability for eradicating D. opuntiae in cactus pear crops. We have demonstrated that D. opuntiae possesses significantly higher dielectric constants and loss factors within the Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) band than its host, highlighting its greater vulnerability to microwave-induced damage. Notably, the distinction in dielectric properties between living and deceased D. opuntiae females suggests the potential of microwave imaging to determine pest vitality. These insights underscore dielectric heating’s potential as a targeted, efficient pest control technique, offering a novel solution to safeguard cactus pear agriculture.

articleTitle: Gradient-Informed Weighted Sum Multi-Objective Topology Optimization in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Among all optimization approaches for the design of electromagnetic devices, topology optimization (TO) has recently gained great interest due to the broad spectrum of additive manufacturing (AM) techniques, allowing the realization of components with complex geometries. TO aims at finding the best material distribution within a design domain $\Omega_{d}$ under objective and constraint functions, where the former is retrieved from the solution of a partial differential equation (PDE) governing the physical problem. TO generally lies in the class of large-scale optimization problems and the decision variables $x_{i}$ of TO maps the presence or absence of material in each finite element discretizing $\Omega_{d}$. These variables generally belong to a continuous decision space $x_{i} \in[0,1]$, however, it can be conveniently defined also in a binary space, i.e., $x_{i} \in\{0,1\}$. As shown in Figure 1, in such a case, the material can only be absent $\left(x_{i}=0\right)$ or present $\left(x_{i}=1\right)$ without the appearance of intermediate values.

articleTitle: 2-D Photonic Crystal Leaky-Wave Antennas: Theoretical Investigation and Design Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The electromagnetic radiation from an electric line source embedded within dielectric photonic crystals is thoroughly investigated in this contribution. The structures analyzed consist of periodic chains of circular voids in dielectric media. We demonstrate the potential utility of these holey lattice structures in the design of leaky-wave antennas that show high directivity. The radiation mechanism of two-dimensional (2-D) dielectric lattices has been investigated in terms of leaky modes [1], presenting a method based both on the analysis of the band diagrams of the Bloch waves propagating in the 2-D photonic crystals (PCs) and the leaky-wave investigation of open waveguides. This study provided an insightful perspective on antenna design. In [2] the leaky-wave radiation from bisected Dielectric Rod Photonic Crystals (DRPCs) and Holey Photonic Crystals (HPCs) was investigated. Bisected DRPCs consist of two-dimensional periodic chains of circular dielectric rods in free space and over a metal plate, while HPCs involve air columns drilled in a dielectric host medium. It was found that HPCs are the optimal choice for achieving high directive radiation, outperforming dual structures based on DRPCs by 6 dB in terms of directivity. In this contribution, further details on the working principle and guidelines for the design of highly directive HPC leaky-wave antennas (HPCLWAs) bisected by a metal plate are provided. In particular, it is shown how high directivity is maintained even when the relative permittivity of the hosting dielectric medium is decreased and the total band gap of the 2-D PC vanished. Indeed, even in the absence of a complete stopband in the 2-D PC band diagram, it is still possible to design a directive HPCLWA, by carefully investigating the leaky and bound modes of the relevant open waveguide. This original finding holds significance in manufacturing, as it enables the utilization of cost-effective methods like three-dimensional (3-D) printing. An example of HPCLWAs, designed to operate at f = 24 GHz and excited by a simple probe source, is shown in Fig. 1. More details will be shown at the conference.

articleTitle: Dynamic Model for Predicting Instability of Multiphase Processes: Direct and Inverse Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A method is set forth for modeling multiphase processes aimed at characterizing and predicting their instabilities. The technique employs autonomous polynomial dynamical systems (DSs) derived using approximation of the measurement data in terms of specifically formulated inverse problems. Complete description of singularities is performed using the developed discriminant criterion. Examples of realization are discussed.

articleTitle: Phaseless Radar Coincidence Imaging via Low-Rank Matrix Recovery Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Phaseless synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a novel, waveform-diverse imaging approach which may have profound implications in system design, cost, and robustness for remote sensing applications. Phaseless image reconstruction contributes towards the development of distributed, multi-static SAR systems that can be deployed on a large number of small, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with benefits in robustness, cost, increased spatial diversity, accuracy, resolution and ability to operate in contested environments.

articleTitle: Multi-solver Electromagnetic Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Computational electromagnetics (CEM) has become an indispensable tool for engineers in a wide range of applications in the aerospace and naval industries. The complexity of these industries, with challenges such as advanced antenna design, Electromagnetic Environmental Effects (E3), and radar cross section (RCS) control, demands the use of powerful simulation tools. However, new times bring new advances to the industry and, with them, new challenges to the computational electromagnetic field. Seeking cutting-edge advances in very low observability (VLO) techniques and E3 in modern platforms further underscores the need for these tools, capable of dealing with multiple scales and all kinds of novel modern materials (metamaterials).

articleTitle: Electromagnetically Unclonable Function with Immunity to Machine Learning Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Over the past decade, non-Hermitian physical systems and their abnormal singularities, known as exceptional points (EPs), have deepen our understanding of how to engineer spectral and spatial properties of waves, leading to remarkable advances in signal synthesis, routing, and modulation across the spectrum. In particular, spectral sensitivity near the EP-singularity in non-Hermitian physical systems has recently been extensively explored for making the next-generation photonic, acoustic, and electronic sensors with unprecedented sensitivity and resolvability [1]–[5]. However, it is still debated whether this new class of sensors can surpass traditional sensors in terms of reliability and signal-to-noise ratio, since mesoscopic fluctuations and noises could also be amplified at these singular points [6–8].

articleTitle: Anisotropic 3D Printed Unit Cells for More Realistic EEG Physical Head Phantoms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution deals with a comparison of several anisotropic unit cell models for mimicking properties of head tissues to create more realistic fabricable anisotropic head phantoms for electroencephalogram (EEG) systems. The selected unit cells can be exploited for creation of a white matter or skull anisotropy, while being suitable for practical realization of head phantoms by 3D printing techniques. Their effective conductivities are calculated by numerical simulations in CST Studio Suite and their maximum anisotropic ratios are evaluated for various conductivity ratios of the host and inclusion materials. Further, the numerically calculated effective conductivity of a simple sandwich unit cell is validated by the analytical equivalent electrical circuit networks method.

articleTitle: Preliminary Research on Nonlinear Correlation Coefficient Criterion in EMTR Method for Spatial Radiation Source Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: To enhance the precision and resolution of radiation source localization using electromagnetic time reversal technology in free-space environments, this paper introduces a novel nonlinear correlation coefficient criterion that employs the Gaussian kernel function. A series of simulations were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of this new criterion against the conventional energy criterion and the linear correlation coefficient criterion. The simulation results reveal that the Gaussian kernel-based nonlinear correlation coefficient significantly reduces the size of the focusing spot within the localization region, thereby boosting spatial resolution. Moreover, the application of the nonlinear correlation process effectively eliminates the pseudo-focusing spot adjacent to the radiation source, leading to a prominent improvement in spatial localization resolution.

articleTitle: The Research on a FSS with High Roll-Off Characteristics Based on SIW
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this letter, a frequency selective surface (FSS) unit with high roll-off characteristics was designed by cascading and branching two substrate-integrated waveguide cavities (SIWCs) of different sizes. The metal surfaces at the top and bottom of the unit feature periodic slits. The coupling between the aperture resonance and the resonances within the two cavities can generate two transmission zeros, forming a sharp lower sideband and a sharp upper sideband. The structure is depicted in Figure 1 (a-e), where the cross slots on the top and bottom surfaces are of the same dimensions, and the coupling slots in the middle layer are cross slots of different sizes, with all elements in each layer having the same periodicity [1]. The typical response of an SIWC-FSS with a single cross slot, similar to the response of an SIWC-FSS with lattice or square ring slots [2]. It can excite both aperture and cavity resonances simultaneously. By adjusting the coupling between these two different resonances, the transmission zeros can be easily controlled at the lower or upper sidebands. The slot lengths of the single SIWC-FSS with either lower or upper sharp sidebands are the same, but the cavity sizes differ. Therefore, by combining two such SIW cavities in a periodic unit, a highly selective FSS with two sharp sidebands can be achieved.

articleTitle: Resonator-Like Antenna for Parametric Excitation of Ultra-Short Spin Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In novel, beyond Von Neumann, computational approaches the use of magnons (or quanta of spin waves) is particularly promising due to the small intrinsic energies of individual magnons $(\mu \mathrm{V})$, the possibility of using phase, in addition to magnitude, as a state variable, and the possibility to control the magnon dispersion properties in a magnetic sample by varying the direction and magnitude of the bias magnetic field [1].

articleTitle: A Hybrid Cavity-Planar P-band Illuminator for Primary Focus Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A compact dual-polarized feed operating between 300 and 420 MHz has been designed to illuminate the $32-\mathrm{m}$ parabolic reflector of the Noto radio telescope. The feed combines the compactness of a planar design to the higher illumination performance of a guided solution. Four half-wavelength dipoles distributed in the sides of a square are integrated in a metallic cavity improving the reflector’s illumination. Each pair of parallel dipoles is excited, through a common coaxial port connected to two parallel strip lines, without making use of external $0^{\circ} / 180^{\circ}$ power dividers and/or baluns. Numerical results for the radiation pattern and the matching properties are shown for the single illuminator and after the reflection with the primary dish of the Noto radio telescope.
