articleTitle: Exploring Neutral Particle Dynamics with Fs-TALIF in Fusion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Line radiation from neutral atoms and molecules is instrumental in plasma physics diagnostics. However, the rate at which they emit radiation is influenced by several factors such as plasma density, temperature, and gas density, which in our study, is hydrogen. This complexity has led to the widespread use of kinetic neutral simulations to reduce uncertainties, allowing for radiation diagnostics like fs-TALIF [1] to provide a clearer picture of plasma characteristics. The accuracy of these simulations is crucial for leveraging diagnostic tools and ensuring confidence in developing future fusion systems.

articleTitle: Measurement Setup of a Ka-band Switchable Circularly Polarized Phased-Array Module for LEO Satellite Communications Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Phased Arrays are a growing trend in antenna technologies due to their versatility, their easy integration with communication systems and their low-profile. The implementation of these devices in satellite communication systems is commonly found in literature [1] where they become particularly interesting due to their long-term reliability, fast steering, and the capacity of creating multiple beams.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis and Optimization Design of Electronic Ignition System for Fuel Powered Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: With the application and development of vehicle electronic control systems, the electromagnetic environment inside the vehicle is becoming increasingly complex, which affects the normal operation of the electronic control ignition system of fuel vehicles, and even causes stalling problems. This article focuses on the electromagnetic compatibility faults in the electronic control ignition system of fuel vehicles, analyzes the mechanism of disturbance sources and their sensitivity disturbance mechanism in the electronic control ignition system, and analyzes the fault problems generated by the ignition system by building a real vehicle testing platform. It proposes an optimization method to increase bypass capacitance, and finally proves the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed optimization method through simulation and experimental testing. The electromagnetic compatibility optimization design scheme proposed in this article solves the problem of stalling failure in the actual vehicle electronic control ignition system, saves economic costs, and has great engineering value. It also has certain reference value for solving electromagnetic compatibility engineering problems in other electrical systems of vehicles.

articleTitle: Deep and Reinforcement Learning Approach to Enhanced Microwave Imaging for Tumor Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, a framework integrating Deep and Reinforcement Learning with microwave imaging techniques is presented to improve tumor identification. The proposed approach implements microwave imaging reconstruction by using the Quadratic Born Iterative Method (BIM) and Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNNs). Through the adoption of Deep QNetworks (DQNs) and Reinforcement Learning, an agent is implemented to learn and perfomr accurate tumor identification within breast images. This is confirmed by the achieved Intersection over Union (IoU) values greater than 0.9 in the discussed validation tests, thus revealing successfull applications in the framework of medical imaging.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of Electro-Mechanical and Solid-State Switching Matrices for a Portable Microwave (pMWI) Scanner in Brain Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work systematically evaluates two different switching matrices, dubbed herein as EMech and Correlator. One is based on ad-hoc electromechanical switches, the other on off-the-shelf solid-state ones [1]. These matrices interface a 2-port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) and a 22-antenna array of a low-complexity portable microwave imaging (pMWI) system for brain monitoring [2], falling into to the category of multistatic system with switching network [3]. Hence, a whole $22 \times 22$ scattering matrix is sequentially filled by $2 \times 2$ segments.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized A-T-A Frequency Selective Rasorber Based on Cross-Dipole and Interdigital Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized frequency selective rasorber (FSR) that features two absorption bands on both sides of a passband. The structure of the proposed FSR consists of a resistive absorber frequency-selective surface (FSS), a passband FSS, and an air gap between the layers. Interdigital resonators are implemented to guarantee parallel resonance in the resistive layer, whose unit cell element is a resistor-loaded cross-dipole. The FSR exhibits a passband of high selectivity around 4.78 GHz with a minimum insertion loss of 0.77 dB and provides an operating bandwidth from 2.32 to $8.33 \mathrm{GHz}\left(\left|S_{11}\right|\lt -10 \mathrm{~dB}\right)$, under normal incidence. The proposed rasorber is capable of reducing the radar cross section of communication systems operating in the C-band, by reducing out-of-passband reflections in other directions, giving them stealth characteristics. The FSR prototype was fabricated with a low-cost FR-4 substrate in both layers, and measured for validation.

articleTitle: Extended Multi-branch basis functions for non-conformal problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) approaches [1] used to connect two non-conformal surfaces in the Method of Moments typical employ Interior Penalty (IP) methods to mitigate charge accumulation along the half RWG basis functions connection boundary. These IP approaches are introduced via a combined impedance matrix $(Z-\beta$. $I P$). Alternatively in soft non-conforming problems, Multi-branch (MB-RWG) basis functions can be utilized [2]. Generalizations of multibranch basis functions can lead to higher degress of nonconformality as the use of $N^{+}-N^{-}$ branches MB_RWG [3] when $N^{+}$ and $N^{-}$ triangles have common vertices at the endpoints of the shared countour, but not along the contour.

articleTitle: Comparison of 3D-printed Feed Chain Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: From the initial works of 2010s, Additive Manufacturing (AM) processes have gained increasing attention in the microwave area so as to become a new multidisciplinary research topic that merges mechanical, material and electromagnetic skills. The result of these activities has led AM to be considered nowadays as a valid option for manufacturing and fast prototyping [1]. In the microwave area, there is no domain where its applicability has not been tested successfully, although some aspects on surface finishing, accuracy, repeatability and thermal and mechanical stability are still under consideration for improvement. Among the AM processes, all metal ones, such as Low Power Bed Fusion (LPBF), are of particular interest for the manufacturing of antenna feed chains, in particular in the case of dense array which finds application in HTS/VHTS satellite [2] or in the future 6G non-terrestrial network [3] to operate in GEO and LEO orbits, respectively.

articleTitle: Unleashing Bandwidth: Passive Highly Dispersive Matching Network Enabling Broadband Absorbing Microwave Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An electromagnetic absorber is a layer that effectively absorbs the incident electromagnetic waves, either by converting them into heat or by storing the energy of these waves for future use. Two main classical types of microwave absorbers include Dallenbach [1] and Salisbury [2] absorbers. A Dallenbach absorber comprises a metal-backed, lossy dielectric layer whose thickness is one-quarter of the wavelength. In contrast, a Salisbury absorber comprises a resistive sheet positioned at a distance of one-quarter of a wavelength from the metallic ground plane. Since the introduction of these two absorbers, extensive research has been conducted on applying these concepts to different realms of microwave engineering, employing a variety of both naturally occurring and artificially engineered materials [3, 4]. Although capable of outstanding absorption at a designated frequency, the inherent requirement of thick layers and the resulting narrow bandwidth limit the applicability of these conventional absorbers in many applications. In recent years, Employing artificially engineered surfaces, such as high-impedance surfaces (HIS) and metasurfaces, has revitalized the field of ultrathin absorbers, providing a considerable improvement in design flexibility and miniaturization [5–9]. Over the past few decades, these absorbing layers have become indispensable components in various technological applications, including energy harvesting, biomedical sensing, imaging, and stealth [10–15]. Despite achieving significantly reduced thicknesses compared to their traditional counterparts, these ultrathin absorbers often suffer from limitations in bandwidth. From a practical perspective, a key objective has been to engineer absorbers with minimal thickness while reducing reflectance across the widest possible bandwidth. Nonetheless, Rozanov’s seminal investigation [16], has set the fundamental bound on the maximum bandwidth-to-thickness ratio achievable for physically realizable thin metal-backed dielectric absorbers. As the thickness of absorbers decreases, their effective absorption bandwidth inevitably narrows. Subsequently, a comparable upper limit on the absorption bandwidth was established for thin absorbers based on metamaterial screens and high-impedance surfaces, exemplified by modified Salisbury absorbers [17, 18]. Here, we introduce an innovative design concept for ultrathin absorbers that exceeds the established threshold on the bandwidth-to-thickness ratio of modified Salisbury absorbers. Moreover, we will demonstrate that a Salisbury-type absorber designed according to the proposed concept, incorporating a specific order of dispersion in the impedance grid, can achieve a bandwidth-to-thickness ratio surpassing the limit established by Rozanov for a same-thickness Dallenbach absorber with identical dispersion order within the dielectric.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Six-Port Technology in Microwave Nondestructive Testing: Current Status and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Since its introduction in the late 1960s, six-port technology has served as a valuable tool for determining the amplitude and phase of microwave signals. This purely passive technology offers adaptability at high frequencies, extending its applicability up to the terahertz (THz) level. However, its historical limitation in sensitivity has hindered its competitiveness against traditional vector network analyzers. Despite this drawback, six-port technology possesses exceptional phase-resolution capabilities, which render it suitable for addressing emergent applications. This work outlines the evolution of six-port technology, highlighting its strengths and potential for innovative solutions in microwave nondestructive testing and beyond.

articleTitle: A Compensation Method for Reducing the Influence of Printing Voids on the Wave Propagation Properties of FDM-manufactured Dielectric Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution investigates the influence of printing voids, caused by 3D-FDM printing, on the propagation properties of such manufactured dielectric waveguides. For compensating the void effect, the paper evaluates an easy accessible estimation method, which includes the measurable mass density, dielectric mixing equations and a propagation model for rectangular and quadratic dielectric waveguides. For the validation of the proposed method numerous test objects were printed with different printer settings and were further characterized. The final results regarding the printed material’s effective permittivity and resulting propagation properties are discussed in detail. Furthermore, the printing void’s influence on applicable operation bands is presented and compensation measures are proposed.

articleTitle: A Study on Lateral Wave for Edge Diffraction of Electromagnetic Wave by Dielectric Wedges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this study, the edge diffraction of an electromagnetic plane wave by a two-dimensional dielectric wedge has been investigated by the extended PO (Physical Optics) approximation method [1]. The numerical results have then been compared with those of reference methods such as HRD (Hidden Rays of Diffraction) solution and FDTD (Finite-Difference Time-Domain) simulation. The comparison showed a good agreement between approximation methods and FDTD simulation in the outer region, while some significant differences can be observed inside the dielectric wedge as in Fig. 1(a). These differences remind us that an important contribution may be missed in our approximation solutions for the internal field. This problem is closely related to the boundary condition of the edge diffracted field, in which the diffracted field propagates in both outer and inner regions but with different wave numbers. Thus, the lateral wave is introduced to compensate for this difference between the two media.

articleTitle: Tunable Frequency Selective Antenna Based on Variable Liquid Metal Coupling Length
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article, we introduce an innovative tunable selective antenna leveraging variable liquid metal (LM) coupling length. Frequency reconfiguration is achieved by manipulating the LM length. The tuning mechanism relies on the precise movement of LM within 3D-printed microfluidic channels, controlled by varying voltage. The proposed antenna boasts a straightforward configuration and compact size, operating within the frequency range of 1-3.6 GHz. It generates multiple frequency bands including WiMAX, WiFi, and WLAN. Through meticulous optimization of the physical length of the liquid metal, six distinct frequency bands at 0.9-1.2 GHz, 1.2-1.6 GHz, 1.6-2 GHz, 2-2.4, 2.4-2.9 GHz, and 2.9-3.6 GHz GHz without any overlap are generated. Our study demonstrates a strong agreement between simulation and measurement results, affirming the efficacy of our design.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Dual-Polarized Meta-Atoms for Reflecting Meta-Surfaces Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the recent years meta-surfaces became a matter of interest in the design of electromagnetic applications. Especially reflecting meta-surfaces gain a lot of attention related to the development of the future 6 G mobile communication standard. One key technology therein is the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). In the frequency range 6 GHz - 9 GHZ, RIS are usually realized in printed circuit board technology. Therefore, electrically small patches, so called meta-atoms are placed over a ground plane. Thus, the impinging wave is modulated to reflect into a predefined direction. Often described as reflection beyond Snell’s law. A periodically repeating group of meta-atoms is called unit cell. In previous works the application of Characteristic Modes to the unit cell design for reflecting meta-surfaces has been shown [1–2]. Whereas the design of the meta-atom is considered superficially in most literature. In order to achieve intuitive insight into the entire design process the application of the Characteristic Mode theory for the meta-atom design is discussed.

articleTitle: A Topological Regularization Term for Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Inverse scattering algorithms seek to reconstruct the support and wave properties of an object through knowledge of transmitted signals and measured scattered waves. There are a myriad of techniques for reconstructing a scatterer that provide unique advantages in different imaging environments. It would thus be beneficial to use knowledge from an inverse scattering reconstruction obtained using one algorithm to improve imaging performance using a different technique. We propose incorporating prior information concerning the topology of the object being imaged into a regularization term constructed using persistent homology. The topological regularization term penalizes reconstructions which have an incorrect number of connected components and loops and updates the image to better match previous information. We aim to improve the quality of quantitative reconstructions obtained using the well-known distorted Born iterative method (DBIM) through the use of this topological regularization term. Reconstructions from simulated data and a variety of scatterers show that the addition of this novel regularization term can improve the fidelity of images obtained using DBIM and preserve topological features of the object being imaged.

articleTitle: A Compact Capsule Antenna Design Based on Metamaterial Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper a compact capsule antenna design based on a metamaterial resonator for MICS band biotelemetry applications. The main radiator of the antenna consists of electric inductive capacitive (ELC) and split-ring resonators. To assist improve impedance matching and frequency tuning, a shorting pin and slots in the ground plane are employed. The overall size of the antenna is $14 \times 14 \times 0.635 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. According to the numerical results obtained by homogeneous and realistic Hugo models, the encapsulated antenna operates at 403 MHz with 15 MHz bandwidth. To the best of our knowledge, the suggested design is the most compact encapsulated antenna reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Monopole-based Wideband Antenna with Embedded Band-notch for Applications in Upper UWB
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this letter, a wideband antenna with band-notch characteristics for application at the upper part of the ultrawideband (UWB) spectrum is presented. The proposed monopolebased wideband antenna with the in-built band-notch property has an overall dimension of $0.34 \lambda_{0} \times 0.39 \lambda_{0} \times 0.024 \lambda_{0} \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. The design incorporates a simple annular ring on the bottom layer, facilitating easier fabrication and eliminating the need for expensive microwave filters. Parameter analysis shows that adjusting the ring and patch dimensions can easily shift the stop band, effectively filtering interference in the crowded $6 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ band. The measurement results and time domain characteristics confirm that the proposed system can be a suitable, cost-effective choice for the upper UWB application.

articleTitle: Wake Fields Analysis of Curved Tube Section of Particle Accelerator by Time-Domain BEM Considering Lienard-Wiechert Fields of Electron Bunch
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electron beam dynamics in bunch compressor section of X-ray FEL and Linear Collider is very sensitive for various external disturbances, and should be carefully considered in the machine design. One of difficulties in the design of bunch compressor is exact evaluation of effects of wake fields on the beam motion at curved section of accelerator tube. In particular, it is not easy to simulate wake fields and evaluate influences on the beam dynamics at slightly curved beam tube section by using standard FDTD scheme due to its grid discretization. articleTitle: Using field-particle correlations to diagnose wave-particle interactions in laboratory experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The recently developed field-particle correlation (FPC) technique [1, 2] provides a valuable new approach to combine single-point measurements of particle velocity distribution functions and electromagnetic fields to identify the kinetic physical mechanisms underlying the collisionless energy transfer between waves and particles and to quantify the resulting rate of change of the microscopic kinetic energy density of the particles in weakly collisional laboratory and astrophysical plasmas. Although the measurement of the particle velocity distribution functions in laboratory plasmas represents a significant technical challenge, the potential for gaining invaluable physical insight from such measurements motivates the development of new diagnostics. Cutting-edge laboratory diagnostics to achieve this goal have been developed based on a number of different approaches: laser induced fluorescence, incoherent Thompson scattering, or wave absorption.

articleTitle: Physics-compliant modeling and estimation of RIS-parametrized wireless channels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this talk, we review our recent efforts to formulate, calibrate and leverage compact physics-compliant models of wave scattering in arbitrarily complex linear systems parametrized by programmable metasurfaces (also known as reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, RISs). RISs are foreseen to enable the paradigm shift toward smart radio environments.

articleTitle: Tunable Bound States in the Continuum in Toroidal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The properties of toroidal metasurfaces such as ultrahigh-Q bound states in the continuum (BIC) resonances and nonradiating anapole modes, have attracted significant attention. High-Q resonances are of particular interest for creating sensors, detectors and tunable structures. In this work, we focus on tunable toroidal metasurfaces that utilise vanadium dioxide, a widely used phase change material for active photonics and room-temperature bolometric detectors. The phase change transition of vanadium dioxide occurs in a narrow temperature range providing a large variation in material resistivity. Through heating thin film patches of vanadium dioxide integrated into a metasurface comprising gold split-ring resonators on a sapphire substrate, we achieve remarkable control over the amplitude and frequency of toroidal dipole BIC resonances due to their high sensitivity to losses present in the system. Breaking the symmetry of meta-atoms reveals enhanced tunability. The predicted maximum change in the amplitude of toroidal dipole BIC resonances reaches 14 dB with a temperature variation of approximately 10°C. The proposed tunable metasurface holds promise for various applications, including active photonic systems and room temperature bolometers.

articleTitle: Investigation on LNN-Self-Calibration Procedures for Dielectric Waveguide Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The measurement of Dielectric Waveguides (DWG) in the THz range presents unknown challenges. For transmission- and reflection based measurements of the Scattering Parameters (S-parameters), standardized calibration methods have been applied until now, with the main ones being Through, Reflect, Match (TRM) or Through Reflect Line (TRL) methods. However, all of these methods require the Device Under Test (DUT) to be removable. Therefore, an alternative method for Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) based measurements of dielectric waveguides is evaluated. In this paper we examine the possibility of applying the Line Network Network (LNN) method to dielectric waveguides. This method requires no movement of the waveguide structure in a measurement, which leads to less systematic errors and brings the possibility of free space coupled as well as directly coupled measurement setups, as the LNN relies only on the design parameters of the used DWG. The LNN method requires three consecutive obstacle positions for the calibration. This setup leads to a fully actuated self calibrating MEMS-DWG measurement setup. For this purpose, the behaviour of both DWG and dielectric slot waveguides (DSWG) have been investigated. Also, the performance of the different calibration networks was investigated. The obstacles were optimized using the LNN calibration method on simulated results at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: A deployable V-band Reflectarray Antenna for 12U CubeSat Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A deployable V-band reflectarray antenna (RA) with aperture dimensions of 504×504 mm is proposed for 12U CubeSat platform. The reflectarray board is split into three panels so that its stowage volume could reach 504×168×60 mm, to be carried on a 12U CubeSat platform with dimensions of 600×200×100 mm. Double circle rings unit-cell is used to constitute the RA for its low loss and excellent performances under oblique incidences. Theoretical computed results of RA indicate that extremely high gain, narrow beam width and low side lobe are reached. The deployment structural design of RA is also presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Fabry–Perot Cavity Antennas with Polarization-Conversion Metasurface Radiating Angularly Scannable Circularly Polarized Pencil Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: New advanced methods of polarization manipulation are gaining momentum in electromagnetic engineering community as we proceed on the path of higher frequencies and aggressive scaling. Circularly polarized (CP) beams are matter of interest, because of the inherent advantages of circular polarization, among which we may mention the absence of a specific alignment need between transmitting and receiving terminals, a higher resilience to fading, and an increased penetration capability through obstacles; this is the reason why devices operating in circular polarization regime are spreading and evolving fast in applications ranging from health engineering to remote sensing, telecommunications, and radar.

articleTitle: Specialized X-Band LNA Design for SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) utilizes the principle of radar waves reflecting off surfaces to obtain high-resolution images. SAR is typically employed by radar systems mounted on platforms such as satellites, aircraft, or unmanned aerial vehicles. Especially in military applications, SAR is utilized for tasks like enemy detection and target identification by providing high-resolution images [1, 2]. Working in the X-band is important for SAR because the X-band provides a suitable frequency range for obtaining high-resolution images. X-band frequencies are commonly used in high-resolution radar systems because this frequency range allows radar waves to reflect smaller details from objects, enabling the capture of more precise images. Therefore, SAR systems operating in the X-band are preferred for obtaining detailed and high-resolution images. In this context, the design of the LNA used in SAR systems operating in the X-band plays a significant role in improving the system’s sensitivity and enhancing the quality of high-resolution images [3].

articleTitle: In-body and on-body antennas for the ISM 2.45 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This study involved the design of three antennas, two intended for in-body applications and the other antenna for on-body use. Antennas were designed with a phantom that has the electromagnetic properties equivalent to human muscle at 2.45 GHz. The phantom has dimensions of 400 x 350 x 150 mm. Antennas were fabricated and tested using pork tissue. Simulations were conducted to investigate the transmission between these antennas within the 2.45 GHz ISM frequency band. Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) values were investigated. Fabricated in-body antennas showed good results inside the pork tissue. Simulated results also showed a transmission value of -40dB between antennas was obtained with the in-body antenna located in the center of the phantom.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Reduction Based on Disordered Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the contemporary fields of technology and defense, the research of electromagnetic cloaking technology and Radar Cross Section (RCS) reduction techniques play a crucial role [1]. The advancement of metamaterial technologies [2], especially metasurfaces [3], has introduced new perspectives and methods for RCS reduction techniques. While traditional RCS reduction research has often relied on periodic structures due to their simplicity in design and implementation, this approach has limitations in practical applications.

articleTitle: Multipath Propagation Influence on Retrievable Information in Indoor Electromagnetic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Indoor sensing of non-cooperative targets by means of systems mainly designed for wireless communication is a topic attracting huge interest. In this frame, since few years, several studies have addressed the interaction of electromagnetic waves with the surrounding environment to improve the detection and tracking performance. As a contribution to this filed, the present work focuses on a linear microwave imaging approach and conducts a theoretical analysis to investigate how multipath reflections, experienced when the electromagnetic signal propagation occurs in an indoor environment, affect the imaging capabilities. The analysis is carried out in terms of the retrievable spectral content and explores how this quantity is influenced by multipath propagation effects. As a preliminary study, a canonical indoor scenario is considered, and a 2D ray-based scalar model is adopted to model the signal propagation.

articleTitle: FDTD Examination of Propagation Effects in GPR Wall Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rebars in a reinforced concrete wall can be monitored using Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) techniques. Here the influence that the corrosion or decay of the rebars has on typical GPR signals is investigated. The absorptive characteristic of oxidised rebars is seen to be detectable, particularly using polarisation sensitive sensing schemes. The influence of the aggregate used in the concrete is also examined, and in severe cases can produce significant effects in the GPR signals. This is seen to reduce the GPR sensitivity to rebar oxidation, but can show where the concrete is becoming aerated due to corrosion.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Finite Antennas Over Two-Dimensional Infinite Periodic Structures Using Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Two-dimensional periodic structures have been widely applied to phased array antennas, frequency selective surfaces (FSS), radio wave absorbers, or reflectarrays [1–3]. Size of the two-dimensional periodic structures is often much larger than wavelength and they are modeled as infinite periodic arrays via Floquet theorem. It is well-known that numerical analysis of the two-dimensional infinite periodic arrays can be performed efficiently by Floquet theorem because the two-dimensional infinite periodic arrays are reduced to so-called unit cell owing to Floquet theorem.

articleTitle: The Veselago Lens as a Scattering Problem: 2D Solutions Through Asymptotics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution focuses on the analytical derivation of the Green’s function of the ideal lossless Veselago lens. The problem is dealt with by considering the lens as a scattering object. Then, the electromagnetic field of a linesource illuminating the lens is seen as the sum of the field due to the line-source in free space plus the scattered field due to the lens. The asymptotic evaluation is exploited to evaluate the thus obtained field integral representation. The approach is also a step towards the truncated lens case.

articleTitle: Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging by Linearized Inverse Scattering Method Based on Physical Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We report on the imaging method for targets located in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment using the inverse scattering method. We considered the application of the linearized inverse scattering method with the physical optics approximation for the metal scattering problem in the NLOS environment. By assuming geometry of the NLOS environment known, we can obtain the numerical Green’s function that connects the observation points and the imaging region and enables the application of the inverse scattering method to NLOS targets. We applied the method on a T-junction as a typical NLOS environment and validated the 2D imaging of scatterers located in NLOS region through 3D electromagnetic simulations. We confirmed that the resulting images reflect the position and size of the scatterers on the imaging plane. Therefore, the effectiveness of this imaging method is verified.

articleTitle: Radiation and Polarisation Performance of SADino: an Italian Aperture Array for Technological Verification Tests in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper focuses on SADino, an aperture array deployed at the Sardinia Radio Telescope site (San Basilio, Sardegna, Italy). SADino is a sub-array of the Sardinia Aperture Array Demonstrator, an Italian aperture array that was designed as a demonstrator of Low Frequency Aperture Array systems. The flexibility intrinsic to SADino will offer the opportunity to investigate and experimentally verify different antenna configurations and algorithms for data processing, e.g. new methods of beamforming and procedures of data calibration. In this study, the SADino performance will be investigated in terms of its radiation pattern and polarisation purity. Thanks to the possibility of re-positioning the dual-polarised antennas on the site, two different alignments of the antennas with respect to the cardinal directions have been studied. Results at 270, 345 and 420 MHz will be shown.

articleTitle: Bone Tissue Regeneration Monitoring Using Magnetic Scaffold via Microwave Imaging: a feasibility assesment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Magnetic scaffolds (MagS) are the combination of traditional biomaterials (e.g., polymers, bioceramics, bioglasses) and magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) [1]. MagS are multifunctional devices that can be controlled, in a remote and noninvasive way, by an external static or dynamic electromagnetic (EM) field. Among possible applications of MagS we can mention hyperthermia of deep-seated tumors, or enhanced drug delivery, as well as alternative diagnostic approaches. Also, MagS can play a disruptive role in tissue engineering (TE), enabling the magnetic guidance of tissue repair by using very low frequency $(1-100 \mathrm{~Hz})$ or pulsed EM fields. However, MagS are mostly developed as bone substitutes for TE applications [1], [2]. Even though MagS are intrinsically a theranostic tool, their potential is highly underestimated. In particular, limited efforts have been spent to assess monitoring capabilities of MagS for the follow up of bone tissue regeneration. A preliminary analysis on the signal level variations that can be observed during hyperthermia treatments and during bone regeneration are reported in [3] and [4], respectively. Therein, a 1D model based on the transmission line formalism and initial guideline to design a monitoring device were provided.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of Spinal Fixation System Effect on Neural Activation During Spinal Cord Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This preliminary study investigates spinal fixation system effect on neuromodulation for spinal cord system when a spinal fixation system is implanted near the lead electrodes of the spinal cord stimulator. Three implantation positions, three different stimulation waveforms, and nine nerve fiber diameters were considered in this study. For the configurations under this study, the spinal fixation system does not have significant impact on the activation threshold for the nerve system under this study.

articleTitle: Bayesian Parameter Estimation for Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering using Contrast Source Inversion and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the traditional approach to electromagnetic inverse scattering problems, we seek a single reconstruction of the dielectric properties using knowledge of transmitted signals and the measured scattered electric field. The Bayesian approach to the problem desires information regarding the posterior distribution of the dielectric properties given the data. The benefits of Bayesian parameter estimation include the ability to quantify uncertainty of any point estimation chosen from the posterior distribution, as well as a more flexible and intuitive approach concerning the injection of prior information into the inversion scheme. However, in most practical problems we are unable to analytically specify the posterior distribution and must instead rely on techniques such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) in order to produce estimates of any desired reconstruction statistics. These MCMC methods are often computationally intensive, and can be prohibitively expensive for nonlinear inversion techniques in which the dimension of the parameter space is large and multiple solutions of the forward scattering problem are required at each iteration.

articleTitle: Radar-based Tomography with Filtered Backprojection Using Attenuation and Time Shift Profiles of a Reference Reflection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper we present monostatic tomographic imaging using a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system operating from 126 GHz to 182 GHz. Instead of an active receiver, we use a metallic corner reflector that is positioned opposite the radar and behind the test object. Both radar and corner reflector are included in a parallel-beam based measurement setup, consisting of electrical translation stages and a turntable to enable measurements at multiple angular positions. The information for reconstruction was obtained by investigating the reflection of the corner reflector in terms of spatially dependent attenuation and time shift caused by a test object. Here, a 3D-printed cuboid made of polylactic acid (PLA) and a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe were placed in the middle of the measurement setup. The image processing is based on the Fourier slice theorem using the filtered backprojection algorithm, whereby the obtained data from the reference reflection is assumed as a projection separately in case of attenuation or time shift.

articleTitle: High-Q Factor Dual-Layer Anapole Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Simulation results and an experimental study are presented for a dual-layer metamaterial exhibiting a resonance with Q-factor of 4000 in the mm-wave frequency range, achieved by combining resonances from two complementary planar metamaterials. The initial layer, which is the original metamaterial, is composed of metallic unit-cells shaped like epsilon letters and is based on a high Q-factor planar toroidal metamaterial [1]. This metamaterial shows significant localization of electromagnetic energy in the near field region rather than in the radiation zone due to the destructive interference of toroidal and electric dipole moments with identical radiation patterns in the far zone. The second layer, which complements the first one, consists of a metallic layer with cutouts in the epsilon letter shape. Individually, the original metamaterial demonstrates a high Q-factor resonance and confines the electric field of the incident wave. Conversely, the inverted structure does not respond to the incident wave but is instead stimulated by near-field interaction with the original metamaterial. The low losses observed can be attributed to the interaction between the two most significant multipoles excited within the metamaterials. In the case of the original metamaterial, this interaction involves destructive interference between toroidal and electric dipole moments, leading to the formation of an anapole. On the other hand, the properties of the inverted metamaterial stem from the interaction between toroidal dipole and magnetic quadrupole moments. Both metamaterials are fabricated as free-standing to avoid dielectric losses from the substrate, which can significantly diminish the resonance’s Q-factor. The simulated metamaterial (Fig.1a) is excited with the wave polarized along the wires of the metamolecules of the original type, allowing for the support of dual loops of currents along the voids, leading to toroidal excitation. The inverted structure, rotated to complement the original one, does not exhibit excited currents with the wave’s set polarization; instead, it is activated by near-field interaction with the original metamaterial. Transmission spectra of the metamaterials at varying distances are illustrated in Fig. 1b, with optimal results obtained at a distance of 0.8 mm. The metamaterials were fabricated using a xTool laser cutter on a 50nm brass film, with the original and inverted structures comprising 10x10 metamolecules of 1.3 mm radius and periods of 2.60 mm and 2.55 mm, respectively. Experimental transmission spectra (Fig.1c) were measured utilizing a Keysight PNA Network Analyzer with VNA Extenders WR-12. The layers were housed in 3D-printed holders separated by spacers ranging from 0.6 to 2 mm in thickness. The most pronounced resonance, with a Q-factor close to 4000, was observed at a distance of 0.8 mm, similar to the simulation.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of XLA very light space-borne orientable antenna for telecommunication applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the past, many proposals for extremely large (XLA) inflatable antennas have been studied although only the ECHO I satellite has been lunched as late as the sixties, indeed the difficulty is efficiently orienting such very light and delicate structures in space. Further progress has been made with the projects ESA/NASA QUASAT in 1980s, the ARISE in 2005 and the Russian SPEKTR-R in 2011 [1]. However, XLA, having a diameter of 30 m or more, cannot be built with rigid structures like SPEKTR-R (10 m diameter and 4 ton mass).

articleTitle: Advances on Huygens Metasurface Based Transmitarrays at University of Technology Sydney
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Transmitarray antennas have attracted significant attention due to their advantages of high gain, compact profile, and adaptable radiation characteristics. Typically, they comprise multiple layers of flat antenna elements and a feed source for illumination. The phases of these elements are individually tailored to ensure suitable phase responses, thereby enabling the realization of a highly directional radiation beam with considerable gain. Transmitarrays can electronically manipulate their beams by adjusting the transmission phases of the array unit cells using PIN diodes, micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) switches or varactor diodes. In various wireless communication applications such as satellites, aircraft, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), there is a demand for conformal high-gain antennas to meet aerodynamic requirements. To address this need, conformal transmitarray antennas are highly sought after, as they can be designed to conform to the shapes of different mounting platforms. This allows for integration onto the platform surface with the feed positioned inside the platform. Given current manufacturing capabilities, one of the most practical approaches to implementing conformal transmitarrays is to utilize very thin array elements with thicknesses ranging from approximately 0.5 mm to 1 mm, facilitating ease of bending. Nevertheless, the majority of the planar transmitarrays documented in literature utilize multi-layer array elements, typically involving three or more metal layers printed onto two or more dielectric substrates. Many of these elements consists of a number of metallic vias. Consequently, these configurations are not suited for conformal transmitarray applications. Additionally, it is important to highlight that multi-layer structures incorporating metal vias for beam steering in transmitarray designs require complex packaging and fabrication procedures, potentially impacting antenna performance, particularly within millimeter-wave frequency bands. Hence, there is a pressing need for the development of dual-layer unit cells without metal vias to facilitate conformal transmitarrays and beam-steering transmitarrays.

articleTitle: Towards the validation of the semi-specific model to assess PEMFs neuroprotective effect through numerical dosimetry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The application of low intensity and low frequency pulsed electro-magnetic fields (LF-PEMFs) may represent a neuroprotective treatment of acute ischemic stroke. The ongoing I-NIC project is a double-blind study, which aims to validate PEMFs stimulation as a non-invasive, effective, tolerable, and safe tool to treat cerebral damage in patients affected by ischemic stroke. Dosimetric evaluation through the novel semi-specific numerical modelling approach, applied on active and placebo patients recruited for the I-NIC project, is currently ongoing and is showing promising results towards demonstrating the possible correlation between the reduction of the ischemic lesion and the magnetic field values induced by the PEMFs stimulation.

articleTitle: P-refinement in Electromagnetic Simulations Using Finite Element Method with Maximally Orthogonalized Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We analyze the performance of the maximally orthogonal (Max-Ortho) curl-conforming basis functions under $\boldsymbol{p}$-refinement in entire-domain finite element solutions of simple waveguide problems. In the process, we compare the Max-Ortho basis functions with the Classical basis functions and demonstrate the benefits of the former in terms of convergence and achievable accuracy. In addition, we assess the limits of the Max-Ortho basis functions in terms of maximally usable polynomial orders and finite element sizes.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dielectric Deep-Groove-Gratings as a Quarter Waveplate in the Terahertz Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: the diffractive optical elements based on planar high-resistivity silicon gratings are proposed to perform as a quarter waveplate as well as a half waveplate component in the selected band of THz frequencies. As proof of principle quarter waveplates we developed the Si-based quarter waveplate for 0.4 THz frequency demonstrating an operational bandwidth of up to 200 GHz. The finite difference time domain simulations were found in good agreement with THz time domain spectroscopy, frequency domain spectroscopy as well as vector network analyzer experiments measuring transmission amplitude and phase spectra in the range of 0.1-1.0 THz.

articleTitle: A Time Domain Combined Field Integral Equation for Open Screens
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The time-domain electric field integral equation is a versatile tool for the modelling of the scattering of transient fields by perfect conductors. It allows for the inclusion of both closed and open scatterers, and the impact of high but not infinite conductivity can be accounted for by the inclusion of a surface impedance term. Unfortunately, it cannot produce the currents induced on the front and back of a perfectly conducting open screen without further post-processing. Moreover, when a multi-screen treatment is required (when junctions are present for example), the singular time stepping matrix can lead to catastrophic loss of significant digits. To mitigate these issues, this contribution introduces a time domain combined field integral equation for these scattering problems. The equations and their discretisation are introduced and their effectiveness in fixing the above issues is demonstrated by a representative set of numerical examples.

articleTitle: A Method to Enhance the Active Modal Configuration of a Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna Array Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A mathematical model to decompose the analysis of mutual coupling in antenna arrays into lower level aspects is proposed in [1]. Thereby, characteristic modes are used as an interface to split the analysis of the coupling phenomena into two subproblems: The first subproblem is which characteristic modes are excited to which extent by the individual array elements without the presence of the other elements, and the other subproblem is how the characteristic modes of the elements are coupled to the characteristic modes of the other elements.

articleTitle: Additive manufactured antennas and feeds for terrestrial and space systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Two additive manufacturing (AM) methods used for antenna fabrication are metal printing and dielectric printing followed by conductive plating [1]. Examples of metal printed antennas are shown in Fig. 1a (linear polarized quadridge horn antenna) and Fig. 1b (circularly polarized choke ring horn antenna). The quadridge horn is part of satellite high gain reflector antenna feed, operating over 18 to 31 GHz, for use in NASA’s Wideband Commercialization Project [2]. A comparison of the antenna’s performance with a conventional machined antenna showed negligible difference over the full frequency range [3]. The choke ring horn antenna was designed for NASA’s Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe mission and had similar performance to an equivalent antenna fabricated using conventional machining [4]. The AM processes developed underwent rigorous screening and testing to yield a part with high reliability, needed in space applications.

articleTitle: A connected Vivaldi aperture array outrigger station for the BINGO radiotelescope
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The BINGO radio telescope [1], is a new radio observatory currently being deployed in the Piancó Valley in Brazil. The main telescope within this observatory comprises a dualreflector system with a 40 m diameter primary paraboloid reflector and a 36 m diameter secondary hyperboloid reflector. This dual-reflector system will be illuminated by a multihorn feed consisting of 28 circularly polarised horn antennas operating between 980 MHz and 1260 MHz. This telescope will act as a transit telescope and is designed to explore the Universe within a redshift range of 0.127 to 0.449, focusing on utilising the neutral Hydrogen emission line to map Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) with the aim of aiding in our understanding of the nature of dark energy. In addition to this science case, BINGO has the potential to detect and localise FRBs through an interferometry system, including new auxiliary, smaller radio telescopes called outriggers. The BINGO team has plans to use Vivaldi aperture array receivers to expand and enlarge the reach of the BINGO project. Such phased arrays can be used either in the form of outriggers or alternative receivers, i.e., phased array feeds, in the main dual-reflector telescope. As outrigger stations, BINGO will be able to localise up to 10 times more FRBs than the corresponding value for single reflector antennabased outriggers.

articleTitle: Hybrid Near-Field Scanning Microwave Microscope with an Optical Confocal Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: There are a number of micro-and nanometer-scale manufacturing processes, which demand or would highly benefit from tools allowing high-spatial-resolution quality control for identification of defect spots and defective parts. These may include, for example, fabrication of microfluidic components or micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) as well as certain processes and technological steps in semiconductor and electronics industries. Addressing this need, we have developed a scanning probe microscope that utilizes optical confocal distance sensor and near-fields of microwaves to probe and image samples and parts with a sub-micrometer spatial resolution, which exceeds the resolution of the available optical tools. The near-field microwave probe remains out of contact with the part/sample surface during imaging to prevent or dramatically reduce the probe damage and wear-out. The main foreseen use of the microscope is high-spatial-resolution inspection of parts with varying surface shape and/or electrical properties (dielectric constant and conductivity). As demonstrate in Fig. 1, the lateral spatial resolution of the microwave near-field probing of the tool is better than $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, which exceeds the resolution of about $2 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ of far-field optical systems currently employed in industry. The tool can be used for inand off-line inspection of topographic features, such as channels and protrusions in microfluidic systems and MEMS. Due to the ability of microwaves to penetrate through dielectric materials the microscope can be utilized for imaging of buried structures, for example, metal lines or voids in a dielectric material (see, e.g., the review [1]), which can find applications in non-destructive failure analysis of semiconductor device packaging.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Scattering from Parallel Cylinders in the presence of Perfect Electric Conductors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Scattering by a set of arbitrary cylinders in inhomogeneous scenarios represents an electromagnetic canonical problem. In particular, we consider herein the presence of Perfect Electric Conductors (PEC) bounding the region of electromagnetic wave propagation. This scenario covers a wide range of electromagnetic devices, including Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces, metagratings [1], and (in a parallel plate waveguide technology) lens antennas [2]. Interestingly, for planar PEC surfaces, an efficient analytical tool can be developed based on the extension of the scattering matrix method proposed in [3] for cylinders in free space. Notably, differently from recent contributions [2], [4], the proposed analysis tool also can consider dielectric and extended scatterers (including eventually non canonical shapes) in order to realize the desired functionalities. Additionally, this tool is adaptable also to cases where the set of cylinders is positioned within free space bounded by dihedral corners, which could be a situation of interest for antenna applications [5].

articleTitle: Modelling the Quantum Hydrodynamic Response from an Arbitrarily Shaped Nanoantenna: A Volume Integral Equation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Antennas, as transmitters and receivers of radio waves/microwaves, play an indispensable role in any modern communication system. With the advancement of nanotechnology, antennas are made smaller and smaller and nowadays down to the nanoscale. These nanoscopic antennas, aliased as “nanoantennas”, are nanoscopic replica of their radio/microwave counterparts. They interact with high frequency electromagnetic (EM) waves, e.g., optical frequencies, and radiate visible light. Nanoantennas have found a wide range of applications from nanoscopic communications, via chemistry, to biosensing, just to name a few, and themselves represent a great conceptual expansion than the conventional radio/microwave antennas. Notably, the critical feature of a nanoantenna can be made as small as a few nanometers. This very small size inevitably triggers the consideration of quantum mechanical (QM) effects. At this regime, in contrast to the “bulk material” picture where the EM response of a medium is described by macroscopic parameters, e.g., permittivity and permeability, finer “mesoscopic” material models, which can depict nonclassical effects originating from granularities in metals, must be used. Many semi-classical models (see a recent review for the models [2]) have been proposed. Among them, one category that enjoys much popularity is the hydrodynamic approach. This approach offers a set of models in a hierarchical structure. Starting from the lowest level, the inclusion of the finite compressibility of electron gas results in the nonlocal hydrodynamic Drude model (HDM) [3]. Furthermore, by considering surface scattering, the generalized nonlocal optical response (GNOR) model can be derived [4]. Last, by adding higher order terms, e.g., the von Weizsäcker term, the exchange-correlation term, the quantum hydrodynamic (QHD) model is proposed to account for quantum effects, e.g., electron spill-out, tunneling [5], [6].

articleTitle: Comparison of Vegetation Scattering Models for GNSS-R
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A variety of microwave bistatic scattering methods for vegetation layers have been developed and applied to global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R). These methods can be grouped into three categories: incoherent models based on radiative transfer (RT) theory, coherent methods based on analytical wave theory and the distorted Born approximation (DBA), and full wave simulations utilizing fast hybrid methods (FHM). Some comparisons of RT methods and FHM have been performed, e.g., in [1]. Yet, little is known about how RT and coherent methods compare. In this study, the significance of coherent vegetation scattering effects for GNSS-R is investigated using a simulated forest of truncated dielectric cylinders over a reflective surface.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance and Versatility of Wire Antennas with Metasurface Covers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: With the ever-growing demand for enhanced performance and adaptability in communication systems, several innovative approaches to improve antenna technology have been developed. Among these, metasurfaces have emerged as a key enabling technology due to their ability to achieve a precise control over electromagnetic wave propagation [1], Recent advances in this field have yielded metasurface covers capable of seamless integration with wire antennas and enabling unprecedented control over radiation and scattering patterns, received power, and impedance-matching [2–7], For instance, extensive research efforts have been put in the framework the design of cover able suppressing the scattering level of an antenna source, enabling novel degrees of freedom in the design of overcrowded telecommunication platforms [2], More recently, it has been also shown how the use of bianisotropic metasurface cloak – such as the one shown in Fig. 1(b) - may break the reciprocal behavior of conventional antennas and allow designing a radiating system with almost zero scattering and high transmission efficiency [6]–[7], This versatility extends also to the realization of reconfigurable and tunable wire antennas (such as the one shown in Fig. 1(a)), capable of adapting their radiation, frequency of operation or polarization characteristics to the evolving requirements of the communication system [4, 5].

articleTitle: A Summary of Recent Advances in Finite Element Particle in Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Particle in cell (PIC) methods is a popular means of understanding and exploiting plasma physics. This has given rise to numerous codes, both those are publicly available and others. Given the range of applications of plasma physics, from klystrons to accelerators to pulsed power devices to micro-plasma devices to high precision etching to fusion, there is a widespread need for PIC codes [1]. The literature in developing these codes is long and is summarized in [2]. While we will briefly review the state of the art, we digress to pose the problem.

articleTitle: Comparing MoM-CBFM and DDA Approaches in Solving EM Scattering of Realistic Solid Hydrometeors at Submillimeter Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: CubeSats with submillimeter ice-cloud radiometers are emerging as a promising low-cost approach for studying ice clouds to improve our understanding of Earth’s dynamic atmosphere and its impact on climate. Like for all microwave instruments, a crucial quantity for the physical (as opposed to empirical) quantitative retrieval of solid hydrometeors in the cloud is their single-scattering properties (SSPs). We previously applied the EM scattering solution method, MIDAS [1] (short for MoM Integral-equation Decomposition for Arbitrarily-shaped Scatterers), to calculate SSPs of arbitrarily shaped ice aggregates at select microwave frequencies, namely Ka, Ku, and W-bands. MIDAS applies a Method of Moments (MoM) with piecewise constant basis functions, followed by a domain decomposition method, namely the Characteristic Basis Function Method (CBFM). It has demonstrated a significant advantage in computational efficiency at the microwave frequencies mentioned above over the DDSCAT code based on Discrete Dipole Approximation (DDA), with comparable accuracy [1]. Volume-integral MoM and DDA formulations are mathematically equivalent and offer high versatility to scatterer geometry relative to other scattering solution methods, allowing calculations of SSPs for realistic complex-shaped ice hydrometeors [2]. Computational efficiency becomes thus a deciding factor in adopting one method or the other when both methods maintain satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: Exact Transmission through a Metamaterial Parabolic-Cylinder Radome
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A radome whose interfaces with the surrounding medium are confocal parabolic cylinders with the same symmetry plane is considered. The medium on both convex and concave sides of the radome is linear, homogeneous, lossless and isotropic; it is characterized by a real positive electric permittivity $\varepsilon_{1}$ and a real positive magnetic permeability $\mu_{1}$ or, equivalently, by a refractive index $n=\sqrt{ }\left(\varepsilon_{1} \mu_{1}\right)$ and an intrinsic impedance $Z_{1}=\sqrt{ }\left(\mu_{1} / \varepsilon_{1}\right)$. The radome is made of a linear, homogeneous, lossless and isotropic metamaterial characterized by a real negative permittivity $-\varepsilon_{2}$ and a real negative permeability $-\mu_{2}$ such that $\varepsilon_{1} \mu_{1}=\varepsilon_{2} \mu_{2}$. Because of causality [1], this entails that the media outside and inside the radome have real and opposite refractive indexes, and positive intrinsic impedances: $Z_{2}=\sqrt{ }\left(\mu_{2} / \varepsilon_{2}\right)$ is real positive and possibly different from $Z_{1}$. The primary field is a plane wave symmetrically incident on the concave side of the radome, and the analysis is conducted in the phasor domain, with a time-dependent factor $\exp (+\mathrm{j} \omega \mathrm{t})$ omitted throughout.

articleTitle: Perfect narrowband absorbers using simple lithography-free structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Light absorption is a key phenomenon for a variety of technologies [1]: radiative cooling, photovoltaics, sensing, communication and camouflaging are just a few examples. These applications demand scalable and compact devices that modulate their absorption spectra, usually engineered using cavities and/or periodic structures acting as resonators. Weak light matter interaction limits the absorption within ultra-compact devices, although epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials allows to greatly increase such interaction [2]. The lack of design standardization presents a big gap for designing absorbers. We present a thorough analysis of an arbitrary material on top of a PEC (perfect electric reflector) and a material separated by a spacer from the PEC. We overview the absorption phenomena for different permittivity regions, thicknesses, angles of incidence and polarization. This work helps standardize the design of these absorber configuration.

articleTitle: Toward The Design Of Preconditioners For The Global Multi-Trace Integral Equation For The Vector Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A Calderón preconditioner for the global multi-trace PMCHWT-like formulation based on the vector potential is presented. The technique is applicable on multi-domain structures containing multi-material junctions comprising both PEC and homogeneous domains. The PEC structures are simulated with EFIE-like or MFIE-like techniques. The MFIE-like equations are tested with test functions defined on the dual mesh to obtain low frequency stable results. A domain diagonal, a trace-type diagonal and a rescaled diagonal preconditioner are compared, which all show an iteration count independent on the mesh density for a global multi-trace example.

articleTitle: Far-Field prediction from a reduced number of phaseless bipolar Near Field data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper proposes an effective phaseless nonredundant Near-Field-Far-Field (NF-FF) transformation with a planar bipolar scan. The here developed characterization approach relies on the nonredundant sampling representation of the squared amplitude of the electromagnetic field, derived by assuming the source as enclosed in an oblate spheroid. A remarkable reduction (about $90 \%$) of needed NF samples, as compared to standard $\lambda / 4$ sampling, has been reached. Furthermore, by exploiting the available a priori information on the antenna under test, an effective representation of the unknown has been devised, to improve the performance of the solution algorithm. A numerical analysis has been carried out to assess the effectiveness of the proposed characterization approach.

Author Keywords: Non-redundant sampling representations of electromagnetic fields

articleTitle: Resonant free multi-trace, single source equations for penetrable structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution introduces a multi-trace, single source formulation for the scattering of time harmonic electromagnetic waves on composite structures, that does not suffer from resonance in homogeneous penetrable regions. Multi-trace, single source equations for the electric and magnetic field are combined in a novel formulation that is free of resonances. A Calderón preconditioner is applied to limit the number of iteration required for the solution of the discrete system. The fast convergence and resonant free character of this new formulation is demonstrated in a numerical experiment.

articleTitle: The Spectral Theory of Transients (STT): A Unified Formulation with Illustrative Examples
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Spectral Theory of Transients (STT) [1, 2] is a mathematical strategy for constructing exact closed-form solutions for short-pulse propagation and scattering in rather general configurations involving, for example, short-pulse propagation in inhomogeneous media, caustics, edge and head-wave diffractions, etc. It is the time-domain counterpart of the conventional complex-spectrum representation of time-harmonic wave fields.

articleTitle: Steering the Beam of an End-Fire Antenna Using Near-Field Meta-Steering Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article, a beam-steerable end-fire antenna based on the concept of near-field meta-steering is presented. The antenna design comprises a conical log spiral antenna, a phase correction surface, and a pair of near-field phase-gradient metasurfaces. The proposed 3D beam-scanning antenna exhibits a peak gain of 15.8 dBi and can steer the beam to any direction within a large conical region with an apex angle of 98°, with less than 1.3 dB gain variation.

articleTitle: Symmetries in time-varying media: on the conservation of spin angular momentum, helicity, and chirality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The introduction of time as an extra degree of freedom in optical systems, known as temporal metamaterials, significantly expands the realms of optics and nanophotonics by allowing dynamic manipulation of matter at ultrafast time scales [1]. Time-varying media break temporal symmetries and thus also have implications on fundamental physical principles potentially affecting conservation laws and symmetry properties. Regarding symmetries and conservation laws, Noether’s theorem is a crucial statement. In particular, it has been used to address the conservation of spin-dependent optical properties, like electromagnetic helicity and optical chirality, with investigations revealing insights into their conservation conditions and relationships between these dynamical properties and their associated [2–4]. In this respect, our work extends previous formalisms by using the Lagrangian formalism of time-varying media, shedding light on the interplay between time-modulation, the conservation and symmetries of spin angular momentum (SAM), helicity, and chirality. To this end, first, we define Maxwell’s equations and the Lagrangian of a time-varying homogeneous system. According to Noether’s theorem, any transformation of any dynamical variable that keeps the action integral unchanged is known as a classical system’s symmetry. So, there is a time-invariant quantity for each global continuous symmetry. Upon this ground, we investigate SAM and other spin-dependent quantities such as helicity and chirality. articleTitle: 3D GPU-based implementation of the contrast source inversion for breast lesion detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In microwave tomography, applying a proper inversion method to the measured data may result in quantitative imaging of the electrical properties (EPs) at the frequencies of the used electromagnetic radiation. Some physiopathological statuses of the breast tissue can be distinguished based on the estimated EPs [1]. A previous approach presented in [2] reports preliminary results obtained with a two-dimensional implementation of the Contrast Source Inversion (CSI) method [3] applied to simulated data. This work aims to discuss the transition to a 3D algorithm. Some optimization techniques in the MATLAB environment have been applied to the 2D version to reduce time consumption, which becomes a predominant variable with 3D data. Namely, computationally expensive operations on large data have been transferred to GPU (NVIDIA A 100 80 GB). This leads to an advantage especially for the FFT, which is performed in every iterative step. The efforts have permitted to reduce the execution time of each iterative step, reaching a speed-up factor of about 25 with respect to the CPU (Intel Xeon Gold 6430 2.10 GHz 512 GB RAM) version of the code. To obtain preliminary results about the feasibility of the 3D imaging method for detecting dielectric properties, a virtual experiment was performed. The transmit-receive setup is composed of a transmitting antenna that assumes ten equidistant positions around a cylindrical phantom, and a receiving antenna assuming forty equidistant positions around it. A heterogeneous phantom was considered, with electrical properties that emulate the ones of a healthy breast (σ = 0.1 and εr = 4), and a longitudinal cylindrical inclusion (r = 1 cm), whose high electrical properties simulate those of a breast lesion (σ = 1 and εr = 15). The incident electric field was obtained through the simulation of a Hom antenna fed at the frequency of 5 GHz, performed in Sim4Life. Total electric fields were computed in the receiving antennas’ locations and a homogeneous initial guess (σ = 0.01 and εr = 3) was adopted. An additive regularization in the CSI cost functional was introduced to overcome the image artifacts induced by the ill-posedness of the inverse scattering problem. Figure 1 provides results obtained after 3,000 iterations of CSI (about 2.5 hours of execution).

articleTitle: Dual-polarized single-layer reflectarray as passive reflecting surface for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A single layer reflectarray configuration is investigated to achieve a dual-polarization operation mode, at millimetre-wave frequencies. The reflectarray cell is proposed as a viable solution for future implementations of passive reflecting surfaces for 5G applications. The proposed configuration offers independent phase tuning in each polarization, a very thin structure ($\cong 0.0237 \lambda$ at $f=28 \mathrm{GHz}$), and small cell sizes ($\cong 0.4 \lambda$ at $f=28 \mathrm{GHz}$), thus preserving the ability to focus the main beam at large scan angles. A dual-polarized reflectarray prototype is preliminarily designed and numerically tested, demonstrating the ability of the unit cell to provide independent radiation characteristics for each polarization.

articleTitle: A Novel Dimensional Alignment of Electric and Magnetic Field Intensity Vectors in FDTD for PML Implementation (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique [1] often faces challenges in handling boundless space extensions, particularly in wave-structure interactions. A solution to this issue lies in applying an absorbing boundary condition (ABC) with the perfectly matched layer (PML) technique [2]. The PML technique, by absorbing outgoing waves without reflection, improves free-space simulation accuracy and reduces computational requirements.

articleTitle: Ultra-Broadband Material Characterization in W- and D-Band Using a Free-Space Setup
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Knowledge of the complex relative permittivity of certain materials is advantageous and even required in many areas of application. These include the different fields of electrical engineering itself, but also the intersections with other disciplines such as medicine or biology. Development is moving toward higher frequency bands and bandwidths, which underlies the advantages of higher resolution in imaging, for example. This implies that the dielectric properties of investigated materials in higher frequency bands need to be known, as these can be frequency dependent. In this paper, ultra-broadband material characterization of polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyoxymethylene (POM) and acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) samples outside of waveguide boundaries is performed using a free-space setup. The setup is fully scalable regarding the frequency range and in this work, exemplary measurements are carried out in the W-band and D-band in the frequency range from 75 GHz to 170 GHz.

articleTitle: Plane-Wave Diffraction by a Slit Formed by Two Half-Planes with a Fractional Boundary Condition: Higher Order Asymptotics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The analysis of the scattering by a slit formed by two half-planes is a crucial subject in electromagnetic theory and relevant to many engineering applications. A number of scientists have analyzed slit diffraction problems using various analytical and numerical methods. In our previous paper [1], we analyzed the diffraction by a slit in a thin material screen using the Wiener-Hopf technique and generalized boundary conditions [2]. Recently, the diffraction problems related to a fractional boundary condition (FBC) have been analyzed in several papers [3]. Several scientists have analyzed the diffraction problem related to FBC so far.
