For example, Karaçuha et al. solved the diffraction by a slotted cylinder with FBC and clarified the near- and far-fields, total radar cross-sections (TRCS), and resonances [3]. FBC shows intermediate scattering properties between perfect electric conductor (PEC) and perfect magnetic conductor (PMC). ‘Fractional’ means the fractional derivative of this paper’s total electric field components. In this paper, we shall consider a slit in an infinite plate with the FBC and analyze the E-polarized plane wave diffraction by using a Wiener-Hopf approach similar to that employed in our previous paper $[1]$.

articleTitle: The Method of Maximum Power Transmission Efficiency and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This talk presents an overview of the method of maximum power transmission efficiency (MMPTE) and its extended version (EMMPTE) and their applications. All wireless systems are aimed at maximizing the power transmission efficiency (PTE) between the transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) antennas, and the PTE can thus be considered as an essential performance index to be optimized for the design of wireless power transmission (WPT) systems and antennas. The MMPTE exploits the PTE as the performance index and c an be used to design WPT systems, as well as antenna arrays to achieve various field patterns through introducing a test receiving antenna array. It converts a field synthesis problem into a circuit analysis problem and is more accessible for those who are not very familiar with the field theory; it includes the couplings among the array elements and is applicable to the design of antenna array of any type or configuration; it incorporates the impact of physical surroundings and is applicable to any antenna array embedded in any complicated environment; it delivers the best possible solution to the array design problem wherever such a solution physically exists for a fixed configuration of the array. The basic theories of MMPTE and EMMPTE will be elaborated through a number of near- and far-field applications of antenna arrays and WPT systems both in free space and complicated environments. Highlights of the presentation include: an introduction to MMPTE and EMMPTE, the applications of MMPTE and EMMPTE in the designs of focused antenna, smart antenna, beam shaping, end-fire antenna, multi-beam antenna, polarization reconfigurable antenna, and wireless power transmission system.

articleTitle: Isogeometric Shape Optimization of Multi-Tapered Coaxial Baluns Simulated by an Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We discuss the advantages of a spline-based freeform shape optimization approach using the example of a multi-tapered coaxial balun connected to a spiral antenna. The underlying simulation model is given in terms of a recently proposed isogeometric integral equation formulation, which can be interpreted as a high-order generalization of the partial element equivalent circuit method. We demonstrate a significant improvement in the optimized design, i.e., a reduction in the magnitude of the scattering parameter over a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: The Transformer as a Balun
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: One of the main applications of transmission line transformers, in addition to being transformers, is in driving antennas as balun circuits (for example in the VHF and UHF bands). This article reports an equivalent model for a transmission line transformer through which the input impedance calculation is performed. Its operation as a balun is also described.

articleTitle: Comparison of Nested and Non-nested Direct Solver Performance for Generalized Source Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Fast direct integral equation (IE) solvers rely on the initial computation of a hierarchically-compressed blocked representation of the method of moments moment matrix, which is then factorized efficiently using specialized arithmetic [1]. The hierarchical partitioning of the matrix is inherited form that of the basis and testing functions defined on the computation domain. The blocks deemed “admissible” for compression are typically identified using a distance- and size-based criterion and are conventionally expressed by their low-rank (LR) approximation. Direct solvers can be classified by the type (“weak” or “strong”) of admissibility criterion in use and by whether the bases for the LR approximations of blocks are nested or not. $\mathcal{H}$-matrix [1] and $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-matrix [2] methods typically make use of a “strong” admissibility criterion, requiring strict separation between the subdomains on which the basis and testing functions participating in the compressed interaction are defined. While in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix approach each block is compressed independently, in the $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-matrix compression, the bases used for computing LR approximation of blocks associated with parent basis and testing function clusters are combinations of already reduced bases associated with their child subclusters, in what can be viewed as an algebraic variation (with a tighter bound on the rank) of the multilevel fast multipole algorithm [3]. The differences in performance between the two schemes and associated direct solvers have been studied extensively for conventional IEs, which make use of the free-space Green’s function kernel. Recently, with the aim of increasing the LR-compressibility of moment matrices, for impenetrable essentially convex scatterers, generalized source integral equation (GSIE) formulations have been proposed [4], [5]. These IE formulations make use of modified kernels that exhibits significant attenuation of the radiation by elemental sources into the volume occupied by the scatterer. This reduces the effective dimensionality of the truncated (via LR approximation) interactions, which are of diminished broadside and pronounced end-fire nature. These directional properties of the GSIE wave interactions may influence the interplay between child- and parent-level bases in the $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-matrix scheme and call for a designated comparative compressibility and performance study using the modified Green’s functions.

articleTitle: Wideband 1-bit Filtenna-to-Filtenna Cross-Polarization Converter for Filtering Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A filtenna-to-filtenna (FA-T-FA) cross polarization converter (CPC) with 1-bit phase resolution is investigated in this paper. Based on the 1-bit characteristic of the CPC, a filtering transmitarray (TA) is achieved. The unit cell of the TA consists of two back-to-back magneto-electric (ME) dipole antennas and matching vias. Different arrangements of matching vias can generate the 1-bit phase variation.

articleTitle: Study of debris-plasma interaction in the Earth’s ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We will present first-principles modeling and experimental results of the debris-plasma interaction that inform under which conditions ion-acoustic solitons could be generated in low-Earth-Orbit (LEO). The increasing number of small debris (>10 cm) orbiting the Earth represent a threat for present and future space assets. Unfortunately, small (sub-cm) particles cannot be detected with ground-based assets and currently there is no dedicated orbital debris detection sensor in space. Hence, new methods for characterization, detection, tracking and possibly removal of this class of orbital debris are greatly needed. A new way of detecting these small orbital debris has been proposed via ion-acoustic solitons (non-linear waves) generated by the interaction between supersonic-small-debris and Earth’s plasma environment [1–8]. Such plasma signatures can be detected as ion density enhancement traveling away from the debris which makes them good candidates for small debris detection. Using our first-principles modeling tools [9], we explored different regimes of the debris-plasma interaction to assess under which conditions solitons can form. We explore variations on plasma conditions relevant for space and laboratory plasmas, as wells as variations on charging conditions on the debris. Additionally, we present results from experiments performed at the Los Alamos National Laboratory to validate some of the modeling results.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of soliton formation in a simple ion-electron plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Orbital debris, defined as any anthropogenic space object orbiting Earth that no longer serves any useful purpose, poses a risk to all space missions. Due to the dynamic nature of the near-Earth space environment, predicting the trajectory of the debris is extremely difficult, necessitating persistent monitoring. While debris larger than 10 cm can be detected and tracked, smaller debris cannot be tracked using current capabilities. Debris that is too small to track, often termed “lethal non-trackable debris” (LNT), can create significant damage to spacecraft and jeopardize space missions. The detection, tracking, and characterization of LNT space debris would support the safe operation of valuable space assets worldwide.

articleTitle: Using Non-Thermal Electromagnetic Radiation to Track and Characterize Space Debris
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity’s (IARPA) Space Debris Identification and Tracking (SINTRA) program seeks to understand the interaction of orbital debris with the surrounding space environment to determine if this interaction can be used to detect, track, and characterize potentially lethal but currently nontrackable orbital space debris [1]. Our IARPA-funded project seeks to primarily mature the concept that non-thermal electromagnetic radiation (NTEM) generated by colliding debris can meet some of these goals.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of a Specialized Antenna Array for GNSS Receiver Anti-Interference Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to improve the anti-jamming performance of GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) receivers. Based on this, we carefully designed a seven-element circular antenna array with a center element and right-hand circular polarization. The antenna operates in the frequency band of $1.268 \mathrm{GHz} \pm 10 \mathrm{MHz}$, and the gain is greater than -5 dB in the frequency band, and the good right-handed circular polarization is achieved in the range of nearly 100°. This elaborate antenna array is then integrated into a GNSS receiver and subjected to an anti-interference test, which is carried out in an anechoic chamber. The test results highlight the excellent anti-interference performance of the receiver. Even when the interference reaches 130 dB, the receiver shows strong anti-interference ability, unswervingly maintaining its high performance, and the positioning accuracy does not degrade significantly.

articleTitle: Generation of waves by active plasma releases in the magnetosphere and solar wind
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Active experiments in the ionosphere, magnetosphere and solar wind play a role in understanding fundamental plasma physics processes. Different types of active experiments are conducted including using intense electromagnetic radiation to excite plasma waves, generating turbulence that heats the plasma, or releasing plasma into the medium and measure the response. In this talk I will present theory, 3D hybrid simulations and full PIC simulations of the interaction involving the release of different plasma ions in the magnetosphere and solar wind. Both electromagnetic and plasma release experiments can generate strong wave activity over a range of frequencies. A particularly interesting series of experiments carried out by the Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers (AMPTE) satellite mission was the release of neutral barium atoms and lithium atoms in the magnetosphere and solar wind. The AMPTE mission was designed to study the access of solar wind lithium ions into the magnetosphere and the formation of an artificial comet by barium ions. The mission was composed of three spacecraft two of the spacecraft the Ion Release Module (IRM) and the UK Satellite (UKS) were in the same orbit that took them out into the solar wind while a third spacecraft the Charge Composition Explorer (CCE) remained inside the magnetosphere where it could measure the lithium ions that made their way into the magnetosphere. The lithium atoms ionized relatively slowly allowing the lithium atoms to spread out before ionizing forming a large area in front of the magnetosphere. The barium atoms ionized by photoionization extremely rapidly forming a dense, expanding, plasma cloud that interrupted the solar wind flow creating diamagnetic cavities. On the upstream side of the cavity a region of compressed plasma and enhanced magnetic field was created as the result of being produced by the slowing down and deflection of the solar wind, and magnetic field line draping. Intense electrostatic and magnetic turbulence was observed by both the IRM satellites at the boundary of the diamagnetic cavity, with the most intense waves being detected near the outer boundary of the compressed region. Theory and simulations examine how the newly created expanding plasma couples to the solar wind by means of plasma-beam and current-driven instabilities, it is shown how lower-hybrid and lower-hybrid drift waves are generated by cross-field proton-barium streaming instabilities and cross-field electron currents. The saturation mechanism for these waves is shown to be the modulational instability described by Zakharov like equations for wave collapse. This instability can also lead to filamentation and coupling to magnetosonic modes, which are also observed. As the result of the modulational instability heating and acceleration of electrons occurs, that is consistent with the observations. The talk will present data, theory and simulations of the plasma release experiments.

articleTitle: Classification of Range-Doppler Radar Echoes for Condition Monitoring in Industrial Processes: Shallow Learning versus Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The process industry (PI) is extremely diverse. In consequence, a plethora of technical processes are applied, which often involve liquids, being processed, stored and transported in chemical as well as biological reactors and tanks. Tailored to such applications, we have previously proposed a novel approach for condition monitoring (CM). Herein, radar systems are used and their functionalities are augmented, which allows for precise and accurate level measurements of liquids, alongside the distinction between different process conditions (PCs). For this purpose, range-Doppler radar measurements are classified based on manually extracted distinctive, highly interpretable features and state-of-the-art techniques from shallow learning (SL). The objective of this contribution is to compare our approach with techniques from deep learning (DL). For data acquisition, typical PCs have been selected: filling, draining, heating, boiling and stirring (with and without foaming). The measurements have been conducted using a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) Doppler radar system, operating in the V-/W-band. As shown, with deep neural networks (DNNs) and appropriate data preprocessing, the accuracy can be increased significantly, by up to 2% and more, despite only very limited training data.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Analytic and Numerical Versions of the Laplacian Representation Approach for the Asymptotic Part of the Layered-Medium Green’s Function in the Mixed Potential Formulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We report on developments in the evaluation of matrix elements of the electric and magnetic field operators involving the asymptotic (large transverse wave-number or small transverse distances) components of the mixedpotential Green’s function of a layered medium. Subtracting these asymptotic terms significantly accelerates numerical computation of the Sommerfeld-type integrals required in constructing Green’s function [1]. The described method is applicable to planar conducting structures embedded in a multi-layered medium. Ability of a fast and accurate evaluation of matrix elements for such structures is critical in many applications, especially in solving forward problems in design and optimization of electromagnetic metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Vector Sensor Satellite for Detection of Harmful Space Debris
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The number of satellites launched into low Earth orbit (LEO) is increasing at an exponential rate. Currently, there are about 27,000 known space objects and over 100 million of unknown pieces of space debris. Collision avoidance requires precise knowledge of the positions for all space objects. New techniques are being developed to detect the small, < 10 cm, objects by the plasma waves they generate in space. The bases for these techniques are that all space objects in orbit around the Earth (1) pass through a magnetized plasma, (2) become electrically charged, and thus (3) produce detectable plasma waves. Field aligned irregularities (FAIs) in the path of orbiting space objects are monitored by the HF radar backscatter and by in situ electron density probes. Space debris and satellites moving through these irregularities and can excite plasma emissions such as whistler, compressional Alfven, or lower hybrid waves. Orbital kinetic energy is the source of lower hybrid waves which is converted into an electromagnetic plasma oscillation when a charged space object encounters a field aligned irregularity (FAI). Such compressional Alfven wavs and whistlers propagate undamped at between 400 and 9000 km/s from the source regions and can be detected at ranges up to 50 km.

articleTitle: Machine Precision Numerical Evaluation of Reaction Integrals in the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: One of the elements that affects the overall accuracy of the solution of Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) via the Method of Moments (MoM) is the accuracy in the numerical evaluation of the double surface reaction integrals that constitute the system matrix, especially for its near-field part (present in any applied fast solution method). Each reaction integral is formed by a source (inner) integral, that can be singular, and a test (outer) integral. The source integral singularity is due to its kernel that is the background Green’s function for the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) or the gradient of the background Green’s function for the Magnetic Field Integral Equation (MFIE).

articleTitle: Parallel Fast Iterative H-Matrix Locally Corrected Nyström Discretization of Integral Equations with an Inaccurate H-matrix Preconditioner
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this research, a new method is presented for addressing the Combined Field Integral Equation (CFIE) using the Locally Corrected Nyström (LCN) technique, focusing on speed, error control, and parallel processing features of the implementation. The method involves utilizing a less precise preconditioner derived from the coefficient matrix, which accelerates the whole process despite its reduced accuracy. However, this fast approach has some challenges in trading-off between solution speed and accuracy since we are approximating H-LU decomposition as well. This is particularly affecting the residual and precision of the solution when dealing with CFIE problems. The method implemented uses MPI parallelization for coefficient filling, and it uses HLibPro, which is OpenMP parallelized, to construct H-Matrices and perform H-LU factorization. To reach the desired compression, ACA method is used to compress the matrices to the tolerance required. Giving larger tolerance to preconditioner matrix and H-LU factorization, makes the problem hard to converge to the desired accuracy. As a reason, it is necessary always to trade-off between accuracy, the speedup and compression of the matrices. To illustrate its efficacy, consider Nasa Almond with 84,000 unknowns (where $l=240 \mathrm{~m}$) exposed to an z-polarized dipole located in the x direction in the far-field. The operating frequency is set at 3 MHz, with geometric dimensions spanning two wavelengths. As it is shown in Fig. 1, the Compression Rate (CR) achieved for the preconditioner H-matrix is $91.56 \%$, while for the coefficient matrix, it is $85.44 \%$. The relative error of the computational problem, $|A x-b|$, is quantified at $4.1023 \mathrm{e}-09$, which converges in four iterations. Moreover, the CPU time required to build both H-matrices is 9555.36 seconds, while it takes 4130.66 seconds to do H-LU factorization with 40 cores working in parallel.

articleTitle: Advanced anapole effects in dielectric and metallic metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Anapole mechanisms have been broadly investigated in nanophotonics for the possibility to obtain invisible electromagnetic devices [1]. In the context of nanostructures with dipolar response, such states are typically understood as the result of destructive interference between quasi-static electric dipole and toroidal dipole. However, the richness of the physics associated with higher order multipoles open several possibilities to achieve anapole effects in other exotic ways. In this talk, two anapole mechanisms in dielectric and plasmonic meta-optics will be presented. First, an anapole mechanism in dielectric metasurfaces due to the interplay between high order multipoles will be discussed [2]. In a dielectric metasurface with inversion symmetry, multipoles of odd [e.g., electric dipole (ED), magnetic quadrupole (MQ)] and even parity [e.g., magnetic dipole (MD), electric quadrupole (EQ)] are decoupled [3]. Multipoles of each parity can exhibit an anapole state based on the destructive interference between multipoles of the same parity. This lattice anapole mechanism explains the origin of accidental bound states in the continuum (BICs) in symmetric dielectric metasurfaces. Specifically, we demonstrate that these states are nonradiating eigenmodes of the system. We exploit such modes for the realization of quasi-BIC with high-quality factor resonances. Contrary to existing techniques, our system allows us to achieve the transformation of a nonradiating BIC into a radiating quasi-BIC under normal radiation incidence and only due to a change in the period of the metasurface [2]. In general, such transformation can happen for other rather simple perturbations of the system, such as by introducing a variable superstrate, which is particularly suitable for sensing applications. Second, the talk includes a focus on anapole states in plasmonic meta-atoms, and a close-toideal plasmonic meta-atom will be discussed. This meta-atom is characterized by low absorption, high near-field enhancement, and negligible scattering due to the anapole effect [4]. We show that the anapole state of this metaatom can be qualitatively explained via destructive interference between quasi-static electric dipoles associated with complementary subvolumes of the nanostructure. We numerically demonstrate the use of this meta-atom as a building block for transparent metasurfaces and metamaterials.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antennas Enabled by Compliant Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Today’s ever-expanding need for wide- and multi-band communications systems places considerable burdens on available apertures. Many systems now operate over multiple bands simultaneously while requiring tunable behaviors such as beam forming and steering, nulling, polarization modulation, amongst others. While phased array systems have largely been successful in realizing many of these phenomena, they are ultimately limited in applications where extreme reconfigurability is needed to achieve a targeted performance (e.g., mechanical deformation) and when dealing with high power microwaves (HPMs). To this end, researchers have augmented classical antenna systems with metamaterials to enhance their intrinsic properties and introduce new pathways to tunability. However, careful considerations need to be taken when designing metamaterial antennas for HPM applications due to their tendency to strongly localize incident fields [1]. Therefore, reconfigurable antenna technologies that can enable unprecedented tunability, mechanical ruggedness, and HPM compatibility are extremely desirable. To this end, compliant mechanisms [2] are an attractive pathway for meeting these challenges. Compliant mechanisms are mechanical structures that realize complex mechanical movements with simple actuations and without gears, pulleys, or hinges, but rather through intelligent design and exploitation of their intrinsic material properties. Compliant mechanisms are often fabricated through additive manufacturing which further lends themselves to rapid prototyping and integration into antenna systems as dielectric support structures or metalized components. An overview of compliant mechanisms for next generation reconfigurable electromagnetic devices was presented in [3]. Figure 1 presents a visual synopsis of many of the desirable properties of tailored compliant mechanisms for reconfigurable antenna design. This presentation will summarize the current state of the art in compliant mechanism augmented antenna design and showcase multiple fabricated and measured prototype devices.

articleTitle: Deep learning procedures for the inverse design of electromagnetic devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revealed the most investigated topic in the last years in many branches of scientific research, ranging from medicine to civil engineering and ICT applications. In this framework, different problem-solving paradigms emerged during the years related to the most convenient way of dealing with the available data from which the AI has to take profit. In the field of applied electromagnetics, deep learning (DL) procedures have been extensively investigated so far. Actually, they revealed effective in dealing with situation of practical interest (e.g., biomedical diagnostics) because of their capability of learning the relevant features from the available data. Hence, in developing this kind of tools a key role is played by the training dataset, as well as by the user’s experience in setting the network parameters in a proper fashion.

articleTitle: Efficient Solutions of Time-Domain Volume Integral Equations Based on Meshless Discretization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) interaction with inhomogeneous and/or anisotropic penetrable objects can be formulated by volume integral equations (VIEs) in the integral equation approach. When the EM wave is transient, the time-domain VIEs (TDVIEs) are required to describe the transient behavior. Conventionally, the TDVIEs are solved by discretizing the time domain with the march-on-in-time (MoT) scheme and discretizing the space domain with the method of moments (MoM). However, the time-domain MoT scheme may have a late-time instability while the MoM requires conforming meshes and double-fold numerical integrations which are tedious and expensive. In this paper, we propose a hybrid scheme to solve the TDVIEs, where the time domain is discretized by a Galerkin’s method with Laguerre functions while the space domain is meshed by a truly meshless method (TMM). The proposed scheme can fully eliminate the late-time instability in time domain and greatly reduce the discretization cost in space domain. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the scheme and its excellent performance has been authenticated.

articleTitle: Reflection and Transmission at a Parabolic-Cylinder Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The two-dimensional problem of the reflection and transmission of a plane electromagnetic wave symmetrically incident from either the convex or the concave side on a parabolic-cylinder interface separating two different media is solved exactly and in closed form, in the phasor domain. The two media are linear, lossless and isotropic, are either isorefractive or anti-isorefractive to each other, and are characterized by different intrinsic impedances. In the anti-isorefractive case, the double-negative metamaterial on one side of the interface has real negative permittivity and real negative permeability; because of causality, its refractive index is negative and its intrinsic impedance is positive [1]. Thus, the two media have real propagation constants of opposite sign, and real positive intrinsic impedances.

articleTitle: Multilayer K-Band 4 × 4 Planar Array for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized 4x4 antenna array with beamforming capabilities, operating at 18.9 GHz. The antenna is integrated in a multilayer PCB in a vertical stacking and it can be scaled to fit applications such as new space satellite communications. By using the sequential rotation (SR) technique, it is possible to achieve both for LHCP/RHCP. In this paper, two different SMP mini connectors will be used to measure the resonance of multiple radiating elements testing: 1) the discrepancies between simulation and measurements of the active element and 2) which connector is more suitable for the task at hands.

articleTitle: Research of anapole modes in ring-shaped subwavelength periodic structures fabricated on thin free-standing metal film
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Over recent years, numerous designs of metamaterials with diverse functionalities have emerged from various research groups, including negative-refractive-index materials, electromechanical metamaterials, chiral materials, photonic crystals, electromagnetic cloaks, and optical metamaterials [1], [2]. Based on the type of electrical conductivity involved, metamaterials can be categorized into those utilizing metals and those relying on the dielectric optical properties of materials. Ultrathin planar metamaterials composed of periodic subwavelength structures are meticulously arranged to show remarkable electromagnetic characteristics, where the anapole states are of particular interest seeking to realize nonradiating electromagnetic sources [3], [4].

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing for 5G: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) comprises a relatively new set of fabrication tools that enable designs that cannot be produced by traditional fabrication methods (e.g., machining, or molding/casting), but also have material and design limitations that are not fully understood and are evolving rapidly as the technology continues to improve. In this environment, its imperative that RF and AM engineers work collaboratively to get the most out of the new opportunities enabled by AM, while planning for the challenges and uncertainties of a new technology. Here we present three case studies from recent and ongoing projects at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (JHU/APL) that highlight a range of opportunities and challenges regarding AM for 5 G applications.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Compatibility of Wireless Transmission in High-Speed Railway Train Control System Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the high-speed railway environment, electromagnetic interference poses a significant threat to radiocommunication within train control systems, leading to critical security concerns for railway transportation and passenger safety. To tackle the electromagnetic compatibility challenges of wireless links in complex circumstances, a method based on knowledge graph for analysis and management is proposed. This method establishes an electromagnetic compatibility knowledge graph for the wireless transmission in the railway train control system by representing the three elements of electromagnetic compatibility as triple information in the graph database. Furthermore, the application of the knowledge graph is discussed with practice cases. This approach offers a thorough and efficient electromagnetic compatibility analysis framework for the wireless transmission in train control system, supporting the stable operation and safety of the high-speed system.

articleTitle: Diffraction by circular pin: Wiener-Hopf method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The paper considers the boundary value problem of the diffraction of a symmetric TE-wave by a semi-infinite pin located coaxially inside a circular waveguide. The problem is reduced to a system of singular integral equations, which is solved by the Wiener-Hopf method in the class of meromorphic functions. Based the factorized Bessel functions and the entire function, a technique for constructing a solution in the form of the Fourier component of the surface current density is developed. The Meixner condition is satisfied by shifting the zeros of the entire function. The correctness of the solution was verified using the stitching method. The solution also provides a limiting transition to a thin pin, where a semi-infinite pin and a hollow cylinder of the same radius are physically equivalent. In the case of the limiting transition, when the radius of the pin approaches the radius of the waveguide, the solution provides a complete reflection of the oncoming mode, which is the only mode of the waveguide propagating in the opposite direction.

articleTitle: Circular Dielectric Waveguides for D-Band Applications in Communications and Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Dielectric Waveguides (DWGs) are mechanically flexible, lightweight and potentially very cost-effective. For the preferred low-loss materials like PE (Polyethylene) or PTFE (also known as Teflon) the required inner core’s diameter of circular DWGs is a bit less than the free-space wavelength, and the lower-permittivity cladding’s diameter is typically 2.5 to 3 times the core diameter [1]. This results in a cable diameter of only a few millimeters (5…7 mm) if we operate the DWG within the D-Band frequencies (i.e., 110-170 GHz). On the other hand, the losses of such waveguides increase more or less linearly with the frequency. Therefore, in terms of manufacturability, size, and performance, we believe that the D band is an optimal choice for DWG-based interconnections, if their length is in a range of approx. 1 … 30 meters.

articleTitle: The Fredholm Factorization Method Directly Applied to Generalized Wiener-Hopf Equations for Wedge Diffraction Problems in Complex Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work we present a new and comprehensive theory for the solution of electromagnetic diffraction problems involving impenetrable wedges in arbitrary linear media. This theory utilizes Bresler-Marcuvitz transverse equations, characteristic Green’s function procedure, and the Wiener-Hopf technique to address complex scattering problems [1]. The effectiveness of this technique has already been demonstrated in the analysis of wedge problems in isotropic media [2], and now we have extended its application to more general cases [3–4]. We derive Generalized Wiener-Hopf equations (GWHEs) from spectral functional equations in angular regions filled with arbitrary linear media with the application of boundary conditions as solution of transverse equations. These equations can be systematically interpreted with network formalism. We recall that GWHEs have plus and minus unknowns that are defined into different complex planes but related together. We believe that this mathematical technique significantly expands the possibilities for spectral analysis of electromagnetic problems involving angular regions filled with complex arbitrary linear media. We observe that the GWHEs in arbitrary linear media usually report physical unknowns defined into multiple complex planes (more than 2) as the physical problem usually contains more than one propagation constant. Traditional spectral methods such as SommerfeldMalyuzhinets (SM) method, the Kontorovich-Lebedev (KL) transform method, and the Wiener-Hopf (WH) method are fundamental and complementary in studying diffraction problems in presence of sharp discontinuities immersed in isotropic region. The primary benefit in utilizing the SM and KL techniques is the application of the spectral complex angular plane derived from the Sommerfeld integral theory, which has also been successfully applied in the Wiener-Hopf framework through the concept of rotating waves in isotropic angular region, see for instance [2] and references therein. However, the definition of this complex plane is possible in problem with one propagation constant. One of the most important result obtained in presence of anisotropic media is the exact solution obtained by Felsen in the case of the scattering by a PEC wedge immersed in uniaxial medium illuminated by plane waves at normal incidence [5], by applying a generalized version of separation of variables. In the present work, we apply for the first times direct Fredholm factorization [6] to GWHEs avoiding introduction of spectral mapping to resort to CWHEs. In particular the method is effective for problems with more than one propagation constat where the spectral mapping cannot be introduced, and other techniques are ineffective. The fundamental tool in direct Fredholm factorization is the application of Cauchy integral representation to GWHEs that allows to represent unknowns in one complex plane starting from multiple complex planes. With this tool we allow all unknows of GWH problem to be represented using integral equations in one complex plane that can be regularized with Fredholm factorization procedure, see for instance [6, 7]. The proposed methodology is validated through examples, beginning with the examination of diffraction by a PEC wedge in anisotropic media.

articleTitle: On a Novel Calderón Preconditioning Strategy Based on High-Order Quasi-Helmholtz Projectors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The first of Calderón identities indicates that the operator of the electric field integral equation (EFIE) can potentially act as a preconditioner for itself. However, the discretization of this preconditioning operator via the boundary element method (BEM) requires constructing a dual space commonly defined on a barycentric refinement of the orginal mesh. This contribution introduces a novel Calderón strategy that leverages high-order quasi-Helmholtz projectors. Unlike the standard strategies, which are based on barycentric refinements, a dual space is obtained by combinating functions of higher order. This strategy allows the development of a discretization of the Calderón identity that is suitable for arbitrary order. The well-conditioning of the proposed formulation is investigated, and numerical results are presented to corroborate the theory.

articleTitle: An Efficient GPU Acceleration Scheme for Solving Electromagnetic Problems with Moderate Scales
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient graphic processing unit (GPU) acceleration scheme for solving electromagnetic (EM) problems governed by integral equations. The conducting targets are considered and the electric field integral equation (EFIE) is used to formulate the problems. The EFIE is discretized by the method of moments (MoM) and the resultant matrix equation is solved by the proposed GPU acceleration scheme under constrained computational resources. A numerical example regarding EM scattering by an airplane model is provided to demonstrate the scheme and the speedup up to 19.49 times is achieved.

articleTitle: T-method Time-domain Analysis of Eddy Currents on Bellows Duct of Booster Synchrotron in Synchrotron Radiation Facility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents 3D eddy current analysis using current vector potential method (T-method) for bellows beam duct of booster synchrotron at the UVSOR synchrotron radiation facility. To achieve immediate acceleration of an electron bunch, rapidly increased and strong dipole magnetic field is imposed at curved section of beam duct of booster synchrotron (Fig.1). Accordingly high intensity eddy currents are induced at the curved section and it is necessary to consider to suppress influences of the eddy currents for electron beam dynamics. For this purpose, beam duct of the booster synchrotron at the UVSOR has bellows structure for longitudinal direction of electron motion (see Fig.1). On the other hand, effects of such the bellows structure for suppression of eddy currents were not evaluated quantitatively yet.

articleTitle: Adaptable MRI Coils for Enhanced Deep Brain Stimulation Imaging: A Bioengineer’s Guide from Concept to Clinic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Ultrafast MRI at 3 T and above has fundamentally transformed neuroimaging. It enables dynamic sub-second monitoring of brain function while providing sufficient soft tissue contrast to allow precise delineation of submillimeter cerebral structures. When used in conjunction with neuromodulation therapies such as deep brain stimulation (DBS), MRI can provide indispensable insights into electrode positioning and the functional response to stimulation. However, MRI remains largely inaccessible to patients with DBS devices due to the risks associated with RF heating of the implants. Despite continuous efforts, progress in making 3T MRI readily accessible to this patient population has been limited.

articleTitle: On Computation of Green’s Function for 1-D Periodic Structures in Planar Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Efficient resolutions of recurring source [1] or medium boundary [2] configurations are robust tools in computational electromagnetics for developing modern engineering systems. Herein we touch upon the Green’s function (GF) of Helmholtz equation for a scatterer with infinite periodicity in a planar layered medium, as a proper combination of formulations in [1] and [2] conveying the benefits of each to the end usage. In [2], for a single electromagnetic line source (SELS) situated in the layer $\# i$, the GF observed at the layer $\# j$, the scattered field contributions through continuous integration of all the spectrum of plane waves that are reflected back and transmitted through the medium of arbitrary number of planar layers is efficiently performed via the suitable quadratures, in addition to the closed form identities of the same spectrum for the direct part representing radiation in the free-space with the wave number $k_{s}$.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation Of An Em Scattering Formulation For Buildings With Multiple Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic wave propagation in urban environments is a complex problem due to interactions with buildings and one needs knowledge of high-frequency scattering characteristics, such as reflection and diffraction. Scattering by a building with windows is one of the most important problems, as it consists of conductive and dielectric materials. In order to analyze and predict the EM wave behavior in such scenarios, analytical and numerical approaches are essential. The Kirchhoff Approximation (KA) is one method for calculating the high-frequency scattering of EM waves. It has been successfully applied to analyze the scattering field by a single window aperture with/without window glass on an infinite conducting screen [1], [2].

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of SKA-Low Antenna Arrays with Dynamic Macro Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The SKA-Low radio astronomy telescope forms part of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) project. Accurate electromagnetic modelling of SKA-Low arrays consisting of SKA log-periodic antenna (SKALA) elements, is crucial to optimising the instrument’s performance. The current approach is to use iterative solvers based on the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM), however, the associated computational cost is a limiting factor to exploring station design layouts. This paper presents SKA-Low antenna array analysis results, using an alternative dynamic macro basis function (MBF) iterative solver and nested cross approximation (NCA). Significant runtime improvements over the MLFMM solver in the commercial FEKO software suite are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Flow around Metasurface Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Thin metasurface structures have been used as electromagnetic sensors to measure two-dimensional (2-d) radiofrequency (RF) field distributions incident on the surface. For example the electric field distribution was detected by the lumped resistors embedded in a mushroom-shaped metasurface absorber, which worked as a short-dipole array. The resistors interconnecting the square metal patches on the surface in the x - and y -directions absorbed the incident power of the Ex and Ey polarizations at the resonance frequency of the mushroom structure [1]. While the single-layer mushroom structure provided high absorption inherently at a single resonance, a broadband characteristic was achieved by using a stacked structure of two mushroom layers [2]. The voltages on the individual resistors were monitored by RF detectors to map the 2-d amplitude and phase profiles of the RF electric field vectors incident on the surface. The measured field distributions were used for in-situ and real-time monitoring and localization of RF noise sources. The accuracy and effectiveness of the measurement technique was evaluated and confirmed for spherical wave illumination based on a numerical analysis using the plane-wave spectrum (PWS) technique [3]. The electromagnetic field of the spherical wave incident on the absorber surface was expanded into a large number of plane waves, for each of which reflected and absorbed fields were calculated by treating the metasurface as an equivalent impedance surface using an effective medium model. The plane wave fields were then synthesized to obtain the spatial distributions of the reflected and absorbed fields on the absorber surface. The results of the numerical analysis were practically in good agreement with those of electromagnetic simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Real-Time Identification of Small Objects with Inaccurate Background Wavenumber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: There exist various non-iterative algorithms for identifying unknown targets from scattering parameter data for example, bifocusing method, direct sampling method, factorization method, Kirchhoff migration, MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), and orthogonality sampling method. Throughout many researches [1, 2, 3, 4] it turned out that they are fast, effective and stable methods.

articleTitle: Diffractive Deep Neural Networks based on Programmable Nonlinear Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Neural morphic computing, including all-optical diffractive deep neural networks (D2NNs) and photonic circuit neural networks, has gained popularity for their fast and efficient computing architecture. Microwave-based D2NNs have also been proposed, such as reconfigurable metasurface-based D2NNs that allows real-time adjustment of transmittance weight using programmable amplifiers [1]. Planar neural networks constructed using artificial surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) have also been developed, where the programmable weight matrix can be modulated in real-time by controlling the voltage applied to a varactor diode coupled to the SSPP coupler [2]. However, these designs lack reconfigurable and self-contained non-linear activation functions that do not rely on external digital control circuits.

articleTitle: Conformal Electromagnetic Skin Based on Flexible Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the last years the diffusion of wireless sensors for health related applications is increasing exponentially. The unlicensed millimeter-wave (mmW) band around 60 GHz offers advantages in terms of miniaturization and wide bandwidth. Since these devices operate in contact or in proximity of the human body, they need to be tested in real exposure condition. While for ethical reasons compliance testing is not performed directly on human beings, it is possible to use phantoms that reproduce the electromagnetic (EM) properties of biological tissues. Compared to liquid [1] and semisolid phantoms [2], solid phantoms have the advantage to be long lasting and do not require any shell [3]. However, at mmW it is challenging to find a combination of materials that allow to match the permittivity of the skin (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 7.98 – j 10.90) without using water. The only available solution are solid, but rigid phantoms, that are representative only for a predefined posture of the body. As an alternative solution, this paper proposes a skin-equivalent solid and flexible phantom that reproduces the reflection coefficient at the air/skin interface in the 55-65 GHz range. The phantom consists in a 2.1-mm layer of silicone and carbon powder (40% of the composite weight) backed by an electrotextile (Fig.la). The thickness of the silicone/carbon layer is optimized to approach the skin reflection coefficient when considering a transverse magnetic (TM) or transverse electric (TE) impinging plane wave for the angles of incidence from 0° to 60°. The maximum relative error between the reflection coefficient of the realized phantom and the skin is 2.6% for the magnitude and 13%. The phantom has been experimentally validated using a free-space transmission/reflection system. The measurement results of the magnitude of the reflection coefficient for normal incidence (see Figure lb) are in good agreement with numerical simulations, showing a relative error within 1.9% in the 55-65 GHz range. Such a phantom represents a promising solution for body-centric measurements where reconfigurable, flexible, conformal or dynamic body models are necessary.

articleTitle: Drude-like Scatterers for Reconfigurable Multipolar Refractive Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Refractive Huygens metasurfaces represent a radical advancement in the fields of electromagnetics and optics. These devices, consisting of subwavelength transmissive meta-atoms, can be designed to tailor the phase, amplitude, and polarization of incident electromagnetic waves in unprecedented ways [1].

articleTitle: Pulsed Electric Fields for Regeneration of Injured Spinal Cord: Calcium Oscillations Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The European RISEUP project, funded by the Future and Emerging Technologies (FET) Open of Horizon Europe Program 2020, explores the possibility of applying pulsed electric fields to repair Spinal Cord Injuries, taking advantage of the well-established effect of cell membrane electropermeabilization. An Electro Pulsed Bio-hybrid (EPB) device delivers specific electrical stimulation protocols, based on microsecond pulsed electric fields, that support and guide the differentiation of stem cells to generate a cell bridge on the lesion. Stem cell differentiation is regulated by the intracellular calcium concentration which is considered a possible target of the interaction with the pulsed electric field. In this context, multiphysic and multiscale computational modelling is a key tool to understand and predict the outcomes of in vitro experiments on stem cells.

articleTitle: A Study of Resonance Modes for Microwave Imaging in Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The present numerical study explores the resonant modes generated within a microwave imaging chamber having perfectly conducting walls and loaded by a breast phantom. The objective of this preliminary work is to investigate whether such a resonant set-up, and an understanding of the modal field distribution, can be used to improve microwave imaging. As such the perturbation of the resonant frequencies and associated modes are identified utilizing the eigenmode projection technique. A simplified 2D model is utilized to assess the sensitivity of the resonant modes and frequencies to various tissues, such as different sizes, shapes, and locations of tumour and fibroglandular tissue regions, located within the breast model. It is found that there is a considerable variation in the sensitivity of the resulting modes to tissue anomalies located within the breast.

articleTitle: Effect of Data Compression on Crack Location Prediction Using Acoustic Emission Sensor Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Acoustic emission based Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) sensors are installed on structures for continuous data collection to determine anomalies (e.g., crack, corrosion) and prevent unexpected failures. Due to the aging infrastructure in the world (e.g., pressure vessels, pipelines, power plants), the demand for SHM sensors for 24/7 monitoring has increased dramatically. Acoustic Emission (AE) method is a non-destructive evaluation (NDE) method based on detecting and characterizing elastic waves released by rapid release of strain energy from a localized source (e.g., crack growth) within a material.

articleTitle: Quantum Information Science Approach to Linear and Nonlinear Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The presence of waves in laboratory and space plasma is due to collective processes which are inherently classical in nature. The linear propagation of electromagnetic waves follows from Maxwell equations in which the constitutive relations are obtained using either a kinetic or a fluid description of the plasma. Even though these descriptions require a large number of charged particles inside a Debye sphere, the interparticle distance is long compared to the de Broglie wavelength of any electron or ion in the plasma. As such, quantum effects are negligible and classical treatments have been successful in providing insight into plasma behavior in fusion, terrestrial, and space plasma. However, this does not preclude the exploitation of quantum computers for simulating classical plasma. It requires us to formulate appropriate theoretical models that appear to be “quantum-like” while maintaining the integrity of the classical description of electromagnetic wave propagation in plasma.

articleTitle: Reconnecting Compressed Current Sheets: Impact of Highly Sheared Flows and Resulting Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We investigate kinetic-scale current sheets with a magnetic field reversal that are formed by compressing a larger scale fluid current sheet down to kinetic scales. The compression forces the current sheet to generate an intense localized ambipolar electric field in the Hall direction. As a result, the ions do not fully respond to the electric field, while the electrons develop an intense sheared ExB flow, which carries a current and alters the structure of the current sheet, giving it multiple spatial scales and enabling bifurcated or embedded current sheets to form depending on the level of compression. The localized electric field also modifies the particle orbits and the equilibrium distribution functions leading to non-gyrotropic distributions by renormalizing the gyromotion. We model this physics via an exact Vlasov equilibrium [1] which captures the essential physics of compression and through asymptotic perturbation theory. This equilibrium is shown, through a non-local linear analysis, to be unstable to lower-hybrid waves due to the electron-ion hybrid (EIH) instability [2]. The analysis shows that the electrostatic EIH develops eigenmodes which are confined to the central portion of the current sheet near the magnetic field reversal point and can lead to substantial anomalous dissipation, both resistivity and viscosity, which can impact reconnection. We model this physics through rigorous eigenmode analysis and through first principles particle-in-cell simulations. With the resulting models and simulations, we are able to make direct comparisons with observations from NASA’s MMS mission [3, 4].

articleTitle: Well-conditioned T-Matrix Method for a Dipole-Excited Infinite Dielectric Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The elements for the scattering of the source fields with finite support by objects of longitudinal uniformity are still under development to model novel use cases [1], [2]. Here we revisit a classical approach formulating its well-conditioned version for a dielectric cylinder illuminated by a dipole. This requires the numerical quadrature evaluation on a path of the complex plane representing the longitudinal spectrum [3], each contribution of which is the outcome of the 2.5 dimension problem formulated on the transverse plane in terms of 2D coupled polarization surface integral equations (2) elaborated via extended boundary condition method [4]. Also known as the T-Matrix method, this method has recently been approached to have its linear algebraic systems well-conditioned for normal incidence in 2D [5] and its specified treatment to the solutions of coupled unknowns in the transverse plane with the complex-valued wavenumbers is incorporated herein.

articleTitle: Finite Element Tearing and Interconnecting Method for Electro-Acoustic Modeling of Acoustic-Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: High-performance filters based on acoustic resonators have been used extensively in modern communication systems because of their capabilities to meet stringent specifications for steep skirts, wide bandwidths, low insertion losses, high out-of-band suppression, and small sizes. For an efficient design of such filters, it is critical to have an accurate and fast numerical modeling that could capture important characteristics such as wave guiding, spurious transversal modes, and acoustic radiation. Unfortunately, such a numerical modeling is very challenging because the electro-acoustic phenomenon involved represents a large and multi-scale computational problem. Although the finite element method (FEM) is well suited to modeling such a multiscale electro-acoustic problem, the simulation can be very time-consuming because a large number of degrees-of-freedom (DOFs) is required to obtain a high accuracy for practical design. An effective technique to tackle this problem is to employ an effective domain decomposition technique such as the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) method. With the FETI method, we first decompose the computational domain of an acoustic-wave resonator to be simulated into many nonoverlapping subdomains that can be handled with an efficient direct sparse solver. We then enforce transmission conditions (TCs) at subdomain interfaces to couple adjacent subdomains to formulate a global interface system. We finally solve this global interface problem using an iterative method to obtain the solution at the subdomain interfaces, from which we can compute the solution in each subdomain. Although FETI has been extensively studied for a variety of electromagnetic and elastic problems, many technical difficulties have been encountered in the electro-acoustic modeling of acoustic-wave resonators. For example, due to the electromechanical coupling and anisotropic properties of piezoelectric materials, the resulting global interface system in FETI is found to be ill-conditioned, and the convergence of iterative solutions even with a robust Krylov subspace method is slow. To alleviate this issue, we developed two approaches based on the construction of a higher-order TC and design of an effective preconditioner to accelerate the rate of convergence. In this presentation, we will discuss some of the technical issues we have encountered and the solutions we have explored and demonstrate the improved performance of the resulting FETI modeling.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conducted Emission EM Noise in High Voltage Power Conversion Systems for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The high-voltage power conversion device serves as an integral component in the propulsion systems of electric vehicles (EVs), a relevance amplified by the expanding adoption of EVs. Among various power conversion systems deployed in EVs, the foundational direct current to direct current (DC-DC) converter is instrumental in supplying the requisite voltage to diverse components from a high-voltage power source. This capability profoundly influences both charging efficiency and vehicular performance. Consequently, associated with electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise interactions among components, system stability, and safety considerations-particularly in relation to high-capacity batteries - have ascended in significance. To address these concerns, this paper conducts an in-depth analysis of the EMI noise characteristics in LLC Resonant DCDC converters across a range of various operational conditions [1].

articleTitle: A Multiplicative Calderón Preconditioner for the B-Spline-Based Electric Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present a multiplicative Calderón preconditioner for the electric field integral equation (EFIE) when discretized with B-spline-based basis functions, that is, the resulting formulation is free from the dense-discretization breakdown. We obtain the preconditioner by establishing a set of suitable dual basis functions, which can be explicitly expressed as a superposition of a refined discretization, as is known from the (low-order) Buffa-Christiansen (BC) functions. In contrast to the BC functions, our approach applies to arbitrary polynomial degrees of the basis functions for single- and multi-patch (curvilinear) descriptions of the geometry, which can be open or closed. Numerical results demonstrate the optimal nature of the derived preconditioner.

articleTitle: A dielectric waveguide solution for automotive high-speed communication - a potential extension to traditional signal transmission options?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The continuously and rapidly developing automotive sector is in the urgent need for high-speed interconnectivity solutions. Such solutions are required to provide 100 Gbps per lane in order to manage the vastly increasing data volume generated by sensors necessary, for instance, to facilitate automated or even autonomous driving. From Rosenberger’s perspective as a leading high-speed connectivity supplier for the automotive industry, dielectric waveguide technology is a candidate that potentially could outperform traditional copper and optical solutions in short distance applications below 15 m requiring large data bandwidth. In a nutshell, the multi-layered polymer waveguide is lightweight, robust against physical and chemical influences, and inexpensive while introducing galvanic isolation and a minimum of loss and dispersion. Thus, the transmission via a single polymer microwave fiber should be competitive to established multi-lane copper solutions, such as four IEEE Std 802.3cy™ ethernet connections, achieving 100 Gbps. The research efforts and research contributions in polymer waveguides at Rosenberger originate from academic collaborations and focus on the D-band frequency regime between 110 GHz to 170 GHz for more than a decade, readying the technology to meet the developing capabilities and requirements of integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Debris Plasma Density Perturbations as Seen Through a Modern Collective Thomson Scatter Radar Processing Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In January 2023 MIT’s LL and Haystack Observatory performed a joint experiment to understand possible signatures of space debris in the ionosphere, and we previously reported on signatures of the objects that were successfully identified. This work was initiated by the United States Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA) SINTRA program which is devoted to high-risk debris sensing research.

articleTitle: Design of Drude Metasurface Antennas for High-Band Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: With the increasing requirements for wireless communication systems, multiband antennas were put forward. However, there are serious blockages for a high-band (HB) antenna when a low-band (LB) antenna with the larger overall size is placed on the radiation direction of it (Fig. 1(a)), which hinders the development of multiband antennas. To address this challenge, various routes have been presented, including metasurface cloaks [1], choking methods [2], and bandpass frequency selective surface [3]. Most of them concentrated on the structural optimization. Here, from the perspective of dispersion engineering of homogeneous materials, a novel methodology utilizing the Drude metasurfaces to design high-band compatibility antennas is proposed.

articleTitle: A Comparison of ECG and FMCW Radar Heart Beat Measurements Based on an Envelope Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Non-contact monitoring of vital signs is growing for the last few years. One of the advantages is that the patient will not be affected by an attached sensors. The white coat hypertension is one further reason. The latter can lead to higher heart frequency by a consultation as when the patient measures it at home. Non-contact vital signs monitoring at the patient’s home can reduce this affect which leads to better diagnoses. In this publication, a new signal processing method for heart beat extraction out of radar measurements based on a dedicated vital sign FMCW radar is shown. The results will be compared with an ECG (GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Monitor B650). The pronounced radar system hardware consist of three separated modules: a 2 TX x 4RX MIMO radar front-end, a filtering-amplification module and a data acquisition module for the data transfer. All parts are developed in the laboratory of applied radar- and optical systems (LaROS) at the Trier University of Applied Sciences. The presented signal processing is optimized for the presented radar topology and the frequency range of the 24 GHz ISM band and is based onto a signal envelope analysis.

articleTitle: Magnetosphere-relevant wave research at Caltech involving or motivated by lab experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Laboratory experiments at Caltech use pulsed power methods to produce plasmas that replicate both solar corona loops and astrophysical jets. The solar loop and jet experiments use similar technology and diagnostics but differ in the symmetry of the boundary conditions. Both types of plasmas evolve through a reproducible sequence starting with MHD-driven flows and expansion, followed by MHD instabilities, and then coupling of the MHD instabilities to non-MHD phenomena instigating various non-MHD waves and also extreme electron energization. The MHD flows are driven either directly by $\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}$ forces or else indirectly by $\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}$ forces creating a pressure gradient that then drives flows. The instabilities are kink, sausage, or Rayleigh-Taylor and in some cases are Rayleigh-Taylor instigated by the effective gravity produced by a kink. Typically, the MHD instabilities cause a thinning of the current channel causing the current density to increase. The current density has to increase because the large inductance of the circuit causes the system to behave as a constant-current system. A technique [1] for measuring the $\mathbf{k}$-vector of waves for which displacement current can be ignored has been developed and used in the lab [2] and also for the MMS spacecraft [3]. The class of waves where displacement current can be ignored includes Alfven and whistler waves. The technique measured a whistler wave excited at a magnetic reconnection location and since $\mathbf{k}=\mathbf{k}(\omega)$ the whistler dispersion was identified by this dependence [2]. A separate model concerns the Doppler-shifted cyclotron resonance of relativistic electrons; namely the situation where $\omega-\mathrm{kv}_{\mathrm{par}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{c}} / \gamma$. By using relativistic transformations of both the fields and dynamics to the wave frame it is found that the energy an electron gains from ‘resonance’ tends to knock the electron out of resonance with the net result that the electron bounces in and out of resonance. This process has been shown [4] to map exactly to that of a pseudo-particle trapped in a pseudo-potential well where the pseudo-kinetic energy is given by the square of the acceleration as measured in the wave frame and the pseudo-potential is a function of $\mathrm{v}_{\text {par }}$. Curious features are that the shape of the pseudo-potential is governed by initial conditions and that maximum pitch angle scattering comes from electrons that do not start at exact resonance. For certain initial conditions the pseudo-potential shape has a two-valley structure which results in a very large pitch angle scattering. This can be the dominant contributor to pitch angle scattering [5] and results from the extent of the $\mathrm{V}_{\text {par }}$ oscillation (analog to position oscillation of a normal harmonic oscillator) being approximately double that of a one-valley structure.

articleTitle: High-Performance Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Resonant Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In electromagnetic (EM) cavities, the resonant frequencies and cavity eigenmodes play an important role in understanding and analyzing the properties of cavity EM fields. This research aims to investigate a high-performance time-domain (TD) numerical method for analyzing EM resonant frequencies and their associated eigenmodes in cavities. Compared to frequency-domain (FD) solvers, the TD simulation is a natural candidate for understanding the broadband analysis of complex cavity enclosures. Nevertheless, due to the high Q-factor of the cavity, it takes a very long time for the EM energy to decay after being coupled into the cavity. Moreover, for large cavities with closely spaced resonances, an even longer simulation is required to resolve nearby resonance peaks.

articleTitle: Propagation of Higher-Order Waveguide Modes from the OMT into the Far Field
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of a circularly symmetric Q-band (30- 58 GHz) feed horn with a turnstile orthomode transducer (OMT) is analyzed using electromagnetic simulation to quantify the activation of higher order modes in the waveguide that connects these two components of the feed assembly. The effect of these higher order modes on the far-field beam pattern is demonstrated, as propagated through MeerKAT offset-Gregorian reflector optics. This investigation follows from a study that found that a dipole OMT with asymmetric balun design unexpectedly activated higher order waveguide modes in the L-band (856-1712 MHz) which propagate into the far field for the same reflector geometry. In that case a fundamental mode analysis proved to be ineffective at explaining the measured far-field beam patterns in the upper half of the operating range. There is a high degree of symmetry in the Q-band design studied in this paper, and this work determines that the higher order mode activation is approximately -20 dB lower than reported for the L-band dipole OMT design. The effect of introducing deliberate asymmetry into the turnstile OMT design is also analyzed to assess how a small manufacturing error could change the outlook. The proposed analysis method is computationally attractive for evaluating the effect of several adjustments to the design of the OMT on the far-field patterns.

articleTitle: Coherent Reflectometry from Space: Sensitivity to Sea-Surface Height and Atmospheric Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper summarizes example results of an ongoing study that focuses on coherent reflectometry data recorded by dedicated GNSS receivers on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites. The main goal of the study is to assess the overall sensitivity of coherent reflectometry data to changes in sea-surface height and to assess the impact of atmospheric disturbances on respective height retrievals (altimetry). The given example tracks are located in the Caribbean and have grazing incidence with about 15° of elevation angles at the specular point. The results show, in agreement with previous findings, that phase and Doppler residuals derived from the satellite data are sensitive to sea-surface height changes and therefore relevant for altimetry. Apart from the altimetric sensitivity we found further anomalies in the residual Doppler. The standard deviation of Doppler after altimetric correction shows highest values for the track with local time in the evening. We suppose an impact of ionospheric plasma instabilities that are frequent in evening hours at low latitudes. We will extend the analysis for further validation.

articleTitle: Antenna Characterization by the Back-Scattering Measurement Method Using the Integrated RF-Frontend as Load Modulation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of characterizing an antenna over-the-air by measuring its back-scattered field while modulating this field using the integrated RF-frontend which acts as a variable antenna load. This eliminates the requirement for implementing dedicated load switching circuitry commonly utilized for this purpose. Numerical results are presented for a 100 GHz on-chip antenna and for two example frontends: (i) a Tx frontend employing only a power amplifier, and; (ii) a transceiver frontend employing a Tx/Rx switch, a power amplifier and a low-noise amplifier. Using the proposed procedure with both frontends, the input reflection coefficient of the Device Under Test is recovered with a relative numerical error of less than $10^{-11}$. Also, the procedure for estimating the realized gain demonstrates a relative error of less than 5%, primarily attributed to the accuracy of the electromagnetic simulation model. Furthermore, the impact of measurement uncertainties is analyzed.

articleTitle: PT-Symmetric Metasurfaces and Their Beamshaping and Beamfomring Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Antennas with directive radiation have been studied for decades because of their widespread applications in radar, communication, and imaging. Leaky-wave antennas exploiting (fast) leaky wave to form a directive radiation pattern are generally based on passive waveguides and transmission lines with periodically arranged small apertures [1]–[5]. Very recently, leaky waves excited in metamaterial structures, such as the ε-near-zero (ENZ) artificial medium, have been proposed to make compact antennas with enhanced frequency agility and directivity [5]. However, there are still several limitations associated with the fabrication complexity of bulky metamaterials and the resonant absorption in the ENZ band.

articleTitle: Experimental exploration for precursor solitons in a flowing plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Over the past decade, theoretical studies by Sen et al.
