[1] have proposed that when charged object moves through a plasma at a speed larger than the ion acoustic speed, it generates ion acoustic solitons. The solitons are excited in front of the moving object and propagate faster than the object. This novel effect has possible application in tracking small sized space debris in the Earth’s ionosphere. To explore this application, Truitt and Hartzell [2] investigated the excitation of precursor soliton for the plasma conditions expected in low Earth orbit (LEO), i.e. 200-1000 Km. The first experimental demonstration of the generation of a precursor soliton in a flowing dusty plasma over a charged object was reported by Jaiswal et al. [3]. Recently, Kumar et al. [4] demonstrated the excitation of two and three-dimensional precursor solitons in a flowing dusty plasma. In this work, we report experimental studies looking for precursor solitons in a flowing plasma. The experiments are performed in the Space Plasma Simulation Chamber (SPSC) at the Naval Research Laboratory (NRL). A series of biased rings placed at the end of the SPSC are used to create a radial electric field along with an applied axial magnetic field resulting in an azimuthal plasma flow. The inferred flow speed (based assuming the driven flow is the E x B speed) changes from a subsonic to a supersonic value by different combinations of radial electric fields and axial magnetic fields. A debris object is placed in the chamber such that plasma flows past over it. The debris is biased with a square voltage pulse.

articleTitle: A Multibeam Antenna Array Fed by a New Design of RF Beamforming Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Space-based communication is becoming increasingly important in the current 5G landscape and the imminent arrival of the 6G mobile communication systems, which requires beams of antenna arrays to cover different directions to ensure high communications quality. To this end, the analog beamforming network (BFN) that can generate multiple beams simultaneously has attracted widespread attention and research. Traditional BFNs, such as Blass matrices, Butler matrices and Nolen matrices, were thoroughly studied and widely used in many applications. However, beams in these BFNs are dependent to each other, i.e., when one beams changes, other beams will be affected, which is a major drawback. To achieve flexible control of each beam, a new structure of BFN known as generalized joined coupler (GJC) Matrix was proposed [1]–[2]. Different from traditional BFNs, the GJC matrix can realize simultaneously and independently beam steering by changing the values of phase shifters within the network.

articleTitle: Optimization of electrical conductivity of multilayer additively manufactured microwave components on polymer substrate by Laser sintering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this contribution, a method for laser sintering of metal traces printed by additive manufacturing (controlled micro-extrusion) with nScrypt technology is investigated. Preliminary tests were conducted to identify a laser source compatible with the selected metallic deposits on a Poly-etherketone-ketone (PEKK) polymer substrate. These tests led to an enhancement in the direct current (DC) conductivity of the printed metallic squares, reaching up to 12.7% of the bulk conductivity of silver. This improvement was achieved within a shorter sintering time compared to conventional oven thermal treatment (17 hours). Subsequently, multilayer planar resonators were fabricated to compare microwave performance with and without laser sintering, showing a 26% improvement in quality factor.

articleTitle: Classical and Quantum Computational Electromagnetics: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Classical and quantum computational electromagnetics (CEM) are important for the development of new technologies. For instance, classical CEM, together with circuit theory, are responsible for over 90 percent of the design of modern computer chips. The knowledge base for classical CEM has been developed since the 1960’s. On the other hand, the knowledge base for quantum CEM is less mature and less richly endowed compared to classical CEM. We will review the past achievements in classical CEM, recent achievements in classical CEM, and quantum CEM.

articleTitle: Statistical Estimates of Intentional Electromagnetic Interference in Unshielded Twisted-Wire Pairs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A recently developed worst-case/statistical approach to assessment of radiated intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) in general multiport systems is here applied to the special case of an unshielded twisted-wire pair (TWP). Worst-case analysis overcomes lack of knowledge on the waveform of the electromagnetic pulse, while statistics take into account the random incidence and polarization angle of the impinging plane wave, as well as non-uniformity of wire twisting. The worst-case peak of the induced-voltage waveform and the worst-case dissipated energy in TWP terminal loads are characterized through cumulative distribution functions. Significant properties are inferred with reference to common-mode and differential-mode quantities.

articleTitle: On a Novel Pivoting Strategy for the Nested Cross Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Surface integral equations are a popular choice for solving electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems. Standard discretizations via the boundary element method, however, lead to dense system matrices. Therefore, in practice, so-called fast methods are used to reduce the complexity in terms of CPU time and memory consumption for the construction of the compressed system matrix as well as the cost for a single matrix-vector product. For electrically small problems, the adaptive cross approximation of H-matrices [1] is a popular choice due to its purely algebraic nature, resulting in quasi-linear complexity with respect to the number of unknowns. The complexity can be reduced to linear by introducing a nested dependency of the low-rank blocks between the levels of the tree-structure, resulting in an H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix.

articleTitle: 18-32.3 GHz Cryogenic Front-End for 40 m Yebes Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The 40-meter radio telescope, as a single-dish instrument, is primarily dedicated to the investigation of the galactic interstellar medium through rotational molecular spectroscopy observations [1]. On the other hand, the 40-meter RT also operates as a Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) instrument [2]. These findings, and the possibility to study the spectrum of different astrophysical media with unprecedented sensitivity [3], are built upon the utilization of an advanced K-Q-W receivers’ configuration, which was installed in 2019. The proposed configuration offered several notable enhancements, including a nearly 40% instantaneous bandwidth in the Q band, the addition of a new W band receiver, an upgraded optical system enabling simultaneous observations and the incorporation of a calibration load featuring a nearly black-body emitter at hot and cold temperatures [3] [4].

articleTitle: Simple Randomized Cur Algorithms for Method of Moments Matrix Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Method of Moments (MoM) discretization of electromagnetic scattering problems modeled with Integral Equations [1] results in systems of equations with a vast number of unknowns, demanding significant computational resources. Over the past three decades, substantial research has produced highly efficient algorithms [2], termed “Fast Solvers”, with reduced storage requirements and computational complexity, enabling iterative solutions on personal computers with millions of unknowns and even billions on supercomputers.

articleTitle: Simulations of nonlinear plasma structures generated by charged orbital debris
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Orbital debris and meteoroids immersed in space plasma obtain an electric charge, enabling them to electromagnetically interact with the ambient environment. Beyond the well-characterized linear response, charged objects can also produce nonlinear responses in the form of coherent plasma structures. These structures include solitons, shocks, and vortices, and might be detectable in situ or remotely. Understanding the physics anthropogenic plasma signatures could enable us to sense, characterize, and track debris.

articleTitle: An approach to discretize one-dimensional equivalent radiating panels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We deal with the problem of the discretization of a 1D radiating panel. After carrying out the dimensioning of the panel, a practical implementation can be provided by a non-uniform array. In the proposed approach, the array element positioning is performed by exploiting a quadrature rule which takes into account that the singular functions supported on the region of interest associated to the most significant singular values of the radiation operator are related to those supported on the equivalent panel by a radiation integral. The quadrature rule enables also to choose a set of weights which are essential in the definition of the excitation coefficients of the array elements. The performance of the approach is assessed numerically.

articleTitle: Impact of Magnetic Traction on Drive Vibration Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Examining the operational parameters of electric drives and diverse electrical equipment regarding reliability and longevity of bearing units reveals that wear or deviations in linear dimensions and geometric conformity of the bearing seats from regulatory standards result in a disturbance of the harmonized configuration of electric motor components, particularly their rotors.

articleTitle: SMD Coincident Antenna Array for 2D Field Acquisition and Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Field acquisition and reconstruction by means of (near-)coincident arrays is quite consolidated in acoustics. Techniques such as Mid-Side, XY and Ambisonics, supported by algorithms for signal processing, paved the way to 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional sound recording and field synthesis, by placing microphones very close to each other in a single spot. On the other hand, the use of antenna coincident arrays for electromagnetic field acquisition is quite rare. This article proposes a preliminary study on the feasibility of coincident antenna arrays by means of surface mounted miniature chip antennas and the application of a 2-dimensional field acquisition technique such as Mid-Side to electromagnetism.

articleTitle: Enhanced Chipless RFID Detection Algorithm for Dense Multipath Channels based on Calibration Equalization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Main objective of this paper is to introduce an enhanced detection algorithm for Frequency Coded (FC) Chipless RFID tags within dense multipath channels based on Calibration Equalization Techniques (CET). In real-world multipath channels, few resolvable paths between the transmitter and the receiver of the reader are hitting the chipless RFID tag or the frequency selective surface, while many other paths are directly linked between the transmitter and the receiver without passing the tag and unfortunately those have in most cases the major contribution of the received power as illustrated in equation 1

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband 1-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Design for 26 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel wideband 1-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) design to operate at 26 GHz. The unit-cell, with the compact dimensions of $4.2 \times 4.2 \mathrm{~mm}$, features a hexagon-shaped patch on the top layer and a corresponding full ground plane on the bottom layer. The integration of two pin diodes allows precise control of the unit-cell phase, facilitating operation within the frequency range of 23.8 GHz to 31.1 GHz, with a targeted phase difference of $180^{\circ} \pm 10^{\circ}$ between states. Furthermore, a $10 \times 10$ RIS is design and studied, recurring to CST-MWS full-wave electromagnetic simulation tool. This larger structure maintains the compact design philosophy of the individual unit-cell while achieving noteworthy results. With an aperture efficiency $(\eta)$ surpassing $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$, the $\mathbf{1 0} \times 10$ RIS proves its effectiveness in optimising signal transmission and reception. Moreover, it exhibits a remarkable scanning capability, achieving a scanning angle of ±50° in both

articleTitle: Electronic Material Test Approaches for Natural and Stimulated Emissions in the Ionosphere and Magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Air Force Office of Scientific Research’s (AFOSR) mission is strengthening science to enhance longer-term capabilities of the United States Air and Space Forces. AFOSR funds higher-risk basic science primarily at universities. The Ionosphere (located $\sim 80-600 \mathrm{~km}$) and Magnetosphere (located $\sim 800-1000 \mathrm{~km}$) region’s natural and stimulated emissions affect material function. Imprecise environment and emission related material degradation mechanism understanding causes material system design specifications to exceed predicted need to assure performance. Single event effect failure in microelectronics highlight’s the challenges of operating within these zones [1]. Opportunities to enhance material function include identifying and quantifying non-linear combinations of environmental factors, including atomic oxygen exposure, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation, ultra-high vacuum effects, thermal cycling, and electrostatic influences. Extending theory to include new modes of magnetic, electronic, excitonic, photonic interactions with second-order material effects; using non-traditional materials in the space environment such as lanthanide-containing 2D MXenes combined with other 2D materials; innovating bio-inspired nanoscale sensing of electromagnetic fields, thermal environment, and magnetization using metal-insulator transition in complex oxides; and the exploitation of physics governing excitons (bound electron-hole pairs) are potential approaches to expanding viable materials systems and analysis fidelity.

articleTitle: Extended Fluid Simulations of Precursor Ion Acoustic Solitons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The topic of precursor nonlinear structures (solitons) excited by a charged object traveling through a plasma has attracted much recent attention due to its potential application in the detection and tracking of small sized space debris objects. The basic principle of such excitations in a plasma medium was expounded in a simple one dimensional fluid model calculation [1] leading to a paradigmatic nonlinear partial differential equation, the forced Korteweg de Vries (fKdV) equation, that yielded a variety of driven nonlinear solutions in the form of precursor solitons, “pinned” solitons, wakes and dispersive shocks. The scale sizes and amplitudes of these nonlinear structures for ionospheric conditions are within the detection capabilities of ground based radars or in-situ sensors. Hence they can provide an indirect means of detecting debris objects. Subsequent studies have established the existence of such solitons in a variety of theoretical models [2, 3] as well as in laboratory experiments in a dusty plasma medium [4], While the basic qualitative features of this novel phenomenon are similar to those appearing in analogous hydrodynamic excitations, there are important physical differences arising from plasma effects that are not well explored yet. In particular, the complex dynamics of the plasma sheath region surrounding the moving charged object that is responsible for the creation of the soliton needs to be better understood. In the present study we address this issue with the help of detailed fluid simulations of the sheath and presheath regions in front of the moving charged object. We investigate the evolution of driven nonlinear ion acoustic waves through numerical investigations of the full set of two fluid equations that go beyond the usual weak nonlinearity approximation of the fKdV or forced Kadomtsev-Petviashvilli (fKP) equations. The simulations are done for both planar and cylindrical objects in plasma conditions specific to the LEO and GEO regions of the ionosphere that are heavily populated by orbital debris. Realistic charging models are used to establish the surface potential and charge on the moving object and stochastic fluctuations of the charge are taken into account. The threshold condition for the excitation of the solitons is explored as a function of the ratio of the object speed to the ion thermal speed, the surface charge of the object, the shape of the object and the sheath parameters in order to identify the physical origins of the “pinned” and precursor solitons. It is found that the presheath region plays a dominant role in the excitation of the solitons and its dynamics needs to be investigated in greater depth. This can be done using a kinetic approach or particle-in-cell simulations both of which can benefit from the basic findings of the present extended fluid simulations.

articleTitle: Development of the ambipolar electric field in a compressed current sheet with and without a guide field
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Current sheets are important to space and laboratory plasmas, and particularly to the Earth’s magnetotail, where during active periods the solar wind compresses the magnetosphere creating thin current sheets. As a current sheet with a reversed magnetic field configuration is compressed, magnetic reconnection can occur. This process can affect the plasma state of the magnetotail, driving space weather and injecting energetic particles into the radiation belts, which impacts Earth orbiting satellites.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf method in problems of plane wave diffraction by two opposite staggered perfectly conducting half-planes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Diffraction of a plane wave on two opposite staggered perfectly conducting half-planes is considered using the Wiener-Hopf method. The Neumann boundary value problem is reduced to solving a system of Fredholm integral equations of the second kind, the solution to which is expressed analytically through the integral operator in the form of the sum of the Neumann series.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Beam-Switching Dielectric Resonator Antenna with an Integrated Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A fully 3D-printed dual-port dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented. It employs an integrated polarizer to obtain right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) over $\theta= \pm 45^{\circ}$. The isolation is better than 30 dB by introducing a 3D-printed vertical metallic reflector, of width 1 mm, between the excitation ports. The proposed antenna has applications in satellite IoT (S-IoT) as well as 5G/6G beam-switching MIMO areas. The antenna operates in the S-band $(2 \mathrm{GHz}$ to 3 GHz). A 10 dB bandwidth of $61 \%$ was achieved in the range 1.72 GHz to 3.22 GHz. The peak gain at 45° was found to be 6.7 dBic with an axial ratio bandwidth of $51.76 \%$ (1.79 GHz to 3.04 GHz).

articleTitle: Enhancing Pavement Integrity Assessment: The Role of Ultra-Wideband Horn Antennas in Ground Penetrating Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This study explores the use of ultra-wideband TEM horn antennas for non-destructive Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) evaluation of road pavements. By integrating antennas tuned to 2.7 GHz within the regulatory spectrum, we demonstrate enhanced resolution and penetration in pavement assessments. Employing CST Microwave Studio for simulations and applying empirical models for material properties, we reveal how GPR can effectively identify subsurface defects. Results from Fast Fourier Transform analyses on signal interactions with and without pavement irregularities underline the antennas’ diagnostic precision, offering a promising direction for preventive road infrastructure maintenance.

articleTitle: Integro-differential equations in the problem of electromagnetic wave scattering on a dielectric body covered with graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We consider the determination of resonance frequencies of dielectric bodies coated with graphene. In the addressed problem statement, the graphene nonlinearity is not taken into account. The initial boundary-value problem for Maxwell’s equations is reduced to a system of integro-differential equations on the graphene surface. We prove the Fredholm property of this system under certain sufficient conditions and establish the discreteness of the spectrum of an operator-valued function corresponding to this system in a certain region of the complex plane of the circular frequency spectral parameter.

articleTitle: A Compact W-Band TE10-TE01 Mode Converter for Industrial Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Today, radar-based sensors are widely used in various industrial applications. Apart from standard distance and velocity measurements, further radar-based analytical measurements came into focus in recent years. Typically, radars excite the fundamental TE10- or TE11-mode using rectangular waveguides or circular waveguides, respectively. Depending on the application and the chosen dimension of the waveguides, higher order modes must be considered with various impacts on the measurement accuracy. Especially for large distances in pipes or in small vessels underlying strong movements in contrast, the TE01 mode is advantageous and gathers more and more relevance in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Assessment of a Microwave Imaging Technique for Pediatric Stroke Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Stroke is a widespread disease that may cause permanent damage and, in the worst cases, be fatal also in pediatric and adolescent patients. Timely and adequate treatments play a fundamental role since radically different therapies are required for ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes, and a misdiagnosis can cause further damage. In this scenario, microwave imaging is emerging as a powerful tool for non-invasive diagnostics [1]. However, it requires the solution of a problem that is inherently non-linear and ill-posed. Consequently, ad-hoc inversion schemes are usually necessary, especially when a quantitative retrieval of the dielectric properties is required.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Metasurface Structure with the Aid of Bottom-Up Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a design methodology leading to optimize an electromagnetic metasurface structure usable in a wide band frequency. The structure consists of identical unit cells realized in microstrip technology, being one of them fed by a coaxial cable. The employed approach is the bottomup optimization (BUO) that is implemented by increasing the number of radiators following a squared scheme of $n \times n$ nature. The proposed methodology leads to design optimal complex structures exhibiting a wideband feature. For validating the use of BUO method, the number of radiators has been increased from 1 to 25, i.e., n has been varied form $n=1$, to $n=5$. The initial design parameters of antennas are obtained through particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The simulation results show that the optimized metasurface with the aid of BUO method has a wideband frequency answer in the range from 13 GHz to 22.66 GHz.

articleTitle: Considerations for modifying collective Thomson scattering forward models to accommodate small scale orbital debris
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The technique of collective Thomson scatter (also known as incoherent scatter) has been a mainstay of the ionospheric remote sensing community for several decades, as it uniquely provides full altitude profiles of the ionospheric state, including plasma temperatures and composition. The forward model necessary to analyze observed spectra from large aperture, high power radar systems was developed beginning in the late 1950s, with the ability to sample altitude dependent changes stemming from the very weak nature of the scatter which well satisfies the Born approximation. A number of parallel approaches have been developed for the forward model, including a Nyquist fluctuation-dissipation theorem based framework (e.g. [1]), statistical dressed particle approaches [2], and equivalent parallel circuit models [3] in which the source currents are generated by thermal motions of the electrons and ions in the plasma and complex impedances are presented by each species which must obey electrostatic forcing from a common electric field.

articleTitle: Plasma Instabilities Driven by Electron and Proton Ring Distributions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The charged particles trapped in the planetary magnetospheres are characterized by a loss-cone feature. The perpendicular ring velocity distribution function is an ideal form of loss-cone distribution. The electrons and ions featuring the ring velocity distribution functions are unstable to a number of plasma instabilities, including the quasi-parallel cyclotron instabilities and quasi-perpendicular or obliquely-propagating multiple-harmonic cyclotron instabilities. For the electron instabilities, the multiple-harmonic, or Bernstein mode instabilities with typically peak wave intensities in the vicinity of the upper-hybrid frequency, are well known, and excitation of such instabilities are observed by artificial satellites. For the protons featuring a perpendicular ring distribution, it is also well known that these are associated with the excitation of multiple-harmonic magnetosonic modes. The present paper overviews the linear and quasilinear theories of these ring-driven instabilities, and validation of the quasilinear analysis by particle-in-cell or hybrid-code simulation will be discussed.

articleTitle: Plasma Physics at Comets – What can we learn from laboratory experiments?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Diamagnetic cavities at comets were predicted already in the 1960s [1], and then observed at comet 1P/Halley by the ESA/Giotto spacecraft in 1986 [2]. Recently, the ESA/Rosetta spacecraft spent two years orbiting comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and encountered the diamagnetic cavity of comet 67P more than 700 times [3, 4]. Most encounters lasted a few minutes, with the duration varying from a few seconds up to more than 30 minutes. As the spacecraft moved very slowly (~1ms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>), it can be considered stationary with respect to the plasma. Therefore, the quick succession of detections indicates that the boundary of the diamagnetic cavity moved over the spacecraft. Figure 1 (left) shows three diamagnetic cavity signatures observed with the plasma instruments on Rosetta on 16 September 2015 when the comet was close to perihelion. Rosetta was in the diamagnetic cavity during the periods of nearly zero magnetic field (marked by the coloured regions). Outside the cavity. the plasma was often characterised by a series of asymmetric. steepened waves which are visible in the magnetic field. as well as in the plasma density [5]. Since all observations to date have been made using a single spacecraft. the shape of the diamagnetic cavity boundary cannot be well constrained by measurements. However. it has been suggested. based on wave observations. that bulges on the cavity boundary move past the spacecraft. causing the latter to quickly move in and out of the cavity [6].

articleTitle: High-Gain and Broadband Microstrip Antenna using Triple-Slotted Mechanism for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article, a compact high-gain and broadband antenna, resonating at 24.10 GHz and 26.10 GHz, is discussed for millimeter-wave power transfer and energy harvesting applications. The proposed antenna geometry is very simple, consisting of a rectangular patch incorporated with triple-slots on the rectangular radiating surface. By doing so, higher gain values $(9.14 \mathrm{dBi}$ and 8.05 dBi) and a broader bandwidth of 3.81 GHz are achieved. Also, the radiation pattern is found to be stable and unidirectional. A 50-$\Omega$ microstrip line is used to excite the proposed antenna and designed on the Rogers RT Duroid 4003TM substrate (relative permittivity $= 3.38$, thickness $=0.508 \mathrm{~mm}$, and loss tangent $=0.0021$). The antenna has an overall compact size of $6 \times 12.4 \times 0.8 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ satisfying the requirements of a compact millimeter-wave communication system.

articleTitle: First Results from the LIEFSI Campaign
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electric field double probes are used on many satellite missions to provide high quality in-situ AC and DC electric field measurements. To achieve this accuracy the electric field instrument components and the surrounding surfaces have voltage and current biases applied to them, which mitigate errors due to factors such as the photoelectric effect and stray currents in the system. These corrections help to produce measurements that are vital for understanding the complex processes that occur in the wide range of plasma environments these satellites orbit through.

articleTitle: Sheared ExB Stirring and Cross-Field Electron Inertial Length Structuring Generated by Shear Alfvén Wave Heating
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Alfvén waves play many important roles in the interaction of the Earth’s magnetosphere and ionosphere. In one significant example, shear Alfvén waves triggered by reconnection in the magnetotail carry energy along field lines mapping back to the auroral ionosphere; there, where the electron thermal speed is small compared to the Alfvén speed, electron inertial effects are important, and these Inertial Alfven Waves (IAWs) possess a parallel electric field which accelerates electrons. In some cases, the incoming IAW Poynting flux is sufficient to completely power the aurora [1]. Measurements of the electron acceleration process have even been recently performed in a laboratory plasma [2]. Bulk heating of electrons can also occur by IAWs when electron-ion Coulomb collisions become important in the lower ionosphere. The cross-field density of the ionospheric plasma has been found to contain a great deal of structure, including density cavities. Some of these cavities are co-located with IAWs and measurements by the FAST satellite [3] show that the waves can create the cavities. We present results of an investigation aimed at complementing the understanding of such phenomena from a parameter-scaled, laboratory experiment. Our results demonstrate that, among other effects, sheared cross-field ExB flows can restructure any existing plasma nonuniformities into what appear to be electron-inertial length scale wavelike features, as well as generate expanding, cross-field diffusion waves.

articleTitle: ESA Scout HydroGNSS: A Satellite Mission using GNSS Reflections to Monitor Hydrological Climate Variables
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: HydroGNSS is a small satellite mission under the ESA Scout Programme tapping into NewSpace, as part of ESA’s FutureEO Programme, within a budget of €30M and a schedule of three years from mission kick-off to launch. The mission comprises two satellites using an innovative GNSS-Reflectometry instrument to collect parameters related to the Essential Climate Variables (ECVs): soil moisture, inundation, freeze/thaw, biomass, ocean wind speed and sea ice extent. GNSS-Reflectometry is a type of bistatic radar that uses multiple broadcast signals of opportunity from GNSS satellites, empowering small satellites to provide measurement quality associated with radar satellites [1].

articleTitle: Accurate Analysis of the High-Frequency Near-Field Arising as a Result of Plane Wave Diffraction on an Open Metallic Spherical Shell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this communication we revisit the rigorous solution of the plane wave diffraction from the open perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) spherical shell. The history of this long-standing problem and its solution may be found in [1]. The power of the Method of Analytical Regularization (MAR), employed in obtaining the solution, has been demonstrated for this problem in numerous publications. In particular, the complex eigenvalues of the TE-modes of the PEC spherical shell with a single circular aperture are presented in [2].

articleTitle: Results of Synthesis of an Isotropic Reactance Structure From Given Amplitude and Phase Scattering Diagrams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: a two-dimensional problem of synthesizing an inhomogeneous isotropic reactance plane from given multi-beam amplitude and phase scattering diagrams, on the surface of which several homogeneous plane waves are fall, was solved. The phase relationships between the incident waves can change according to arbitrarily specified laws. The laws of distribution of the synthesized reactance are obtained in an explicit form. The results of calculations of the implemented scattering diagrams for various laws of changes in phase relationships in reflected rays are presented. The analysis problem was obtained strictly using the method of integral equations.

articleTitle: “Advances in Microwave Filters based on Additive Manufacturing Technologies”
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: RF systems of new generation satellite networks and constellations are becoming more and more complex, thus requiring greater data capacity together with a higher density of RF equipment on board. The microwave filters located in new generation RF satellite systems should have low-loss and high-rejection, and they should be very compact and possibly as cheap as possible in mass production. In this scenario, the conventional manufacturing processes of filters based on milled waveguide cavities offer good performance, but are bulky and heavy.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing Folded Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A 3D printed folded reflectarray that uses fully dielectric resonator elements and a spherical polarizer realized with a metalized plastic structure is presented in this paper. To reduce the thickness of the reflecting surface, a 3D printable dielectric material with a high-value of the dielectric constant is used, while the spherical polarizer is exploited to enhance the reflectarray bandwidth compared to a flat configuration. Preliminary results show very good performance of the antenna, with a gain of about 28 dBi and an efficiency greater than 50% in the whole 1-dB bandwidth of 13.4%.

articleTitle: An Inflatable Electromagnetic Simulator Based on Low-Frequency-Compensated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Transient electromagnetic disturbance (TED) such as intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI), fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) and high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) can lead to radiated effects electrical and electronic systems. For large-scale equipment under test (EUT), guided-wave simulators, dipole simulators and hybrid simulators are usually applied [1–2], whereas most of them are ground-fixed. For large-scale EUT such as ultra-high-voltage transformers, it is necessary to develop a transportable simulator for the purpose of on-site TED experiments. An inflatable simulator based on low-frequency-compensated antenna is designed in this paper, which can be used to generate the radiated field of VFTO and HEMP.

articleTitle: Energetic Electron Generation During Electron-Only Reconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A regime of reconnection, called electron-only reconnection since there is insufficient time or space for ions to couple with reconnection structures, provides an opportunity to study electron heating mechanisms more directly than in fully ion-coupled reconnection. Electron-only reconnection is thought to be important for energy dissipation at kinetic scales in Earth’s turbulent magnetosheath, bow shock and the quiet magnetotail. Recent simulations of turbulent near-Sun plasmas suggest that electron-only reconnection with a large guide field plays a key role in the dissipation of turbulent energy at the kinetic scale and results in parallel, i.e. anisotropic, electron heating.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Frequency Selective Surface in Quartz for Transmitarray Applications at Sub-THz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel 1-bit dual-band unit-cell (UC), called Asymmetric Linear Polarizer (ALP) with potential applications in transmitarray (TA) systems operating at sub-THz frequencies. Drawing inspiration from frequency-selective surface (FSS)-based structures, the proposed UC demonstrates promising behaviors in terms of bandwidth and reduced transmission losses. TAs comprising 30×30 ALP UCs are designed using an in-house CAD tool and validated numerically using full-wave simulations. Maximum gain values of 25.8 dBi and 17.9 dBi, corresponding to aperture efficiencies of 25.9% and 22.4% are achieved at 300 GHz and 130 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Array Synthesis Using Spherical Wave Elements for EMF Compliance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Due to the advanced roll-out of 5G networks around the world, there has been an increase in public concern regarding radio frequency (RF) safety [1]. Accurate simulations are required to ensure that all mobile base stations are compliant in terms of reference limits, e.g. those published by ICNIRP [2]. These numerical simulations typically require knowledge of the antenna properties such as spherical (3D) gain, the applied power, electrical down tilt, as well as placement information. Simulation methods such as ray tracing, as described in the IEC 62232 standard [3], can be used to calculate compliance boundaries around these antennas. One of the challenges of applying this method is the formulation of the antenna array element patterns used in the exposure ratio calculation from which compliance zones are derived.

articleTitle: Numerically stable analytical computation of double surface integrals over almost parallel flat supports for time and frequency domain Galerkin discretization of wave scattering problems.
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this contribution, we consider recently proposed analytical methods for the exact evaluation of double surface integrals present in the Galerkin discretization of acoustic and electromagnetic scattering, in both frequency and time domain cases. Either in the frequency or time domain, it is possible to obtain a closed form of the double surface integrals of the impedance matrix. However, the result of this evaluation is affected by numerical instabilities for certain geometrical configurations of the integration domain. We analyze the cause of such instabilities. In particular, we focus on the case of almost parallel domains of integration and illustrate why it is necessary to take care of this configuration when dealing with large-scale problems. Although past works discussed this problem in the frequency domain, we show that time domain analytical methods require a detailed analysis for analogous configurations. We propose a strategy that allows to stabilize the calculation. The method is based on the analysis of the explicit dependence of the formula on the relative angle between the two domains of integration. It furnishes a stable result for small angles by avoiding the computation of differences between big numbers in the formula.

articleTitle: A fast multiplication algorithm for Gabor coefficients
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Optical scatterometry is a fast, non-destructive, and accurate technique for monitoring integrated circuits (ICs) for defects during their lithographic production process. The detection of these defects with potentially sub-wavelength size hinges on the accurate scattered electromagnetic fields as provided by a Maxwell solver. Generating this information typically induces a heavy computational workload. To this end, it is key to develop computationally efficient Maxwell solvers, to provide this information in a fast and accurate manner as a means to safeguard the production quality of ICs.

articleTitle: Investigating Frequency Dependency in Characteristic Basis Function Pattern Modelling with Geometric Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between three Characteristic Basis Function Pattern (CBFP) methods when reconstructing beams of multi-frequency antennas with geometric perturbations. The methods differ mainly in their handling of the frequency parameter. They are assessed by calculating the error of a reconstructed beam as a function of the number of basis functions used. Two examples of existing radio telescope antenna elements, substantially different in shape and function, are analyzed to evaluate each method: a REACH (Radio Experiment for the Analysis of Cosmic Hydrogen) dipole and a MeerKAT offset Gregorian dual-reflector antenna excited by a generic feed horn. It is shown that treating frequency as a normal parameter requires fewer geometric samples to reconstruct a beam to a certain degree of accuracy, compared to performing the CBFP expansion across geometry variation, either per frequency slice or by including all frequencies. The results indicate that some geometric perturbation information is captured in the frequency data.

articleTitle: Leaky-wave Analysis and Design of a Corrugated Sectoral Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A dispersive analysis of a fully metal corrugated sectoral waveguide is presented. This structure supports cylindrical mode and closed-form solutions are not available in literature due to the presence of the corrugations. The phase constant of the cylindrical mode is extracted by means of a full-wave calculation of the fields excited with a rectangular-waveguide feed. The sectoral waveguide is periodic modulated introducing concentric circular slots. Thus a periodic leaky-wave antenna is obtained. The radiated patterns validate the phase constant computed in the waveguide without slots.

articleTitle: Pyramidally Shaped Absorbing Boundary for FDTD Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Currently, the most popular absorbing boundary for a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation is the convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML) [1]. The CPML is a set of layers applied to the edge of the simulation domain where each layer is assigned electric and magnetic conductivities based on the layer depth and other equations to support theoretically minimum reflection for all frequencies and incident angles. However, the use of CPML in terminating the simulation domain increases the simulation time and memory requirements significantly in addition to the programming complexity.

articleTitle: HydroSwarm: towards fine resolution 2D imaging of surface water with GNSS-R flight formation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: It is recognised that GNSS reflectometry (GNSS-R) is uniquely suited to measuring flooding under clouds and under forest canopies because of the L-band and forward scatter nature of the measurements. GNSS-R picks out coherent reflections from flat surfaces at higher resolution than incoherent reflections from elsewhere. When a surface is sufficiently flat, such as inland water or flooded areas, the coherent reflections offer a resolution of sometimes better than 1 km. The drawback is that as the resolution increases, the track footprint becomes thinner, and only a cross-section of information about the surface is produced from each track. If a 2D map is required, the picture must be built up by multiple passes from multiple satellites.

articleTitle: Towards a Broadband-Stable Fast Method for the B-Spline Discretized Electric Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Scattering problems in electromagnetics have a multitude of applications, including, but not limited to, remote sensing and radar systems, electromagnetic compatibility, and antenna design. A natural way to address these problems in free space are integral equations such as the electric field integral equation (EFIE). The EFIE can be approximated by a linear system of equations using the boundary element method (BEM). Typically, in the first step, a mesh is created on the surface of the geometry. Currents on the mesh are approximated by a superposition of basis functions. This results in a geometric discretization error that can be prevented by utilizing exact parametric descriptions of the geometry surface. One commonly employed technique involves the use of non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS), where the surface is described by a union of patches. Basis functions are subsequently established using the same parametric representation by mapping them from a parametric space onto the patches [1]. This aligns well with common industrial design schemes that focus on computer-aided design (CAD) tools and integrates the design and simulation process. Existence and uniqueness of the solution of the BEM for the EFIE using a set of divergence-conforming basis functions have been established in [2].

articleTitle: Design of X-Band GaN Power Amplifier for SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is a imaging technique used to obtain high-resolution images by utilizing the principle of radar waves reflecting off surfaces. SAR designs operating at X -band frequencies are preferred for detailed and high-resolution imaging, as this frequency range allows radar waves to reflect smaller details from objects, resulting in more precise images. Power amplifier design is crucial in SAR applications because power amplifiers are used to amplify radar signals and cover wider areas. GaN transistors are preferred in power amplifier design for SAR applications due to their advantages such as high power, efficiency, frequency performance, durability, and high-temperature tolerance [1–4].

articleTitle: MEDUSE: 10 GHz localized quasi-planar wave measuring bench in order to analyse systems electromagnetic susceptibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper outlines the design of a focused plane-wave illumination bench for studying the electromagnetic susceptibility of electronic systems. The bench consists of a horn antenna and a dielectric lens used to focus plane wave in the X-band at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Millimetre-Wave Waveguide Passive Devices and Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: 3D printing (or additive manufacturing) has become an increasingly common manufacturing tool for microwave filters. The technology has made the jump from laboratories to real world applications and been used in real space missions. This relatively new manufacture technique has also started finding applications at even higher frequencies into millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) and sub-terahertz (sub-THz) regime [1], as ‘high-precision’ 3D printers become available. Without a consensus, but for the sake of clarity, here ‘high-precision’ printers are referred to those with a manufacture tolerance of under 10 μm over a sufficiently large printing volume of centimeter scales, to be generally usable for microwave and mm-wave waveguide devices.

articleTitle: Gradiometer-based Assessment of Magnetic Nanoparticles Quantification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) are gaining importance in the biomedical field because of their versatility for various applications, ranging from diagnostic contrast imaging to tumor ablation through hyperthermia [1]. Their nanoscale dimensions enable superparamagnetic effects, which are crucial for efficient manipulation under external magnetic fields. However, achieving functional and sensitive measurements of MNPs properties remains challenging. This study addresses this gap by employing a gradiometer approach employing MNPs suitable for biofunctionalization application and considering a no-shielded setup for in-vivo application.

articleTitle: Monostatic RCS in a large number of directions: Feasibility study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Full wave analysis of scatterers in the frequency domain can be effectively done by the Method of Moments (MoM) applied to the Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) [1, 2]. In this way, the electric and magnetic currents induced over the scatterer surfaces, are expanded in terms of N basis functions multiplied by unknown coefficients (unknowns), and the linear operator equations, SIEs, are transformed into a matrix equation with N unknowns.

articleTitle: A Review of Evaluations of Radar Cross-Section of Canonical and Complex Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electrical Engineering Department, Colorado School of Mines The phenomenon of target scattering and methods of computing the Radar cross-section (RCS) will be introduced briefly. Analytical expressions for RCS characteristics of canonical objects like spheres, cylinders and wedges are available. Approximate expressions for RCS of simple non canonical shapes like finite length cylinders, circular, rectangular, and triangular flat plates, and truncated cones (frustums) are also available. For more complex shaped targets like rockets and airplanes, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is efficiently used to compute their RCS characteristics. This presentation will provide numerical examples to show the salient RCS features of these targets and their combinations. Target’s RCS fluctuations due to aspect angle, frequency, and incident wave direction and polarization are investigated. An example of complex targets is the fighter plane shown below which is composed of perfectly conducting material for the body and dielectric material for the cockpit. Simulations for this fighter plane were conducted using the FDTD method on a single computer with two graphic processing units (GPU) in less than 4 minutes.

articleTitle: Towards Practical Implementation of Tri-ridged Orthomode Transducers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, two practical designs of tri-ridged orthogonal mode transducers are explored. These designs investigate the effect of including a well-matched central TEM port to help balance the system. The devices were designed to operate over a 3.6:1 bandwidth for a return loss of more than $20 \mathbf{d B}$. Full-wave simulation results confirm the theoretical result that the excitation ports of the system cannot be simultaneously matched and isolated without the matched central TEM port.

articleTitle: Use of 2nd Order Rao-Wilton-Glisson Basis Functions to Model Scattering by Strongly Nonlinear Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Nonlinear electromagnetic scattering problems [1] are becoming relevant with the discovery of novel devices pertaining to the advances in solid state physics. Electromagnetic scattering for a certain class of 2-D devices can be modeled by solving the Time-Domain Electric Field Integral Equation (TD-EFIE) and a nonlinear resistive boundary condition (RBC). An effective strategy to alleviate the challenges posed by nonlinearity is to utilize a fine enough mesh that can capture the nonlinear dynamics in the system with sufficient accuracy. Finer meshes have the obvious drawback of increasing computation time and memory cost. This work explores the application of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions in solving the Time-Domain Electric Field Integral Equation (TD-EFIE) in conjunction with a strongly nonlinear resistive boundary condition (RBC).

articleTitle: On the Theory of Resonant Interaction of Electromagnetic Waves with Periodically Modulated Dielectric Filling of a Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article the peculiarities of the propagation of a signal transverse electric (TE) wave in a waveguide with periodically modulated dielectric filling in the frequency region of “strong” (resonant) interaction between the signal wave and the modulation wave (the first-order Wulff-Bragg condition is satisfied between reflected from filling inhomogeneities harmonics) are investigated. It is assumed that the modulation depth of the waveguide filling is much less than unity. Calculations are carried out with an accuracy up to a small parameter to the first power. A physical explanation of the strong interaction effect is given. An analytical expression for the frequency of strong interaction was obtained in three ways. It is shown that the width of the frequency region of the strong interaction is small (it is proportional to the modulation depth). It is also shown that when the directions of propagation of the signal wave and the modulation wave coincide, a strong interaction occurs between the minus first and zero harmonics reflected from the filling inhomogeneities. In this case the amplitude at the minus first harmonic does not depend on the modulation depth, while at the plus first harmonic it depends on the modulation depth to the first power. When the above waves propagate in opposite directions the minus first and plus first harmonics change roles.

Author Keywords: periodically modulated filling of the waveguide

articleTitle: A Review of the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) in Applied Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) is a broadly used numerical technique, purposely designed for the solution of elliptic boundary value problems in Physics and Engineering, including Electromagnetics (EM). Superficially it resembles surface integral equation formulations, such as the Method of Moments (MoM), however it has been developed on different mathematical concepts. It was originally proposed by researchers in the former Soviet Union (currently Republic of Georgia) and was further refined at the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), Greece, through an efficient Greek-Georgian collaboration in the 1990’s. The fundamental concept of auxiliary sources, i.e. simulation of EM propagation behaviour in terms of fictitious, elementary fields has prompted several, unrelated scholars to develop practically the same, or very similar techniques, known in the literature by various names, e.g. “The Multifilament Current Model Method” or “The Discrete Singularity Method”. Furthermore, MAS is closely related to the “Generalized Multipole Technique” (GMT) or “Multiple Multipole Technique” (MMT). The key mathematical and physical basis, common to all aforementioned methods is the following: the solution to the EM radiation or scattering problem is constructed in terms of discrete fictitious currents (the “auxiliary sources” - ASs), located away from physical boundaries, as opposed to continuous equivalent currents placed on the interfaces, utilized in MoM, for example.

articleTitle: Riemann-Silberstein Vectors: Streamlined Electromagnetics with Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Riemann-Silberstein time domain vectors are shown to be solutions to each of the two first order factors that constitute the decomposed vector wave equation. The entire electromagnetic problem is then re-formulated in a simpler, compact form, at the cost of using complex time domain entities. Advantage is seen, e.g., in finite difference implementations that require fewer operations.

articleTitle: Broadband transparency observation in different topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Double layered metamaterials on the base of Babinet principle previously have been stated to show ultrabroadband transparency in microwave range. As shown in Ref [1], checkerboard patterned planar metamaterials due to match of multipoles decomposition in each layer ensure total transmission, i.e., $\mathrm{T}=100 \%$ of tranmitted wave (Fig. 1 c, green curve). Reasonable question is “does it work for another kind of simple geometries?”. Moreover, in case of manifestation of transparency in these geometries, it is crucial to study how it is related to their symmetry. Here we demonstrate complementary metasurfaces comprising unit cells of rhombic and triangular symmetry. We examine topology of transparency phenomena and attempt to clarify their dependence on the symmetry of unit cell, i.e., number of angles (nods), scale and other.

articleTitle: A ribbon figure-8 coil design for scalable and selective Trans-Spinal Magnetic Stimulation (TSMS)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Trans-Spinal Magnetic Stimulation (TSMS) is gaining attention in medical research as a promising, non-invasive alternative to conventional treatments for refractory chronic neuropathic back pain, such as spinal cord stimulation (SCS) [1–2]. Through a time-varying magnetic field, TSMS delivers electrical pulses to the spinal cord through a coil positioned on the patient’s back. The stimulation must be focal and penetrate deeply enough to reach the spinal cord, which may vary in depth depending on the individual [3]. The various commercial TSMS coils are built by winding metal wires with different numbers of turns, which affect the inductance of the coil. The winding wire diameter may be increased to allow for larger currents and increase the magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$, more profoundly in the tissue. In that case, the coil diameter tends to increase (Fig. 1A), and there may be a loss of focality and, consequently, a lower fiber selectivity.

articleTitle: Advancing High Power Microwave Sources and Antennas to Higher Frequencies+
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The University of New Mexico (UNM) group has been a leader in advancing intense beam-driven high-power microwave (HPM) sources [1] through analytical theory, particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, and experiments. Our group in the past has developed high power sources at L-band, S-band, X-band (for AFOSR and ONR), and even E-band (DARPA) generating at least 100 MW output power. The present focus of our research is to investigate HPM source concepts from X-to-Ka-band. We first performed a comprehensive literature search to identify the most promising path forward. We are in the process of downselecting our choice. In addition to source development, high-power antennas in the X-to-Ka-band pose significant challenges as the dimensions of the apertures are smaller yet need to radiate the very intense power levels.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Large Antenna Arrays with Static and Dynamic Macro Basis Function Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This article compares static and dynamic macro basis function (MBF) schemes for analysing large antenna arrays of disjoint elements with the method of moments (MoM). The MBF solvers are accelerated with directional cross approximation (DCA), a low-rank factorization technique suitable for high-frequency analysis. The characteristic basis function method (CBFM) is used as the static scheme. For dynamic schemes, the residual-driven CBFM, iterative Krylov subspace MBFs, and the iterative block-Jacobi scheme are considered. Numerical results demonstrate superior performance of the dynamic schemes over the static one. The Krylov and block-Jacobi schemes exhibit rapid convergence and faster runtimes than residual-driven CBFM.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Metamaterial and Metasurface with Media Homogenization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metamaterial and its 2D variation, i.e., metasurface exhibit unprecedent electromagnetic functions which are not practical for the materials from the nature. This advantage is mainly attributed to the more precise arrangement of the sub-wavelength scatters in an array fashion. However, the metamaterial and the metasurface are typical multiscale structures, with possible fine geometries inside each of the cells and the large size of total array. This multiscale characteristic poses challenges for the design of the corresponding numerical algorithms.

articleTitle: Measured Performance of Dielectric Rod EBG Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this contribution we present the design and experimental validation of a novel Electromagnetic Band-gap (EBG) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) that operates in the K-band. A study of the radiation mechanisms of 2-D dielectric lattices has been presented in [1]. An approach based both on the analysis of the band diagrams of the Bloch waves propagating in the 2-D EBG and the properties of bound and leaky modes in transversely open lattice waveguides is shown in [2], which provides an interesting perspective for antenna design. Here, we propose a 3-D realistic configuration of EBG LWA. The structure consists of $7 \times 8$ alumina cylinders with nominal dielectric permittivity of $\varepsilon_{r}=9.8$. The cylindrical rods, of radius 1.245 mm, are placed above a ground plane and supported by two vertical metal plates. The period of the structure is equal to 4.1 mm. The size of the structure, dimensioned to operate around $f=24 \mathrm{GHz}$, are $21.5 \times 39.8 \times 28.7 \mathrm{~mm}$. The distance between the two metal wall is 13.5 mm. The antenna, shown in Fig. 1(a), is fed by two counterphase monopoles. A rat-race hybrid junction, located below the antenna, feeds the two monopoles. The proposed structure was first simulated in CST Microwave Studio showing a very good agreement between CST total field and the dominant leaky mode. Fig 1(b)-(c) show the comparison between simulated and measured radiation patterns in the E-plane and H-plane, respectively. The measured directivity is 12.7 dBi at $f=24.6 \mathrm{GHz}$. The measured reflection coefficient at $f=24.6 \mathrm{GHz}$ is $\left|S_{11}\right|=-24 \mathrm{~dB}$. More details will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Dual-band Conformal Capsule Antenna Design for Biotelemetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper a compact conformal capsule antenna design based on the inverted-F antenna (IFA) is proposed for dual-band biotelemetry applications. The primary radiator of the suggested antenna is composed of a meander-line loaded spiral-type resonator which is used instead of the typical F-structure. To improve impedance matching, the antenna ground plane is modified by introducing a proper ring slot. The overall size of the compact antenna is only $14 \times 29.8 \times 0.125 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. According to the numerical results obtained using the CST microwave studio homogeneous model, the encapsulated conformal antenna operates at 402 MHz MICS and 2.45 GHz ISM bands with 18 and 90 MHz bandwidths, respectively.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for SAR Ship classification: Focus on Unbalanced Datasets and Inter-Dataset Generalization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Detection and recognition of vessel targets at sea are tasks of paramount relevance for maritime monitoring purposes. A possible approach to pursue these objectives consists in acquiring and processing Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data related to a given area of interest. Classically, the detection part can be implemented by exploiting statistical properties of the signal to decide whether an image area belongs to background clutter or to a ship (e.g. Constant False Alarm Rate based algorithms). Successively, discriminant features referring to the detected object can be extracted and later fed to a classifier to decide the membership category of the considered target. Recently, thanks to the development of algorithms based on deep neural network architectures, object detection and recognition experienced an unprecedented boost in the observed performances. This work, mainly motivated by the exploration of these novel approaches to the identification of vessel targets, focuses on the analysis of five different deep learning architectures (CNN, pre-trained and non-pretrained versions of ResNet50 and VGG16) trained on two public SAR vessel datasets (OpenSARShip and Fusar). To address the data quantity limitation, a third dataset was created by merging both datasets.

articleTitle: Capacitive-Loaded Ultra-Thin Metamaterial Absorber for X-band with Polarization Insensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The X-band’s versatility stems from its optimal combination of relatively high frequency and effective penetration through the atmosphere, making it a versatile choice for various applications across different domains. This article proposes a low-cost, multiband, and polarization-insensitive single-layered capacitively loaded microwave metamaterial absorber in X-band for surveillance radar application. The super unit cell of the designed absorber is constructed by arranging an array of two subunit cells, where one is a 90° rotated version of the other, exhibiting diagonal symmetry. Further, the electrical size and thickness of the absorber are reduced using capacitive loading by inserting slots in the design. The proposed absorber offers triple-band functionality at frequencies of 8.9,10.4, and 11.2 GHz, boasting absorptivity rates of $99 \%, 91 \%$, and $99.8 \%$ within the X-band spectrum.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic compatibility of maglev train on high-speed maglev demonstration line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Taking maglev train of high speed maglev demonstration line as the research object, the electromagnetic compatibility performance of this train is analyzed. The magnetic field of external electromagnetic radiation emitted by the vehicle in the frequency range of 150kHz-30MHz and the electric field emitted by the vehicle in the frequency range of 30MHz-1GHz are tested. The magnetic flux density (DC-20kHz) of the guest room area was tested and the electromagnetic protection requirements for the public and professional personnel were assessed. The test results show that the magnetic field and electric field radiated by the vehicle meet the limit requirements, and the magnetic flux density in the passenger room also meets the standard limit requirements.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of a Complex Volume Conductor Model on Network Dynamics for Deep Brain Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Computational modelling of deep brain stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder is vital for understanding the complex neural mechanisms underlying the disorder and for optimising treatment efficacy. This work presents a computational study investigating the intricate relationship between an advanced volume conductor model and a biophysical network model of the striatum in modelling deep brain stimulation. We highlight the pivotal role of integrating complex volume conductor models with neural network simulations and provide insights into their profound impact on understanding brain activity.

articleTitle: Frame-Based Analysis of Monostatic Scattering by Semi-Transparent Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work will present a first time implementation of the frame-based Gaussian Beam-Shooting (GBS) method to compute the monostatic scattering cross section (SCS) of semi-transparent cavities. The cavities will consist of rectangular parallelepipeds with thin walls, and the impedance sheet model will be used to represent the reflecting and transmitting properties of the walls. Numerical results will be presented and discussed, regarding the accuracy and the computational efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: Phaseless Imaging of Planar Targets: an Experimental Result
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a phaseless approach providing a qualitative estimate of the reflectivity of a planar target, from single frequency multi-monostatic acquisitions. The solution strategy is based on an approximated linear scattering model, reducing the computational burden, a smart scanning strategy reducing the number of required samples, an effective representation of the unknown reflectivity function and a proper optimization strategy. The performance of the phaseless imaging are experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Compact Shorted Annular Ring Patch Antenna Loaded With DNG Material
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper details the design and analysis of a miniaturized microstrip patch antenna, emphasizing its compact size and enhanced radiation. The proposed design introduces a shorted annular ring, partially loaded with metamaterial characterized by negative permittivity and permeability. The modal equation for the antenna’s cavity is derived and solved numerically. Full-wave simulation results for the return loss and radiation pattern, obtained using CST Microwave Studio, validate the predictions made by the cavity model analysis.

articleTitle: Origami Basis Functions for Modeling the Curvature Correction in H-refinement Methods via Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In computational electromagnetics, the accuracy of simulations is significantly influenced by the meshing quality of the structures under analysis. Higher mesh density generally translates into higher accuracy as it provides a more detailed representation of the structure, although at the expense of greater demands on computational resources. This is particularly true in multiscale problems, where the different levels of detail make the impact of mesh density and quality even more critical. In this context, adaptive meshing techniques, especially through h-refinement, arise as a powerful tool for addressing these problems [1, 2]. H-refinement involves locally refining the mesh in areas lacking accuracy depending on an error estimation process. This method allows for targeted subdivisions in regions with higher errors, thereby systematically reducing the overall error and achieving the desired level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging using the Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radar imaging is a large and ever-growing field with many industrial applications. This paper describes the design and implementation of the Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique (SIRT), which is usually applied to parallel beam measurements, on reflection data captured by a Vector Network Analyser. The dataset is pre-processed and a system matrix is generated in order to implement the SIRT algorithm. Various window functions are applied to the data and their effectiveness is analysed.

articleTitle: Power Enhanced Hybrid Chireix-Doherty Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of a novel power-enhanced Hybrid Chireix-Doherty (HCD) amplifier topology is presented. The Chireix outphasing topology excels at efficient high-power output but is compromised for lower power modes. In contrast, one of the strengths of Doherty’s design is its ability to reduce input drive during low-power output. The proposed method introduces a novel way of combining the best aspects of each topology to provide a high-power and highly efficient PA solution by utilizing inverse Class F as the main amplifier and Class C as the auxiliary amplifier for the first time [1–3]. The RF amplifier designed using the proposed topology achieved a peak power of 45.5 dBm with a Power Back-Off (PBO) range of 3 dB, yielding 75% drain efficiency at 2 GHz.

articleTitle: Loop Antenna Array for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A compact dual-polarized loop antenna is proposed for vehicular applications. The antenna comprises a 4x1 array operating from 24.25 GHz to 26.15 GHz and employs a microstrip-grounded CPW transition. The antenna provides both horizontal and vertical polarization radiation properties with a maximum gain of 6.9 dBi. The combined pattern from both polarizations shows an omnidirectional ripple of less than 4.0 dB.

articleTitle: Interpolatory Curl-Conforming Pyramidal Elements: Progress and Results
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Advanced finite element codes for the analysis and synthesis of three-dimensional electromagnetic structures should be able to use hybrid meshes composed of cells of different shapes, namely cuboids, tetrahedra, prisms and pyramids. For all these elements, with the exception of pyramids, it has long been known how to define divergence-conforming or curl-conforming higher-order basis functions, whether interpolatory or hierarchical [1]. We know that for all elements it is better to work in a parent space where a parent cell is defined. The cells of the observer domain (otherwise called child domain) are obtained using appropriate nodal shape functions which, like the vector basis functions, are polynomials of the parent variables. Unfortunately, things are not so simple for the pyramid because it has four edges converging on its tip. Within a geometrically continuous hybrid mesh, i.e. without gaps between cells, the tangential or normal continuity of the vector basis functions on the boundaries of the pyramids is guaranteed only by accepting that the shape functions and the basis functions of the pyramid are fractional functions with a tip singularity. This meant that for a long time it was not possible to properly define the order of the bases nor was it possible to demonstrate the completeness of the set of shape functions and vector bases of the pyramidal element. As demonstrated in [2, 3], shape functions and vector bases take polynomial form if defined in a grandparent space, different from the parent one. In the grandparent space the pyramid has the shape of a cube (see Fig. 1). Therefore, using grandparent variables we can clearly define the order of the bases (since we work with sets of polynomials) while ensuring the required continuity from element to element.
