articleTitle: Method for Estimating Scatterer Information from the Response Waveform of a Backward Transient Scattered Field When a Line Source and an Observation Point are at Different Positions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for estimating scatterer information from the response waveform of a backward transient field for E-polarization scattered by a two-dimensional (2-D) coated cylinder when an electric line source and an observation point are at different positions. The three types of scatterer information treated in this paper are the relative permittivity of a coating medium layer, its thickness, and the outer radius of a coated cylinder. Specifically, the time-domain Fourier transform method (TD-FTM) and the amplitude intensity ratios (AIRs) of adjacent backward transient scattered electric field components are used to derive estimation formulas. The estimates are obtained by substituting the numerical data of the response waveform and the numerical parameters of a pulse source into the estimation formulas and performing iterative calculations. The effectiveness of the estimation method is verified by comparing the estimates with the set values.

articleTitle: Explicit determination of the spectrum of normal waves in an inhomogeneous plane-parallel dielectric layer with a parabolic permittivity profile
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Explicit determination is considered of the spectrum of normal waves in an inhomogeneous plane-parallel dielectric layer with a parabolic permittivity profile. Exact formulas are obtained for the propagation constants and normal wave field components.

articleTitle: On a High-Frequency Analysis of Some Relevant Integral Equations in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this contribution we analyze the spectral properties of some commonly used boundary integral operators in computational electromagnetics and of their discrete counterparts, highlighting peculiar features of their spectra. In particular, a comparison with the eigenvalues of the continuous operators will be presented that highlights deviations in the high frequency regime and impacts, in a peculiar way, the accuracy of the numerical solutions of each formulation. A study and a proactive analysis of numerical results from standard boundary element solvers and the predictions from the theoretical analysis will corroborate the analytical framework employed and the validity of our observations.

Author Keywords: accuracy of the Boundary Element Method

articleTitle: Adaptive spatial resolution for spatial spectral integral equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Fast formulations for domain integral equations exist for decades. Two popular discretization strategies for them are voxel-grids [1] and Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson-functions (SWGs) [2]. The main advantage of a voxel-grid is that the continuous translation symmetry of the physical problem translates to a discrete translation symmetry in the discretized problem. This allows for a quick computation of the interaction matrix and fast, FFT-based matrix-vector-products. However, voxel-grids do not allow for refinement, and voxels are a somewhat crude approximation to the continuous electromagnetic fields. SWGs do much better at the latter aspect, since they allow for local refinement, and are an order more continuous. But, in general, SWG-discretized objects do not have a discrete translation symmetry, leading to significantly larger computational efforts.

articleTitle: A broadband multipole method for the scattering analysis of antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The EM simulation of the effects of mutual coupling, or crosstalk, is crucial for the design of wideband phased arrays, such as those found in the Square Kilometer Array (SKA). In wideband systems like SKA-Low, operating from 50 to 350 MHz, strong coupling effects naturally occur due to the complex antenna structures supporting higher-order current modes. The EM simulations poses significant computational challenges, inherently resulting from the complexity of antenna geometries, typically modelled with thousands of mesh elements, the proximity between antennas [1], often a small fraction of the wavelength, and the large number of antennas, up to several thousand [2].

articleTitle: Quantifying Uncertainty in Machine Learning Based Soil Moisture Retrieval From GNSS-R Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Spaceborne platforms like the NASA SMAP and the ESA SMOS offer global-scale coarse-resolution observations that can be used to estimate surface soil moisture. However, they acquire observations at a moderate revisit frequency, reducing the impact on applications that require higher temporal resolutions. Global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) is a prime example of a signal-of-opportunity (SoOP) which has been shown to be highly sensitive to variations in soil moisture. In this work, we consider measurements from the NASA Cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) mission which consists of eight low-orbit observatories, that are equipped with two nadirlooking antennas to receive reflected GPS signals. To extract soil moisture content, the traditional approach involves inverting parameterized forward models which account for aspects like dielectric properties of the soil, topography, and incidence angle information among others. Despite their potential, these models typically involve simplified assumptions and demonstrate increased sensitivity to the values of different parameters. To address this challenge, a new line of research tries to address this challenge by utilizing machine learning models and treating the problem as that of supervised regression.

articleTitle: Geometry-and Physics-Aware h-p Adaptation Algorithm for Efficient Electromagnetic Scattering Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In numerical analysis of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from electrically large and complex structures, achieving a high computational efficiency while ensuring simulation accuracy remains a substantial challenge. This study builds upon our previous work with phase-extracted basis functions (PEBFs) and higherorder basis functions (HOBFs) (J. P. Webb, IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag., 47(8), 1244-1253, 1999) to introduce a novel integral-equation-based method that employs a hybrid h-p adaptation strategy. This approach combines the benefits of both adaptive mesh refinement and adaptive basis function order to tackle the computational demands posed by intricate object geometries.

articleTitle: Mm-wave near-field focused antenna array for chipless RFID detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work reports a focused antenna array that could allow for an accurate interrogation of passive sensors. In recent years, some passive sensors have been proposed [1, 2], however there are often problems reading these sensors due to interference with the surrounding environment. The proposed idea is therefore to focus the beam exclusively on the sensor. The reading system is formed by two cross-polarized near-field arrays which are able to concentrate the radiated fields in the area occupied by the sensor under test thus avoiding scattering from nearby objects with a consequent reduction of clutter. The proposed NF focused array is composed of 16x16 elements and it works around 20 GHz (λ equal to 15 mm). The array has a layered structure. There are two dielectric substrates (Itera MT40 material), the lower substrate has a thickness of 0.254 mm and the upper one 0.762 mm. The feeding network, which represents the bottom of the structure, is created on the first substrate. On the top of this substrate there is a perforated metal surface. Metallic rectangular patches are made on the top of the second substrate. Vias cross the entire structure to connect the feeding network with the patches.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Measurement of Waveguide Orthomode Transducers for Quad-Ridge Horn-Feeds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A measurement technique is presented that characterises the full multi-modal S-matrix describing an orthomode transducer, using only one-port coaxial measurements and a sliding waveguide short. The method uses a combination of optimisation techniques, with multiple initial parameter sets, to extract the multi-modal S-parameters from the one-port coaxial measurements for a set of accurate offset shorts at the waveguide port. A cross-validation of the extracted parameters, using a validation measurement set, forms an integral part of the procedure. The method is validated using a standard coaxial to WR90 waveguide transition, and then applied successfully to a quad-ridged waveguide orthomode transducer developed for the future SKA Band A. It is shown that the S-parameters for four quad-ridged waveguide modes can be extracted over a frequency range of multiple octaves.

articleTitle: Scattering at a Superluminal Arbitrarily Decelerating Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present a general analytical solution to the electromagnetic scattering problem at an arbitrarily decelerating interface in the superluminal regime, employing the same methodology of its already addressed counterpart, the subluminal regime. We demonstrate that the solutions in both regimes exhibit similar forms while elucidating their differences. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that arbitrary chirping also occurs in the superluminal regime, albeit constrained. This work constitutes a notable progression in the development of accelerated space-time engineered modulation crystals, offering substantial potential for integration into microwave and optical devices that depend on chirp-based functionalities.

articleTitle: Development of Multilayer Metamaterial Absorber for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The paper proposes a metamaterial absorber design specifically engineered to operate at THz frequencies, serving as a sensor for medical applications using semiconductor multilayer metamaterial structure. Its intricate structure encompasses multiple layers, including a glass substrate, an InSb semiconductor layer, a MgF 2 buffer layer, an InSb resonator ring, additional buffer layers, and a mask. The proposed absorber incorporates Drude and Debye models to accurately represent the frequency-dependent permittivity of its constituent materials. Rigorous simulations are conducted using Finite Element Method (FEM) 3D EM simulator to evaluate its performance comprehensively over 1 THz frequency range and optimized to operate at 0.3 THz. The analysis encompasses various conditions, including absorption, transmission, and reflection across different frequencies and wavelengths. Results confirm the absorber’s efficacy in achieving expected absorption levels at the desired operational frequency of 0.3 THz, thereby validating its potential for effective utilization in biomedical sensing applications.

articleTitle: Study on Improvement of the Fast Inverse Laplace Transform for Transient Analyses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This study investigates a time-domain simulation technique based on the fast inverse Laplace transform (FILT) [1]. The time-domain simulations have attracted more attentions in applications of electromagnetic waves, and the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method [2] may be the most commonly used technique for this purpose. Basic idea of the FDTD method, which directly discretizes the Maxwell equations and the constitutive relations, is intuitive and relatively easy to understand. However, its computational cost sometimes limits the scope of application when high-precision simulation is required. On a different note, the frequency-domain approaches have a long history, and we have a vast store of knowledge. The FILT makes it possible to utilize this knowledge for a wide range of the transient response analyses of electromagnetic fields [3–5].

articleTitle: Examining the Impact of Geometry Modeling Precision on the Accuracy of Monostatic RCS Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) solvers are valuable tools in the analysis and design of circuits, antennas, filters etc. and are indispensable for characterizing scattering as measurements can be cumbersome and expensive. WIPL-D [1] is a full 3D EM solver based on the Method of Moment (MoM) applied to Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) [2].

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis and Applications of Planar Series Feed Antennas for Near-Field UHF RFID, Sensing and Radiative WPT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Near-field antennas have recently attracted an increased attention for the variety of near-field communication and sensing applications. At the same time, the radio frequency identification (RFID) technology has come of age and became an indispensable tool in the numerous industrial applications in the retail tracking, security, counterfeit prevention, and healthcare. Several designs of the near-field reader antennas utilized for different UHF RFID applications have been introduced in [1]. For the so-called smart shelf antenna applications, item RFID tags are typically placed on the reader antenna surface and may occupy various interrogation volumes within the reactive and radiative near-field zones. The UHF $(916-920 \mathrm{MHz})$ RFID antenna design producing the circularly polarized (CP) radiation in the near field of planar antenna based on the periodic strips EM coupled to the microstrip feed line has been presented in [2]. To address the specific demands of the emerging near-field wireless applications, new concepts of the near-field antenna operation are required.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing of the Lower Ionosphere during the April 8, 2024 Solar Eclipse by VLF Transmitter Signal Variations Recordings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Solar eclipses provide opportunities to study the short-time scale dynamics of the physical and chemical processes of the ionospheric D region. Measurements have been made previously using rocket-borne instruments and by receiving signals crossing the region of totality from man-made VLF transmitters. Whereas rockets tend to provide snapshot measurements of the electron density of the lower ionosphere, monitoring VLF transmissions allows for continuous indirect sensing with high time resolution. Radio waves from VLF transmitters propagate inside the waveguide formed by the lower ionosphere and the Earth’s surface. Significant variations in the received amplitude and phase arise from changes in the D region ionosphere. We use the full solar eclipse to collect new multi-point ELF and VLF observations. The map of the transmitters and detector locations in relation to the ionosphere level totality is shown in Figure 1. We utilize the ELF and VLF mobile stations to achieve strategic transmitter-receiver geometries relative to the eclipse trajectory to characterize the D region structure and dynamics in and near the totality zone, improving the spatial resolution of past works to characterize (1) how steep the electron density gradients in the vicinity of totality; (2) the observed ionospheric perturbations when the region of totality is near a powerful VLF transmitter; (3) the lower ionosphere characteristic reaction time to a point like perturbation from the eclipse

articleTitle: On the Theory of Single Aspheric Lenses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Aspheric lenses play a pivotal role in a myriad of applications, including antenna theory, communication systems, sophisticated optical systems etc. These lenses, unlike their spherical counterparts, possess an infinite number of free parameters and by utilizing these parameters it is possible to achieve optical and antenna systems with very high and sophisticated performances. However, the lack of a rigorous mathematical theory essentially limits possibility to utilize their full potential in the related fields. In our days, the design process relies heavily on elementary mathematical principles and empirical methods [1–2]. Even a single thick aspheric lens lacks a comprehensive mathematical theory. In this paper a new mathematical approach to the theory of single lenses is proposed. Surprisingly, even in this seemingly straightforward case, the serious mathematical theory of a single aspherical lens relies on rather nontrivial mathematical principles as partial differential equations, differential geometry, Riemann geometry.

articleTitle: Metal Sheet Thickness Measurement using Dielectric Waveguides with Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, we present thickness measurements of metal sheets with a single millimeter wave radar. Dielectric waveguides (DWGs) are used to split and guide electromagnetic waves to focusing lens antennas on both sides of the sheet. Both, the DWG and the lens antennas are 3D printed. To cover larger dimensions than the printing area of the 3D printer, a concept to connect DWGs is presented. Furthermore, the transition from the DWG into the lens antenna is improved by using a pyramidal horn with a square cross-section. The presented measurement setup allows simple reference measurements to compensate for systematic errors, leading to a maximum absolute error of 4 μm. A standard deviation of 1 μm for individual sheets confirms the proposed measurement principle.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Inverse Scattering Approach towards RCS Modeling of Arbitrary Targets for Digital Twin Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) efforts for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) applications are often challenged by the scarcity of diverse training data for relevant targets. Recently, digital twins have been employed as a means to augment measured SAR imagery for the purposes of ATR training [1]. Such approaches are based on the use of Computational Electromagnetic (CEM) techniques to generate accurate radar cross section (RCS) data (and subsequent SAR imagery) for targets of interest. Unfortunately these approaches lack scalability as they rely on appropriate digital models of the underlying targets. In an effort to promote a more efficient and scalable digital twin construction process, our work explores the use of inverse scattering for the purpose of digitizing arbitrary physical targets in a manner that is amenable to efficient and faithful RCS prediction for arbitrary aspect angles within the desired band of operation.

articleTitle: Regularized Solution of 2D Scattering from Impedance-loaded Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by infinitely long, perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) cylinders of arbitrary cross-section, either closed or open (i.e., with cavity-backed apertures) has been studied by many authors. When the structure is closed and of canonical shape (e.g., of circular or elliptical cross-section) many approaches (such as the method of separation of variables) are available; a wide selection of results is given in [1]. However, for non-canonical structures of arbitrary shape, including those in which an aperture has been opened, far fewer tools are available; the most usual approaches in the low and intermediate (resonance) wavenumber regime usually prefer integral equation methods over differential equation approaches (finite-difference or finite element methods). A single- or double-layer density on the surface of the scattering structure is employed to represent the scattered field in the E-pol or H-pol cases respectively; enforcement of the boundary condition (the vanishing of the tangential electric field on the surface) results in a surface integral equation (IE).

articleTitle: An Innovative Combined Train Speed Measurement Method for Medium-Low Speed Maglev Trains
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper delves into the medium-low speed maglev transit system, presenting a novel urban railway mode that forgoes conventional axle-based sensors such as speed odometers due to its maglev propulsion characteristics. The research introduces eddy current sensors as a viable alternative for speed measurement, leveraging their non-contact nature and immunity to mechanical wear and environmental constraints. A sophisticated sensor information fusion algorithm, integrating Kalman filtering with adaptive weighted fusion, is proposed to augment the accuracy and dependability of speed measurements. Through a meticulous comparative analysis of four speed measurement fusion algorithms based on their variance, the study identifies the most suitable algorithm for practical engineering applications in real projects. This work not only enhances the methodology of train speed measurement but also provides a foundation for future applications in similar non-contact measurement scenarios.

articleTitle: A preliminary experimental demonstration of the Norton Surface Wave in a radio link
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This abstract is a communication providing radiofrequency measurements aiming to highlight the emergence of the NSW (Norton surface wave) [1], which appears particularly in radio links close to a conductive ground. In the case where the emitting antenna is a VED (Vertical Electric Antenna), a condition to verify the emergence of the NSW has been given in [2], as well as the critical distances predicting the ranges where the NSW is predominant. Therefore, a careful choice of the radio link parameters, which takes into account the conditions given in [2], must improve significantly the path-loss. The decomposition of the total wave propagating near the conductive ground is given by ${\mathcal{P}}_{\text {Total }}={\mathcal{P}}_{\text {Two-ray }}+{\mathcal{P}}_{\text {NSw }}$. The subscript “Two-ray” denotes the wave component based on geometrical optics, and the NSW, the component derived from the evaluation of the Sommerfeld Integrals [1].

articleTitle: The Role of Second-Order Symmetries in Waveguide Propagation and its Peculiarities on the Mode-Matching Problem Using the 2D Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In microwave engineering, first-order or axial symmetries are typically considered as a tool to control mode propagation in the design of devices such as antennas, antenna feeders, polarization selective surfaces, and orthomode transducers. Despite being known for a long time [1], second-order, or discrete rotational symmetries, have had a marginal presence in the field, even though they exhibit advantageous theoretical properties when compared to axial symmetries, like enhanced mode classes, degeneracy discrimination, rotationally symmetric mode, suitable for circular polarization, and possibly extended mode class monomode bandwidth.

articleTitle: Analyzing Ultra-Wideband Electromagnetic Problems by Time-domain Integral Equation Formulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The surface integral equations (SIEs) are widely employed to address scattering, radiation, and circuit simulation problems. However, both the frequency domain integral equations (FDIE) and time domain integral equations (TDIE) encounter issues related to low-frequency breakdown [1]. Specifically, there is a dominance of the scalar potential in the impedance matrix at low frequencies (ω → 0 in the frequency domain and Δt → ∞ in the time domain). This phenomenon leads to a significant increase in the condition number of the matrix, which notably affects the solution of the SIE. Moreover, the presence of numerical errors and ill-conditioned matrix often leads to inaccurate solutions at low frequencies. On the other hand, the characteristic of the $\mathcal{L}$ operator makes it susceptible to the mesh density, which results in large condition number compared to the $\mathcal{K}$ operator [2]. The commonly used method to address low frequency problems is quasi-Helmholtz decomposition [3], [4]. This approach helps eliminating the impact of numerical errors at low frequencies. Other strategy involves using additional equations to reduce the numerical imbalance [5], [6].

articleTitle: A mmWave Phase Correlation Based Gas Velocity Sensor Utilizing Time Domain Multiplexed Fixed Target Radar Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative gas-flow sensor concept grounded in time domain multiplexing of fixed target radar measurements. Leveraging an ultra-broadband mmWave FMCW radar system and a signal distribution network based on dielectric waveguides, the single measurement channel is subdivided into three distinct sub-channels in the time domain. Through the integration of marker gas injection and a radar phase cross-correlation algorithm, this method combines cost-effectiveness with highly precise flow measurements. In addition to presenting comprehensive design considerations, this paper substantiates the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed measurement technique through detailed discussions of multiple test measurements.

articleTitle: Field Coupling to Transmission Lines Terminated by Buck and Negative Impedance Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The electromagnetics community has paid a great deal of attention to field coupling to transmission lines. The transmission line models may be complex, but these models usually have linear terminations. Simulating the coupling of fields into real systems requires the application of active and nonlinear terminations. We will use an object – oriented, cyber – physical technique based on the Modelica language to improve run time and to better integrate the coupling to transmission – line networks into system simulations. The RF effects simulation methods are appropriate to all types of electromagnetic coupling including electronic warfare, electromagnetic compatibility/interference and lightning.

articleTitle: Applying the spacetime geometric algebra in magnetized plasma electromagnetism: Is it only a matter of beauty?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Geometric algebras (GAs) offer an elegant way to describe rotations on Bloch hyperspheres. The latter are synonymous to the so-called qubits in the realm of Quantum Information and their implementation via Quantum Computing techniques [1]. The question that naturally arises is if elegance is a high price to pay in adapting the geometric approach in a problem that cubits are involved. However, it is generally accepted in the scientific community that GAs are, by far, the easiest way to describe rotations in space and in higher dimensions [2]. This is become more obvious if one deals with such transformations in the realm of special relativity and the associated Lorentz transformations in four dimensional Minkowskian spacetime.

articleTitle: Optimization of gradient core radomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper addresses optimization of gradient core radomes, whose physical representations have additively manufactured honeycomb cores with tapered wall thickness. However, to simplify the analysis, the gradient core is considered to consist of multiple homogeneous layers with individual permittivity. These layers constitute a permittivity profile which is optimized such that the reflections from the gradient core layers cancel the reflections from the composite skins, which are reinforcing the structure. It is demonstrated that gradient core radomes can be optimized for large bandwidth, low transmission loss as well as low flash lobe level.

articleTitle: The Generalized Electromagnetic Projection Operator Over a 3 Dimension Probabilistic Space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In a recent paper we discovered the existence of a hidden symmetry in a two-dimensional probabilistic space associated to projection operators, also we showed that projection operators help us to give a particular representation of the solutions of the Fredholm integral equations that merge for a broadcasting situation. Now, we explore the case for a three-dimension probabilistic space applied to the representation of the electromagnetic resonant vector (ERV) and for the generalized source (GS) and ask about the possible recover of symmetry properties if we scaled to a higher dimension and, as we have said, give it a useful application. Because for three dimensions there is a simple representation for the symmetry group associated with these operators, so in this work we explicitly construct a matrix representation, which makes us think that it is possible to find hidden symmetries for higher dimensions. For the two-dimensional case, we find a space that contains the originally constructed probabilistic space, but it shows that the concept of probability is immanent to the existence of a space we call the dual space, like in the jargon of quantum mechanics. articleTitle: Evaluation Method for Whole-Body Exposure from 5G Base Stations using Superposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: For high frequencies such as the 28 GHz band used in 5 G mobile communication systems, base stations are installed closer to users than conventional tower-type stations, and beamforming is utilized to compensate for the short propagation distance. Evaluating electromagnetic wave exposure to the human body is important, with the worst-case exposure level being the key factor. Therefore, it is necessary to calculate and compare the exposure levels from different beam directions radiated by base stations located a few meters away from the human body. This study aims to accelerate each exposure evaluation during the exhaustive search for worst-case beam configuration. We investigated a method to calculate exposure levels based on the fact that radiations from an arbitrary antenna can be expressed as a superposition of spherical waves [1]. Pre-calculating exposure data for spherical waves requires a large-scale computing environment. However, the superposition evaluation can be performed on a workstation, reducing the computational resources needed for exposure evaluation for each radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of X Band Synthetic Aperture Radar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) antenna is a type of antenna used in SAR systems, which utilize the principle of radar waves reflecting off surfaces to obtain high-resolution images. These antennas emit radar waves, collect signals reflected from objects, and process these signals to create high-resolution radar images. SAR antennas, typically found on platforms such as satellites, aircraft, or unmanned aerial vehicles, are used in various applications including terrain monitoring, weather forecasting, agriculture, forestry monitoring, environmental monitoring, maritime, and military reconnaissance [1]. The presence of SAR antennas in the X-band is crucial for obtaining high-resolution images. The X-band provides a suitable frequency range for radar waves to reflect smaller details, resulting in more precise images. Therefore, SAR antennas operating in the X-band are preferred for obtaining detailed and high-resolution images. Additionally, the X-band is less affected by weather conditions, which supports obtaining more reliable and accurate results [2]. For these reasons, operating SAR antennas in the X-band provides a significant advantage in radar applications and is commonly preferred in applications such as terrain monitoring, weather forecasting, military reconnaissance, and others.

articleTitle: Advancing Hydrological Insights: Daily Surface Water Dynamics through CYGNSS Data in Tropical Wetlands
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The advent of Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) data heralds a paradigm shift in environmental monitoring, offering unparalleled penetration capabilities through cloud cover and dense vegetative canopies. This advancement is particularly pertinent for the study of tropical wetlands, regions that are experiencing observational challenges and, thus, significantly underrepresented in hydrological studies.

articleTitle: Laboratory Investigation of Triggered Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The mechanisms that control magnetospheric whistler wave generation have been investigated by ground based VLF ($3-30 \mathrm{kHz}$) wave-injection experiments such as at Siple Station and HAARP. Coherent signals were shown to routinely trigger the generation of new coherent waves known as “triggered emissions”. VLF triggered emissions are long-lived, many times the length of the triggering signal, and exhibit spectral characteristics that closely resemble natural magnetospheric chorus waves. These controlled injection experiments have produced a wealth of data, but at the same time, comparison of this dataset to theory is difficult since the ground observations are at the end of the interaction region, giving access only to cumulative effects of the wave-particle interaction.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for THz: Hardware Impairments and Switching Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The demand for unprecedented performance in the upcoming 6 G wireless networks is fomenting the research on THz communications empowered by Reconfigurable Inteligent Surfaces (RISs). A wide range of use cases have been proposed, most of them, assuming high-level RIS models that overlook some of the hardware impairments that this technology faces. The expectation is that the emergent reconfigurable THz technologies will eventually overcome its current limitations. This disassociation from the hardware may mask nonphysical assumptions, perceived as hardware limitations. In this paper, a top-down approach bounded by physical constraints is presented, distilling from system-level specifications, hardware requirements, and upper bounds for the RIS-aided system performance. We consider D-band indoor and outdoor scenarios where a more realistic assessment of the state-of-the-art solution can be made. The goal is to highlight the intricacies of the design procedure based on sound assumptions for the RIS performance. For a given signal range and angular coverage, we quantify the required RIS size, number of switching elements, and maximum achievable bandwidth and capacity.

articleTitle: PIN-diode controlled slot-fed MED antenna for 5G sub-6 GHz applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A new reconfigurable Magneto-Electric Dipole (MED) antenna with a slot feed for 5 G sub-6 GHz applications is designed using the “surrogateopt” optimization algorithm. The antenna covers the n78 and n79 frequency bands when a control PIN diode is in “on” and “off” states, respectively. Impedance matching of the proposed MED antenna is achieved by altering the slot width at its center. Full-wave numerical simulations have been conducted to optimize and verify the antenna performance. An equivalent circuit based on Schelkunoff’s theory for dipole antennas and the transmission line theory has been developed to model the antenna input impedance analytically. Both simulation and analytical modeling results show that the proposed reconfigurable MED antenna, with dimensions of $71 \times 71 \times 13.63 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$, fully covers the n78 and n79 bands and maintains stable gains above 7.6 dBi in these bands.

articleTitle: A hybrid finite element/finite difference method for reconstruction of dielectric properties of conductive objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The aim of this article is to present a hybrid finite element/finite difference method which is used for reconstructions of electromagnetic properties within a realistic breast phantom. This is done by studying the mentioned properties’ (electric permittivity and conductivity in this case) representing coefficients in a constellation of Maxwell’s equations. This information is valuable since these coefficient can reveal types of tissues within the breast, and in applications could be used to detect shapes and locations of tumours. Because of the ill-posed nature of this coefficient inverse problem, we approach it as an optimization problem by introducing the corresponding Tikhonov functional and in turn Lagrangian. These are then minimized by utilizing an interplay between finite element and finite difference methods for solutions of direct and adjoint problems, and thereafter by applying a conjugate gradient method to an adaptively refined mesh. articleTitle: High-Voltage Driver Circuits for Electro-Optical RF Modulators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Pockels cells are used in a broad range of optical signal processing applications, including quantum computing, because of their capability to modify the phase or polarity of a photon stream by application of an electrical field. As the underlaying electro-optical Pockels effect is weak, a high electric field strength, to be provided by a RF control voltage of 500 V, is required for the modulation of the optical signal. To maximize the processing speed, the high voltage pulses must be applied with a repetition rate of 500 kHz. The trend towards higher data rates places greater demands on the Pockels cell drivers, which have to generate a stable high voltage and produce high-voltage pulses by fast switching. This paper focuses on the design of a suitable voltage driver circuit, using a non-conventional cascaded voltage-doubler circuit. It is proven by simulation and measurements that the use of the Karthaus-Fischer cascade is advantageous for providing the required high output currents.

articleTitle: X-Band Near-Field GPR Based on Collimated and Focused Vortex Waves Using Ellipsoidal Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic vortex waves (VW) with orbital angular momentum (OAM), generated by a uniform circular array (UCA), are collimated and focused in the ground by an elliptical reflector in the near field (NF). This antenna system is used in a conceptual design of an X-band $(9.3 \mathrm{GHz})$ high-resolution ground penetrating radar (GPR) for the localization of multiple buried targets. Physical optics and ray tracing are used to calculate the underground NF. The relevant NF radar equation is developed using the Lorenz reciprocity theorem. The formulations of field in the ground are given. The algorithms used for the simultaneous localization of multiple targets are based on the orthogonality of OAM modes. The radar uses wide-band $(8.6 \%)$ FMCW waveform with coherent and noncoherent integration. The signal-to-noise ratio and the detection probability of small targets are calculated. We applied the method to a $\sim \mathbf{1 \%}$ moist sandy loam soil up to a depth of 1 m.

articleTitle: Polarization Independent Interconnected Split-Ring Resonator with Enclosed F Shape Metamaterial Absorber for Wireless Technology.
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article, a polarization-insensitive, flexible and ultrathin metamaterial absorber (MMA) has been presented with six absorption peaks in S-band, C-band, X-band, and Ku-band. The proposed absorbers’ geometry consists of $90^{0}$ rotated and connected four outer square split rings. Each outer split ring consists of rotationally symmetric two split square rings and a circular split ring. Each outer ring has a F shape in the core of the middle. FR-4, a generally accessible, low-cost substrate material with a dielectric constant of 4.3, was used to create the MMA unit cell. The unit cell size is $10 \times 10 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The absorption peaks of this absorber greater than $90 \%$ at $3.088,4.77,9.88,11.23$, $13.34,17.39$, and 18.23 GHz, respectively. The suggested absorber is insensitive to polarization and incidence angle since it is symmetrical. The proposed structure shows steady absorption over azimuth and elevation angles, specifically phi=0 to 90 degrees and Theta $=0$ to $\mathbf{6 0}$ degrees, and its refractive index is almost zero or negative. The absorber unit cell has a tiny and compact design, measuring $0.12 \lambda \times 0.12 \lambda$ in size and with an extremely thin thickness of $0.016 \lambda$. Here, $\lambda$ represents the wavelength at the absorption peak with the lowest frequency. The absorption phenomena of the absorber have been proved by analyzing the input impedance, E-field, and surface current distribution characteristics.

articleTitle: LIO-SAM for Vehicle Localization Using FGO Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In intelligent transportation systems, accurate positioning is crucial for ensuring the safe and efficient operation of vehicles. This paper addresses the positioning challenges in satellite-constrained scenarios by proposing a solution based on Lidar-Inertial Odometry via Smoothing and Mapping (LIO-SAM) We employed the LIO-SAM algorithm as our core positioning mechanism and designed a multi-sensor fusion positioning architecture that integrates LiDAR, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), and GNSS data to enhance positioning accuracy and robustness. By processing multisensor data obtained from on-site railway measurements, we validated and evaluated the feasibility and effectiveness of the algorithm. The experimental results indicate that this method maintains accurate and robust positioning even in satellite-constrained scenarios and achieves higher precision compared to traditional satellite positioning methods. This is significant for improving the safety and efficiency of vehicle operations.

articleTitle: Contribution to the Theory of the Two-Layered Ferrite-Dielectric Circular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The effect of the material and geometry parameters on some traits of the circular waveguide, which contains a co-axially positioned dielectric cylinder and a ferrite toroid of azimuthal magnetization, and supports normal $T E_{01}$ mode, is examined. The method uses definite roots of its characteristic equation, deduced earlier in terms of complex Kummer and Tricomi confluent hypergeometric and real ordinary Bessel functions, and certain new real positive numbers ($\bar{L}_{4 \pm}$ and $\bar{L}_{4 \pm}$ numbers), advanced recently by the authors. With their help the lower and upper cut-off frequencies of configuration are calculated. Knowing them permits to find the width of the area in which it operates as a phase shifter. Assuming the anisotropy of the ferrite medium weak, a numerical study of the dependence of the quantities said is done on: i) the size of the section, occupied by dielectric, stipulating that the relative permittivities of the two layers are equal; i i) the dielectric to ferrite relative permittivities ratio, provided the first is larger than the second one and the axial isotropic cylinder is thin. A profound discussion of the outcomes is presented.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Magnetoelectric Micro-Particles for Neuromodulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural stimulation using magnetoelectric microparticles (MEMP), potentially transforming biostimulation methods. We employ multi-physics modeling to integrate MEMPs into a simulation framework, focusing on designing spherical core-shell structures. These structures exploit resonant modes and the nonlinearity of magnetostrictive materials to amplify deformation under high-frequency magnetic fields. This process effectively down-converts remotely applied high-frequency signals into low-frequency deformations, crucial for neural stimulation. The interaction between the magnetostrictive core and the piezoelectric shell, particularly under resonance, enhances mechanical-to-electrical energy conversion, elevating bio-stimulation capabilities. Our findings suggest a path towards more efficient, targeted, and minimally invasive neural stimulation, with implications for advancing biomedical engineering and neuroscience.

articleTitle: Memristor-Based 1-Bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for 6G Communications at D-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Sub-THz and millimeter-wave bands have gained popularity, with the expectation that they will host the next generation of wireless communication systems. Furthermore, research on beam-steering characteristics provided by Programmable Electromagnetic Surfaces, such as Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RISs), has garnered considerable attention as an enabling technology for 6G communications. Due to size limitations, RISs face challenges related to power consumption in the reconfigurable elements and their integration with unit cells operating at high frequencies. This paper discusses the design of a 1-bit reconfigurable unit cell at the D-band using non-volatile technology to minimize static power consumption. Simulation results show that the proposed unit cell performs well with a reflection loss of less than 1.3 dB in both reconfigurable states across a frequency band from 120 to 170 GHz. Moreover, the phase difference between the two states is maintained at $180^{\circ} \pm 20^{\circ}$, with an operational bandwidth of approximately 16 GHz. The beamforming capabilities, with steering angles from -60° to 60°, of the $12 \times 12$ RIS, utilizing the proposed unit cell, have been demonstrated in terms of controlling the main beam radiation precisely to various angles with consistent performance at frequencies of $147 \mathrm{GHz}, 152 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 152.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A 300-GHz Broadband On-Chip Antenna Integrated With a Transmitter Front-End
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a sub-THz antenna on-chip (AoC) at 300-GHz, integrated with a transmitter front-end (Tx FE) for potential use in short-range, multi-gigabit, wireless or wireline communication links. The compact AoC presents endfire radiation characteristics and is based on a technique that stimulates a pair of coupled patch elements. The advantage of the proposed design is the ability for broadband operation extending from 282 to 345 GHz while achieving a maximum antenna gain and radiation efficiency of around 7 dB and 48%, respectively. The designed Tx FE comprises a 2-stage D-band cascode power amplifier and a common-emitter push-push frequency doubler. Post-layout simulations reveal the PA-doubler chain delivering an almost flat output power of 7.2 dBm across the 290-310 GHz range. Implemented in a 90-nm SiGe BiCMOS process, the proposed design yields a remarkable EIRP of 13.8 dBm, occupying a compact chip area of 2.38 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.
